picks.title: Interventions for adhesive capsulitis: systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.

sections.objective: To compare the benefits and harms of therapeutic interventions for adhesive capsulitis.
sections.methods: Systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.
sections.results: A total of 189 randomised controlled trials involving 12 988 participants and 59 interventions were included. Most trials contributing to principal outcomes were at high risk of bias (71% for pain, 72% for function, and 71% for range of motion). At short term follow-up, moderate certainty evidence suggested that extracorporeal shockwave therapy probably reduced pain compared with usual care (mean difference -1.97 on a 0-10 scale, 95% confidence interval (CI) -2.97 to -0.97). Low certainty evidence suggested that extracorporeal shockwave therapy may improve function (mean difference -11.42 on a 0-100 scale, 95% CI -16.68 to -6.15), although direct and indirect estimates were limited by important incoherence. For short term range of motion, moderate certainty evidence suggested that manipulation under anaesthesia combined with intra-articular steroid injections probably improved flexion (mean difference 33.29°, 95% CI 11.19° to 55.39°), as did manipulation under anaesthesia alone (26.16°, 8.19° to 44.13°). Low certainty evidence suggested that extracorporeal shockwave therapy may improve flexion (22.42°, 12.99° to 31.84°) and abduction (18.62°, 8.09° to 29.14°), but both comparisons were limited by important incoherence. At mid-term follow-up, evidence for possible improvements in function with extracorporeal shockwave therapy and flexion with passive mobilisation was of low certainty, while evidence for pain reduction with extracorporeal shockwave therapy was of very low certainty. Most other comparative estimates were supported by low or very low certainty evidence. Comparative safety remained highly uncertain because adverse events were incompletely and inconsistently reported; the absence of reported adverse events should not be interpreted as evidence of absence of harm.
sections.conclusion: Moderate certainty evidence suggests short term pain reduction with extracorporeal shockwave therapy and improved short term flexion with manipulation under anaesthesia, with or without intra-articular steroid injections. Most other treatment effects remain uncertain because of low certainty and incoherence, and comparative safety and mid-term effects are poorly established. The available evidence is mainly short term and outcome specific. Longer term comparative effectiveness, overall benefits and harms, and applicability beyond predominantly primary adhesive capsulitis remain uncertain.
sections.other: Medline, Cochrane Library, Embase, Web of Science, and Scopus were searched from inception to 1 May 2025, with an update in November 2025. Randomised controlled trials enrolling adults with adhesive capsulitis, comparing active treatment with another intervention, placebo, or usual care. Pain, function, range of motion, and adverse events. PROSPERO CRD420251070468.

picks.title: Perioperative respiratory adverse events in children undergoing adenotonsillectomy with laryngeal mask airway versus endotracheal tube ventilation: multicentre, randomised controlled trial.

sections.objective: To assess the effect of ventilation with a laryngeal mask airway (LMA) compared with endotracheal tube (ETT) on perioperative respiratory adverse events (PRAEs) in children undergoing adenotonsillectomy.
sections.methods: Multicentre, randomised, parallel group trial. 400 children aged ≥2 years and <7 years who were scheduled for adenotonsillectomy under general anaesthesia. Participants were randomised 1:1 to receive ventilation with a laryngeal mask airway (n=200) or an endotracheal tube (n=200) during adenotonsillectomy.
sections.results: 400 children (mean age 4.7 (standard deviation 1.0) years; 155 (38.7%) girls) were enrolled between 24 May 2023 and 4 April 2024, with last follow-up on 4 May 2024. LMA was converted to ETT in three participants. Overall, 22.5% (45/200) participants in the LMA group experienced PRAEs versus 57.5% (115/200) in the ETT group (absolute risk difference -35.0 percentage points, 95% confidence interval -43.5 to -25.7; P<0.001). The LMA group had fewer PRAEs in both the intraoperative (9.0% (18/200) v 17.5% (35/200); -8.5, -15.2 to -1.8; P=0.01) and the postoperative period (16.5% (33/200) v 49.5% (99/200); -33.0, -41.2 to -24.0; P<0.001). The LMA group also had a lower proportion of participants with laryngospasm (0.0% v 3.0%; P=0.03), desaturation (15.0% v 28.0%; P=0.002), airway obstruction (3.5% v 12.5%; P<0.001), and severe cough (10.5% v 42.0%; P<0.001). Neither group experienced serious adverse events.
sections.conclusion: Ventilation with an LMA by experienced anaesthesiologists resulted in fewer perioperative respiratory adverse events than ventilation with an ETT in children undergoing adenotonsillectomy.
sections.other: Four tertiary hospitals in China, 2023-24. The primary outcome was the proportion of participants who developed any perioperative respiratory adverse event (PRAE): laryngospasm, bronchospasm, desaturation, airway obstruction, severe cough, or stridor in the intention-to-treat population.

picks.title: A conserved flowering-time module underlies double-season cropping.
picks.abstract: Adapting crops to intensive cultivation systems under climate change requires varieties that combine yield potential with optimized flowering and maturation1,2. In central and eastern China, barley has long been cultivated in a double-season cropping system, in which early flowering and maturation are critical for escaping presummer terminal heat stress and enabling flexible rotation with summer crops3,4. Here we trace the genomic footprints of 80 years of modern breeding in China using 505 representative cultivars and identify a flowering-time module defined by a single amino acid substitution in PHYTOCHROME C in combination with a winter-type VERNALIZATION 1 haplotype that underpins this adaptation. The derived allele accelerates heading and maturity, and its frequency has risen sharply in modern autumn-sown varieties. Using base editing in barley and wheat, we confirm causality and demonstrate that this flowering-time combination module, PhyC-VRN1, is functionally conserved across Triticeae. Our results identify and experimentally validate a breeding-relevant flowering-time module that has been selected during modern breeding to enable intensive crop rotations, as well as demonstrate how precision genome editing can be used to reconstruct such adaptive modules for climate-resilient crop design.

picks.title: Quantum gases below 10 picokelvin in space.
picks.abstract: Ultracold atom platforms enable low temperatures and long free evolution times, which are crucial for fundamental physics tests and atom interferometry. The lowest equivalent temperature reported in such a system is 38 pK with a free expansion time of 2 s, achieved in atom-chip-based magnetic traps in microgravity. Optical dipole trap (ODT) systems offer better optical access and the flexibility to condense both magnetic and non-magnetic atoms, but have not been used to prepare quantum degenerate gases under microgravity conditions. Here we report an ODT-based Bose-Einstein condensate created aboard the China Space Station, containing 2.0 × 104 atoms, reaching an equivalent temperature of [Formula: see text] pK with a free expansion time of 7.0 s. This record-low temperature could stimulate a new generation of ODT-based experiments in quantum simulation and precision measurements in space.

picks.title: Longitudinal single-cell profiling of breast tumors highlights immune and epigenetic mechanisms associated with sensitivity to aromatase inhibitors.
picks.abstract: Estrogen receptor (ER)-positive breast cancer treatment is based primarily on endocrine therapy. To dissect mechanisms of sensitivity to aromatase inhibitors in ER-positive breast cancer, we profiled tumor biopsies from 25 patients during neoadjuvant therapy using single-cell RNA sequencing, immune receptor sequencing and enhancer activity mapping. Malignant cells with high ER signaling and elevated activity of enhancers with ER binding sites were sensitive to treatment. Resistance was associated with androgen receptor signaling, dedifferentiation and epithelial-mesenchymal transition. Poor responders preferentially used the androgen receptor cis-regulome under treatment pressure. The baseline tumor microenvironment was associated with tumor downstaging. Poor responders exhibited a 'hot', yet ineffective immune landscape enriched for naive lymphoid and undifferentiated myeloid cells. Good responders showed an active immune microenvironment with sustained clonal expansion of T cells. Our longitudinal single-cell analyses elucidate the genetic, cellular and epigenetic mechanisms driving sensitivity and resistance to neoadjuvant aromatase inhibition in ER-positive breast cancer.

picks.title: Preparing for responsive management versus renal dialysis in older people living with kidney failure and frailty or multimorbidity in the UK (Prepare for Kidney Care): a two-arm, superiority, parallel-group, open-label, pragmatic, phase 3, individually randomised controlled trial.

sections.objective: The comparative effectiveness of conservative kidney management and dialysis in older people (aged ≥80 years regardless of frailty and comorbidity or aged 65-79 years if frailty or multimorbidity are present) living with kidney failure is unknown. We aimed to assess the relative effectiveness of preparing for responsive management-a protocolised version of conservative kidney management-and preparing for renal dialysis.
sections.methods: Prepare for Kidney Care was a two-arm, superiority, parallel-group, open-label, pragmatic, phase 3, individually randomised controlled trial conducted in 31 kidney centres in England, Wales, Scotland, and Northern Ireland. Eligible patients had an estimated glomerular filtration rate below 15 mL/min per 1·73 m2, confirmed by at least one additional reading in the 12 months preceding consent that was not due to acute kidney injury, and were either aged 80 years or older, or aged 65-79 years with a WHO performance status of at least 3 or a Davies comorbidity score of at least 2. Eligible participants were randomly assigned (1:1) to prepare for responsive management-a patient-centred approach focused on slowing disease progression, active symptom management, and preserving quality of life without the use of dialysis or kidney transplantation-or to prepare for renal dialysis. Randomisation was stratified by centre and minimised by age; a centralised system ensured allocation concealment until randomisation had taken place. The primary outcome was the mean difference in quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs), combining length and health-related quality of life from the patient-reported EQ-5D-5L scale, including all follow-up from randomisation to Aug 31, 2025. The primary outcome was analysed by intention to treat in the full analysis set, which included all randomly assigned participants, with missing EQ-5D-5L values for living participants imputed. Harms (hospital admissions and dialysis access complications) and adverse events (deaths and hospital admissions, by cause) were assessed in the full analysis set. The trial was registered with ISRCTN, 17133653 (completed).
sections.results: From July 1, 2017, to Aug 31, 2024, 6120 patients were screened across 31 kidney centres in the UK, 445 (7%) of whom were eligible and agreed to be randomly assigned. 228 (51%) of 445 participants were randomly assigned to prepare for responsive management and 217 (49%) of 445 participants were randomly assigned to prepare for renal dialysis. Median age was 82 years (IQR 80 to 86) and 137 (31%) of 445 participants were female. After a mean follow-up duration of 4·5 years (SD 2·1), mean QALYs were 1·354 (95% CI 1·201 to 1·508) in the prepare for responsive management group and 1·472 (1·288 to 1·655) in the prepare for renal dialysis group (adjusted mean difference -0·147 [95% CI -0·350 to 0·056] p=0·16). Specific harms outcomes were not prespecified, but hospital admission rates were similar in the two groups and dialysis access complications were significantly lower in the prepare for responsive management group (adjusted incident rate ratio 0·41 [95% CI 0·19 to 0·88]), based on 74 events in 36 participants across both groups. There were 667 serious adverse events in the prepare for responsive management group (157 [69%] of 228 participants died, with 510 hospital admissions) and 578 in the prepare for renal dialysis group (136 [63%] of 217 participants died, with 442 hospital admissions). None of these serious adverse events met the criteria for expedited reporting.
sections.conclusion: Among older people living with kidney failure and frailty or multimorbidity, we found no evidence that either preparing for responsive management or preparing for renal dialysis was superior in terms of QALYs over a mean follow-up duration of 4·5 years. This trial provides novel comparative information for clinical decision making.

picks.title: Plozasiran for Severe Hypertriglyceridemia and Risk of Pancreatitis.

sections.objective: Severe hypertriglyceridemia is associated with an increased risk of acute pancreatitis. Plozasiran, a small interfering RNA targeting APOC3 messenger RNA, lowers triglyceride levels and potentially mitigates the risk of acute pancreatitis.
sections.methods: In two double-blind, placebo-controlled trials, 757 adults with severe hypertriglyceridemia were randomly assigned in a 2:1 ratio to receive plozasiran (25 mg) or placebo at baseline and at months 3, 6, and 9. These trials had identical designs, end points, and analytic plans. The primary end point was the percent change in the fasting plasma triglyceride level from baseline to month 12. Key secondary end points were the percent change in the fasting triglyceride level from baseline to month 10, a fasting triglyceride level of less than 500 mg per deciliter (5.6 mmol per liter) and less than 150 mg per deciliter (1.7 mmol per liter), the percent change in the fasting serum triglyceride level at month 12 for patients with a baseline triglyceride level of 880 mg per deciliter or greater, and changes in remnant cholesterol and non-HDL cholesterol. A pooled analysis addressed adjudicated acute pancreatitis, incidence, and first-event timing.
sections.results: At month 12, patients in the plozasiran groups had a median triglyceride level that was lower than the baseline level by 79% and 81% in the two trials. These reductions corresponded to a median difference in the plozasiran groups as compared with the placebo groups (placebo-adjusted change) of -45 percentage points (95% confidence interval [CI], -51 to -38) and -47 percentage points (95% CI, -54 to -39). A triglyceride level of less than 500 mg per deciliter at 12 months was reported in 91% and 93% of the patients in the plozasiran groups and in 51% and 50% of those in the placebo groups (P<0.001). The rates of acute pancreatitis were 1 per 100 patient-years with plozasiran and 5 per 100 patient-years with placebo (rate ratio, 0.22; P = 0.008). Adverse events during treatment occurred in 73% of the patients in both the pooled plozasiran and placebo groups.
sections.conclusion: Among patients with severe hypertriglyceridemia, the use of plozasiran resulted in lower triglyceride levels and a lower risk of acute pancreatitis than placebo at 12 months. (Funded by Arrowhead Pharmaceuticals; SHASTA-3 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06347003; SHASTA-4, NCT06347016.).

picks.title: CRISPR mutagenesis of the MYC locus reveals a druggable ultraconserved RNA element.
picks.abstract: Noncoding sequences comprise most of the human genome; however, their functional significance remains largely elusive. Using CRISPR tiling mutagenesis with near-PAMless, high-fidelity SpRY-Cas9, we mapped the fitness landscape of an entire human gene, the 10-kb MYC locus, at base-pair resolution. This unbiased interrogation revealed that 67% of functionally essential base pairs are noncoding. Essential noncoding base pairs are under strong constraint in the human population but show limited evolutionary conservation across species. Within this landscape, we identified an ultraconserved noncoding RNA element in the 3' untranslated region (UTR) that promotes perinuclear localization of MYC mRNA and nuclear localization of MYC protein through interaction with hnRNP L. Steric-blocking antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs) targeting this element selectively eliminate diverse MYC-dependent cancer cells and inhibit growth of patient-derived tumor organoids. Together, these findings establish noncoding sequences as major carriers of functional genetic information and identify a therapeutically actionable RNA element whose targeting disrupts MYC-driven cancer.

items.title: Seafloor geodesy delineates fast megathrust relocking after the giant 2011 Tohoku earthquake.
items.abstract: How and when the subduction megathrust recovers its locking state after a great earthquake is important to understanding earthquake-cycle physics and future hazards. Here we report the delineation of the relocking process after the 2011 magnitude 9 Tohoku earthquake with 14 years of postseismic seafloor geodetic observations. These data, combined with onshore geodetic observations, analyses of repeating earthquakes, and numerical modeling, reveal how the recovery of locking is interrupted by afterslip on the megathrust and accompanied by stress relaxation in the viscoelastic upper mantle. The results indicate that the megathrust has already arrived at a locking state today similar to that before the earthquake despite the ongoing stress relaxation. The acquired knowledge aids understanding of megathrust earthquake cycles at other subduction zones.

items.title: Obesity pharmacotherapies and cognition.
items.abstract: Pharmacotherapies for obesity and type 2 diabetes are increasingly being evaluated for their effects on cognition and brain health. Evidence from preclinical models, observational cohorts, and clinical trials has intensified interest, but findings remain mixed. A central challenge is to determine whether potential cognitive effects arise from direct actions on neural circuits, indirect consequences of improved cardiometabolic health, or both. This Review examines the evidence across cardiometabolic disease, aging, and Alzheimer's disease, focusing on glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1)-based therapies and combination approaches that engage glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide, glucagon, and amylin pathways. We assess how receptor pharmacology, brain exposure, metabolic context, and disease stage shape cognitive outcomes and discuss how mechanistic clarity could guide therapies aimed at preserving or improving cognition.

items.title: Equivalence of pseudogap and pairing energy in a cuprate high-temperature superconductor.
items.abstract: The pseudogap stands out in the phase diagram of the cuprate high-temperature superconductors because its origin and relationship to superconductivity remain elusive. The origin of the pseudogap has been debated, with competing hypotheses attributing it to preformed electron pairs or local order, such as charge density waves. We present unambiguous evidence supporting the pairing scenario, using local shot-noise spectroscopy measurements in Bi2Sr2CaCu2O8+δ. Our data demonstrate that the pseudogap energy coincides with the onset of electron pairing and is spatially heterogeneous with values reaching up to 70 milli-electron volts. Our results exclude a pure local order origin of the pseudogap, link the pseudogap to Cooper pair formation, and suggest that the limiting factor for higher critical temperature in cuprates is phase coherence.

items.title: Denoising the US Census: Succinct block hierarchical regression.
items.abstract: The 2020 United States Census adopted differential privacy to protect individual confidentiality, adding calibrated noise to summary demographic measurements that are then reconciled into population tables. We developed BlueDown, a postprocessing algorithm that combines techniques from linear regression and constrained optimization while exploiting measurement structure for efficiency. On 2020 Census data, BlueDown reduced the error of groupings by race at the county level by 21 to 36% and of all county-level groupings by 9 to 58%; at the tract level, it reduced error of groupings by housing type by 38 to 61%. These gains came at no cost to confidentiality or computational efficiency and would improve the validity of research relying on this definitive dataset and analyses used to guide the distribution of more than $1.5 trillion in annual federal spending.

items.title: Glacial abrupt transitions in ocean circulation were much slower than ice-core records imply.
items.abstract: Dansgaard-Oeschger (DO) events during the last ice age are thought to reflect rapid shifts in the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC). Greenland ice cores suggest warming transitions within only a few decades-or even just over 10 years. Using precisely dated speleothem oxygen-isotope records from the Asian monsoon region, we have shown that the same DO warmings unfolded over more than a century. Isotope modeling revealed that Greenland records primarily capture a rapid atmospheric reorganization triggered by the initial sea-ice retreat in the northeastern North Atlantic, whereas the parallel AMOC recovery and hemispheric thermal adjustment proceeded much more slowly. These findings reveal that natural AMOC transitions evolved more slowly than the rapid North Greenland oxygen-isotope shifts would imply, thereby refining our understanding of "abruptness" during DO events.

items.title: Discovering molecular modulators with nanoswitch screening.
items.abstract: Molecules that modulate protein-protein interactions, including through ternary complex formation, have been established as key therapeutics. Yet they can be challenging to discover, as standard screening approaches often lack throughput or fail to directly assay multibody interactions. We addressed this by combining DNA nanoswitch-based selection of nucleotide-encoded libraries with next-generation sequencing to create FIND (Functional Interaction-based Nanoswitch Discovery), which enables ultrahigh-throughput discovery of compounds that induce or increase protein-protein interactions. We demonstrate FIND by discovering nanobodies that stabilize the interaction between angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 and the receptor-binding domain of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 and by discovering agonists of peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma from a DNA-barcoded small-molecule library. By enabling rapid discovery of molecular modulators, FIND could lead to new therapeutics across many conditions.

items.title: Targeting hormone conversion through dietary fiber improves polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome.
items.abstract: Excessive androgens serve as a primary driver for many phenotypic features of polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS). Although dietary fiber has been shown to alleviate PMOS, its effects on androgen concentrations and the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. In a clinical trial, we demonstrated that a dietary fiber combination consisting of inulin, resistant starch, and β-glucan reduces androgen concentrations in patients' plasma. Mechanistically, dietary fiber increased the abundance of Bacteroides xylanisolvens, which converts androstenedione into a nonandrogenic secondary hormone metabolite we named coproandrosterone, which is further metabolized by gut microbiota into dihydro-coproandrosterone. This metabolic pathway was validated in a mouse model. These findings highlight the potential of dietary fiber to alleviate PMOS by modulating androgen homeostasis through gut microbiota, offering insights for prebiotic and probiotic therapies.

items.title: When fat adapts: From physiological remodeling to disease.
items.abstract: Adipose tissue undergoes extensive remodeling to adapt to changing physiological demands. This plasticity encompasses changes in adipocyte metabolism and number, extracellular matrix organization, vascularization, immune composition, and innervation. When coordinated, these processes preserve energy buffering, thermogenesis, endocrine function, and local tissue support. Pathological adipose tissue remodeling drives obesity-related complications and contributes to many diseases involving organ-associated adipose depots throughout the body. In cancer, tumor-associated fat can develop a metabolic and fibroinflammatory niche that promotes tumor growth and invasion, and remodeling of other depots can directly disrupt neighboring tissues. Recent studies have identified mesenchymal, immune, vascular, and adipocyte states that govern adaptive or pathological outcomes. These findings broaden therapeutic goals beyond reducing fat mass toward restoring adipogenesis, substrate turnover, thermogenic capacity, and tissue-niche function.

items.title: Tumor metastasis co-opts liver hematopoiesis to promote immunosuppression.
items.abstract: Cancer-associated hematopoietic abnormalities contribute to systemic immunosuppression. However, whether tumors can initiate localized extramedullary hematopoiesis to suppress antitumor immunity remains unclear. In this study, we identify a distinct form of hepatic hematopoiesis driven by liver metastasis-associated hematopoietic stem cells (LM-HSCs). Liver metastases establish ectopic periportal hematopoietic niches that recruit bone marrow HSCs through Kupffer cell-dependent C-C motif chemokine receptor 1 (CCR1) signaling. Although LM-HSCs retain self-renewal and multipotency, cAMP response element-binding protein (CREB) activation skews their differentiation toward the myeloid lineage, particularly annexin A1-positive (ANXA1+) immature neutrophils. These neutrophils produce glucocorticoids, which activate glucocorticoid receptor signaling in a paracrine manner and induce immune checkpoint receptor expression and functional anergy in CD8+ T and natural killer cells. Collectively, these findings suggest that liver metastases reprograms hepatic hematopoiesis to promote immunosuppression.

items.title: Echoes of the Anthropocene: Noise pollution as a global threat.
items.abstract: Anthropogenic noise is a rapidly expanding global pollutant, but its effects across biological levels from individuals to ecosystems remain unquantified. We conducted phylogenetically controlled meta-analyses of 214 experimental studies on 177 aquatic and terrestrial species with ranges that span six continents. Noise altered at least one physiological, developmental, or behavioral trait in 80% of species studied, with declines in fitness and abundance and disruptions of predator-prey interactions. Effects occurred in every habitat, although response mechanisms varied for some traits and species, creating winners and losers. Only multispecies analyses can reveal such species- and ecosystem-level impacts of anthropogenic stressors. Our results establish noise as a novel selection pressure reshaping ecosystem dynamics and as a pervasive stressor requiring soundscape protection alongside habitat conservation.

items.title: Obesity management medications: The way forward.
items.abstract: Obesity is now widely recognized as a chronic progressive condition. The altered biological mechanisms that cause obesity frequently require long-term treatment, including pharmacotherapies or bariatric surgery. In recent decades, the pathophysiology of obesity has been understood to an extent that obesity management medication (OMM) discovery could be rationally pursued. Advances in defining the regulation of food intake and energy expenditure by molecular communication from peripheral organs to the brain led to the development of OMMs that appear capable of safely achieving scalable and sustained body weight loss. However, side effects, heterogeneous treatment responses, long-term metabolic adaptations, adherence, and other factors may limit the use of existing OMMs and justify the development of additional medications to improve the health of people living with obesity.

items.title: Quantum gas microscopy of three-flavor Hubbard systems.
items.abstract: Hubbard systems are paradigmatic realizations of strongly correlated many-body systems. Introducing additional species breaks the SU(2) symmetry of the Hubbard model and leads to a wide variety of new exotic quantum phases. Here, we extended quantum gas microscopy to three-flavor Fermi lattice gases in the Hubbard regime. Relying on site- and flavor-resolved detection, we studied the phase diagram of the three-flavor Hubbard model and found signatures of flavor-selective localization and selective pairing at temperatures down to the tunneling energy scale. Our measurements were then compared with numerical linked-cluster expansion calculations. Further increase of phase space density may enable the observation of a distinct pair Mott phase at half filling and shows a path toward the study of color superfluidity and other aspects of quantum chromodynamics.

items.title: The first 1000 days: Modeling language learning from individual children's everyday speech.
items.abstract: Children learn to understand and speak from the speech around them, yet how that everyday input shapes learning remains unresolved. Large language models show that language is learnable from data, but their scale and training conditions differ sharply from a child's natural experience. We trained cognitively feasible, child-specific models on longitudinal home recordings from eight children across their first 1000 days of life. Each model learned incrementally from a single child's ordered speech input without prior linguistic knowledge, developing phoneme-like and word-form representations that tracked each child's learning pace. Learning was dependent on dense daily sampling and replay of recent input, indicating that both experience- and memory-related processes are necessary. These findings show that everyday experience contains sufficient structure for language learning and establish child-specific modeling for testing developmental theories.

items.title: Stacked porous NiTi structure with low cost and ultrahigh fatigue life for elastocaloric cooling.
items.abstract: Elastocaloric cooling (eC) uses shape memory alloys (SMAs) as energy-efficient, eco-friendly refrigerants. However, cost-effectively fabricating SMAs into fatigue-resistant, heat transfer-enhanced structures remains a key obstacle to commercialization of the eC technology. We introduce a "stamping and stacking" (S-S) method for producing porous, fatigue-resistant SMA structures. Honeycomb-like chips are stamped from nitinol (NiTi) thin sheets and then stacked into a layered tubular structure to increase heat exchange surface and at the same time avoid buckling and splitting failures encountered in existing SMA structures. The stacked structure endures >108 compression cycles and can deliver high specific cooling power of 3850 watts per kilogram. Our S-S method reduces fabrication costs by one order of magnitude compared with existing approaches, enabling mass production of eC refrigerant structures for commercial deployment.

items.title: Direct evidence for psychoactive cannabis use 2800 years ago.
items.abstract: Cannabis is the world's most-used illicit psychoactive plant, yet direct prehistoric evidence for its consumption is rare. In this study, we present the earliest direct evidence of cannabis use: offerings of plant parts and chemical compounds in ancient human hair recovered from a monumental tomb in Siberia. The findings suggest that the plant was used for its psychoactive qualities across Eurasia, where specific wild populations might have had naturally higher active compound levels. We show that the practice of cannabis consumption dates back at least 2800 years, anchoring debates around contemporary usage and informing discussions on cannabis in medicine, public health, law, and industry.

items.title: Intravenous Thrombolysis for Acute Ischemic Stroke - New Directions.
items.abstract: In the past 5 years, substantial changes have been made in the use of intravenous thrombolysis (IVT) in patients with acute ischemic stroke. Integrating IVT with endovascular thrombectomy, which improves outcomes in patients with stroke due to large cerebral vessel occlusion, has been a particular challenge. This review discusses the underlying vascular targets for IVT and thrombectomy, the increasing use of tenecteplase instead of alteplase, broadening indications for the use of IVT, and ancillary drugs and dosing methods that may augment the success of IVT.

A triglyceride level of less than 500 mg per deciliter at 12 months was reported in 91% and 93% of the patients in the plozasiran groups and in 51% and 50% of those in the placebo groups (P<0.001). The rates of acute pancreatitis were 1 per 100 patient-years with plozasiran and 5 per 100 patient-years with placebo (rate ratio, 0.22; P = 0.008). Adverse events during treatment occurred in 73% of the patients in both the pooled plozasiran and placebo groups.
sections.conclusion: Among patients with severe hypertriglyceridemia, the use of plozasiran resulted in lower triglyceride levels and a lower risk of acute pancreatitis than placebo at 12 months. (Funded by Arrowhead Pharmaceuticals; SHASTA-3 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06347003; SHASTA-4, NCT06347016.).

items.title: Retatrutide, a Triple Hormone Receptor Agonist, for Treatment of Obesity.

sections.objective: Retatrutide is a triple-receptor agonist of glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide, glucagon-like peptide-1, and glucagon receptors.
sections.methods: In this phase 3, randomized, double-blind trial, we assigned adults with obesity without diabetes to receive a once-weekly subcutaneous injection of retatrutide (at a dose of 4 mg, 9 mg, or 12 mg) or placebo for 80 weeks. Primary outcomes (evaluated in the 9-mg and 12-mg groups each vs. placebo) were the percent change in body weight and the change in the WOMAC pain score (ranging from 1 to 10, with higher scores indicating worse pain) in the subgroup of 574 participants with knee osteoarthritis and the change in the apnea-hypopnea index in the 243 participants with obstructive sleep apnea. For weight-related end points, intercurrent events were handled by a treatment-regimen estimand (intention-to-treat [ITT]). For end points in participants with knee osteoarthritis or obstructive sleep apnea, a hybrid-treatment estimand was applied, with a hypothetical strategy for intercurrent events suggesting treatment failure; ITT results are also reported.
sections.results: A total of 2339 participants underwent randomization. The mean percent change in body weight in the retatrutide groups was -17.6% (4-mg dose), -23.7% (9-mg dose), and -25.0% (12-mg dose) versus -3.9% in the placebo group (differences, -19.8 and -21.0 percentage points, respectively; P<0.001 for both comparisons). Among the participants with knee osteoarthritis, the corresponding changes in the pain score in the retatrutide groups for the hybrid estimand were -3.2, -3.5, and -3.6 versus -1.9 with placebo (differences, -1.6 and -1.8 points; both P<0.001); the corresponding changes for the ITT estimand were -3.4, -3.9, and -4.1 versus -2.5 with placebo (differences, -1.4 and -1.6 points; both P<0.001). Among the participants with obstructive sleep apnea, the corresponding changes in events per hour in the retatrutide groups for the hybrid-treatment estimand were -22.9, -34.3, and -31.7 versus -9.9 (differences, -24.4 and -21.9; both P<0.001); the corresponding changes for the ITT estimand were -22.8, -34.3, and -32.1 versus -9.6 (differences, -24.7 and -22.5; both P<0.001). The most common adverse events were gastrointestinal.
sections.conclusion: In adults with obesity, retatrutide resulted in significant weight reduction, reduced pain in participants with knee osteoarthritis, and reduced apnea-hypopnea events in participants with obstructive sleep apnea. (Funded by Eli Lilly; TRIUMPH-1 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05929066.).

items.title: Targeted Use of Computed Tomographic Coronary Angiography in Acute Chest Pain.

sections.objective: Many patients with suspected acute coronary syndrome in whom myocardial infarction has been ruled out in the emergency department remain at risk for cardiovascular events. Whether further investigation reduces this risk is unknown.
sections.methods: In a multicenter, randomized, controlled trial, patients who presented to an emergency department in 14 hospitals across the United Kingdom were enrolled if myocardial infarction had been ruled out and high-sensitivity cardiac troponin testing indicated an intermediate risk of a cardiovascular event (maximum high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I or T concentration, >5 ng per liter). Participants were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive either outpatient computed tomographic (CT) coronary angiography-guided care or standard care. The primary outcome was a composite of myocardial infarction or death from a cardiac cause.
sections.results: From September 18, 2019, to May 11, 2023, a total of 3170 participants (median age, 61 years; female sex, 30.2%) were assigned to undergo CT coronary angiography (1587 participants) or receive standard care (1583 participants). At 90 days after randomization, CT coronary angiography had been performed in 1462 participants (92.1%) in the CT coronary angiography group and in 35 participants (2.2%) in the standard-care group. Overall, 7 participants (0.4%) had a CT coronary angiography-related adverse event. After a median of 3.0 years, at which point the number of primary-outcome events in the standard-care group exceeded the prespecified minimum of 97, a primary-outcome event had occurred in 112 participants (7.1%) in the CT coronary angiography group and in 116 (7.3%) in the standard-care group (adjusted hazard ratio, 0.95; 95% confidence interval, 0.73 to 1.23; P = 0.71).
sections.conclusion: In patients with suspected acute coronary syndrome in whom myocardial infarction had been ruled out, routine CT coronary angiography-guided management did not result in a lower incidence of subsequent myocardial infarction or death from a cardiac cause than standard care. (Funded by the British Heart Foundation; TARGET-CTCA ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT03952351.).

items.title: Prevalence of Silent Atherosclerosis across Adult Life.

sections.objective: Atherosclerosis may begin in early adulthood and remain clinically silent for decades before cardiovascular disease manifests. Although silent atherosclerosis is associated with cardiovascular events and death independent of traditional cardiovascular disease risk factors, its age- and sex-specific prevalence, vascular territory distribution, and plaque volume across adult life remain incompletely defined.
sections.methods: We conducted a prospective cohort study in Denmark and Spain. Adults 18 to 70 years of age without known atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease were enrolled in five prespecified age strata that included balanced numbers of women and men. Silent atherosclerosis was assessed at baseline with three-dimensional vascular ultrasonography of the carotid and femoral arteries and with coronary computed tomographic angiography.
sections.results: A total of 16,808 adults were enrolled in the study. The mean (±SD) age of the participants was 45±12 years, and 51.4% were women. Silent atherosclerosis was present in 57.1% of the participants (95% confidence interval, 56.3 to 58.0). In the youngest age stratum (18 to 29 years), atherosclerosis was present in 8.7% of the men and 6.7% of the women; prevalence increased with age, with a later, steeper midlife rise among women. Among participants in the younger age strata, atherosclerosis was most often peripheral and confined to a single vascular territory; with increasing age, plaque volume increased exponentially and the prevalence of multiarterial involvement became more frequent. Isolated coronary-artery atherosclerosis was uncommon in every age stratum (≤9.3% of men and ≤5.0% of women).
sections.conclusion: This study of silent atherosclerosis showed that the disease was detectable in early adulthood, with age- and sex-associated increases in prevalence across arterial territories and marked increases in plaque volume. (Funded by the Novo Nordisk Foundation; REACT ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06692127.).

items.title: Effect of Electronic Behavioral Nudges on Low-Value Preoperative Testing: A Pragmatic Randomized Clinical Trial.

sections.objective: Robust randomized trials have demonstrated that routine testing before cataract surgery does not improve outcomes; however, despite this evidence and long-standing professional society recommendations discouraging routine testing, preoperative testing remains frequent in real-world practice, with most patients undergoing cataract surgery receiving at least 1 preoperative test. To measure whether electronic health record (EHR)-embedded, behavioral science-informed nudges reduce preoperative testing.
sections.methods: This pragmatic randomized clinical trial was conducted at a large academic health system (UCLA Health) in Los Angeles, California. Physicians performing preoperative evaluations were randomized to 1 of 3 EHR nudge alerts or usual care. All encounters with patients undergoing a preoperative visit with a randomized physician within 30 days of cataract surgery were silently enrolled. Patients were enrolled from June 24, 2021, to April 11, 2023. Data were analyzed from June 2020 (1 year prior to first enrollment) to April 2024 (1 year after last enrollment). The EHR interruptive alerts cited professional society recommendations against routine testing; each emphasized a different potential patient harm, including lack of safety benefit, financial burden, or psychological stress.
sections.results: During the enrollment period, 229 of 776 randomized physicians had 1 or more eligible encounter during which a patient was enrolled. Together, these clinicians had 1045 preoperative encounters during the intervention period with 967 unique patients. Mean (SD) patient age was 72.1 (9.1) years, and 595 encounters (56.9%) were with female patients. Mean (SD) signed preoperative testing rates decreased from 83% (29%) to 79% (31%) in the combined intervention arms vs 84% (30%) to 82% (31%) in the control arm. In mixed-effects models, exposure to any nudge was not associated with a reduction in overall testing (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 0.68; 95% CI, 0.34-1.34). In prespecified secondary analyses, 16% of orders were cancelled following exposure to a nudge, and the psychological stress nudge was associated with decreases in rates of complete blood cell count (aOR, 0.37; 95% CI, 0.18-0.75; P = .01) and electrocardiogram orders (aOR, 0.42; 95% CI, 0.21-0.83; P = .01) vs control.
sections.conclusion: This randomized clinical trial of EHR nudges did not reach statistical significance on the primary outcome of overall preoperative testing. Secondary outcomes suggest future studies might consider the role of a psychological stress nudge in combination with other behavioral, workflow, and/or payment changes.
sections.other: The primary outcome was the change in the proportion of preoperative cataract surgery encounters with any signed testing order(s) between the 12-month period before the physicians' first encounter (enrollment) and the 12-month postencounter period. Secondary outcomes included order cancellation rates among clinicians exposed to the intervention, separate comparisons of each nudge, and analyses comparing orders for specific categories of tests.

items.title: Potential Disparities in Access to Adult Strabismus Care.

sections.objective: Adult strabismus impacts quality of life through diplopia, eye strain, and psychological burden. Access to care may be limited by various factors, yet disparities in adult strabismus care have not been examined nationally. To evaluate potential disparities in access to adult strabismus care across the US by practice type, insurance status, and county-level socioeconomic characteristics.
sections.methods: This national secret shopper study used standardized telephone calls to US pediatric ophthalmology practices identified through the American Association for Pediatric Ophthalmology and Strabismus and the American Academy of Ophthalmology that simulated appointment scheduling for an adult patients with strabismus. Of 1064 practices contacted, 1060 were included after excluding 4 clinics with disconnected phone numbers. These data were analyzed from August 2025 to September 2026.
sections.results: Overall, 23.8% (252 of 1060) of practices offered an appointment under at least 1 insurance scenario. Patients using Medicaid had a lower appointment success rate than those with commercial insurance (161 of 648 [24.8%] vs 91 of 194 [46.9%]; difference, -22.1 percentage points; 95% CI, -29.8 to -14.3; P < .001). In multivariable regression, other practice types (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 1.82; 95% CI, 1.28-2.58; P = .001) and commercial insurance (aOR, 2.36; 95% CI, 1.67-3.33; P = .001) had higher appointment success, while majority racial and ethnic minority counties (aOR, 0.66; 95% CI, 0.45-0.97; P = .04) and lower median household income counties (aOR, 0.64; 95% CI, 0.44-0.93; P = .02) had lower odds. Among practices offering appointments, academic centers had longer wait times than other practices (mean [SD], 95.1 [59.3] days vs 57.0 [54.1] days; 38.1 days difference; 95% CI, 21.2-55.1; P < .001), as did lower-income counties (mean [SD], 78.6 [68.1] days vs 61.3 [52.6] days; -17.4 days difference; 95% CI, -33.3 to -1.4; P = .03).
sections.conclusion: This national secret shopper study identified potential disparities in adult strabismus care access. Commercial insurance and other practice types had higher appointment success, while majority racial and ethnic minority and lower-income counties had reduced access and longer wait times. These findings highlight a potential unmet likely benefit of adult strabismus practitioners and support targeted policy interventions to improve equitable access to care.
sections.other: Practice type (academic vs other), insurance type (Medicaid vs commercial insurance), and county-level characteristics, including race and ethnicity majority, median household income, Area Deprivation Index (ADI), and Social Vulnerability Index (SVI). Appointment success (ability to schedule appointment during call) and appointment wait time (days between call date and earliest available appointment).

items.title: Genome-Wide Association Study Meta-Analysis of Central Serous Chorioretinopathy.

sections.objective: The pathophysiology of central serous chorioretinopathy (CSC) remains incompletely understood, and there is ongoing debate regarding the origin of primary dysfunction. To elucidate the genetic architecture of CSC and map susceptibility loci to specific ocular cell types and molecular pathways.
sections.methods: This genetic association study was a genome-wide association study (GWAS) meta-analysis aggregating data from 5 large biobank cohorts and included 2584 patients with CSC and 1 044 455 control participants of European ancestry. Cohort data were from July 1, 2010, to October 31, 2023; data analysis was performed from Febuary 2024 to January 2026. Post-GWAS functional mapping was performed using mendelian randomization, bayesian colocalization, and single-cell disease relevance scoring across human ocular tissue atlases. The relevance of the genetic findings was demonstrated by building a CSC genetic risk score and applying it to the UK Biobank (UKB).
sections.results: The meta-analysis identified 10 risk loci reaching the genome-wide threshold (P < 5 × 10-8), including 3 novel loci (TGFB1, LINC00551, and LOC105375630) and 7 replicated loci (CFH, GATA5, PREX1, CD46, NOTCH4, PTPRB, and TNFRSF10A). Integrative post-GWAS analysis prioritized 10 genes, including TGFB1, TNFRSF10A, and CFH, as likely causal effectors. Single-cell enrichment mapping revealed that CSC genetic risk is concentrated in scleral tissue (P < .001) and vascular endothelial cells (P < .001). Mendelian randomization pointed to circulating TGFB1 and TNFRSF10A levels as associated with CSC risk. A CSC genetic risk score applied in UKB revealed a higher frequency of CSC-relevant abnormalities on macular optical coherence tomography in participants in the top 1% of polygenic risk (18/109 [16.5%] vs 8/134 [6.0%]; difference, 10.5 percentage points; 95% CI, 2.6-19.1; adjusted odds ratio, 4.05; 95% CI, 1.65-10.87; P = .002).
sections.conclusion: Convergent genetic evidence supports CSC as a primary disorder of the sclera and choroidal vasculature with retinal pigment epithelium changes likely representing a downstream consequence. Integrative post-GWAS analysis pointed to complement regulation (CFH, CD46), vascular integrity and endothelial cell signaling (PTPRB, TNFRSF10A, NOTCH4, PREX1), and scleral extracellular matrix biology (TGFB1) as important in CSC.
sections.other: Identification of risk loci reaching the genome-wide threshold, prioritized putative causal genes, enrichment of genetic risk within specific ocular tissues and cell types, and performance of a GRS in the independent UKB dataset.

items.title: A bivalent chromatin reader-WOX5 module maintains root stem cell niche in Arabidopsis.
items.abstract: Root stem cell niche maintenance requires precise control of quiescent center (QC) and columella stem cell (CSC) activity, yet how chromatin regulators interface with key transcription factors remains poorly understood. Here, we identify the bivalent chromatin reader EARLY BOLTING IN SHORT DAYS (EBS) as an essential regulator of root stem cell maintenance in Arabidopsis. A strong ebs-1 mutant shows CSC differentiation and QC activation, and EBS function requires its histone mark-recognizing BAH and PHD domains and a C-terminal SUMO-interacting motif. EBS physically interacts with the QC master regulator WUSCHEL-RELATED HOMEOBOX 5 (WOX5) and, together with WOX5, activates WOX5 transcription by promoting EBS enrichment at the WOX5 promoter. Consistently, wox5-1 is epistatic to ebs-1, and WOX5 overexpression rescues the ebs-1 stem cell defects. Together, this work uncovers a chromatin-based positive autoregulatory loop that integrates histone-state recognition and transcriptional feedback, providing a framework for epigenetic control of stem cell fate in plants.

items.title: Decoding the regulatory programs governing glioblastoma plasticity.
items.abstract: Glioblastoma is incurable and resistant to therapy despite genomic stability under treatment1-8, suggesting that non-genetic cellular plasticity is a central driver of progression. Whether such plasticity reflects stochastic state switching or is governed by predictable gene regulation has remained unclear9-13. Here we introduce scDORI (single-cell deep multi-omic regulatory inference)-a deep-learning framework that infers enhancer-driven gene-regulatory networks at single-cell resolution-and apply it to single-nucleus multiome profiles of more than one million cells from primary glioblastomas. Integrating computational inference with systematic perturbation screens across patient-derived models, we show that a structured regulatory program with an asymmetric interplay of activators and repressors governs cellular plasticity in glioblastoma. The resulting transition landscape is hierarchical and predictable, but permits cross-lineage trajectories that are absent from normal neurodevelopment. Within this landscape, low-plasticity states such as the neuronal-like state are not stable differentiation end points but actively maintained configurations, stabilized by a network of safeguard repressors that silence alternative fates. We identify MYT1L as the dominant member of this network, and show that it binds to and represses master regulators of every alternative state to consolidate neuronal-like identity. MYT1L restricted plasticity even under standard-of-care therapy and suppressed tumour growth and invasion in vivo. Conversely, loss of MYT1L reactivated plasticity and accelerated malignant features, indicating that low-plasticity identity requires continuous repression. These findings reframe malignant cell state stability as a balance between activation and continuous repression, and nominate safeguard repressors as candidate therapeutic targets that are distinct from differentiation-inducing activators, with potential relevance across cancers in which phenotypic switching drives therapy resistance.

items.title: A two-dimensional reticular triaxial molecularly woven fabric.
items.abstract: Inspired by macroscopic weaving techniques1-4, molecular weaving, which interlaces molecular strands into ordered networks, has emerged as a powerful strategy for designing functional materials with emergent properties5,6. However, so far, molecular weaving has relied mainly on linear building blocks and biaxial structures. Higher-order weaving (≥3 axes) of nonlinear building blocks is expected to produce intriguing architectures and bring new and unforeseen functions to the resulting materials; however, their construction and property investigation remain underexplored. Here we report a two-dimensional reticular triaxial woven polymer network constructed by incorporating C3-symmetric macrocycles into the woven structure through dative B-N polymerization. The resulting material not only exhibits unique topological chirality and robust mechanical properties but it also serves as a porous material that permits the separation of representative aromatic/aliphatic compounds. This functional utility highlights how higher-order triaxial woven topologies can provide unique advantages in terms of regulating material properties and introduces an extra topological dimension for the construction of functional materials.

items.title: In vivo CAR-T double knockout screen maps synergistic antitumour gene pairs.
items.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cell therapy has transformed the treatment of haematological malignancies, but its efficacy remains limited by multiple negative regulatory mechanisms intrinsic to T cells1-4. Here we perform a high-throughput in vivo CAR-T double-knockout (DKO) CRISPR screen, and identify multiple DKO gene pairs that are both effective and synergistic. The top pair, NR4A1-SOCS3 DKO, has multiple favourable immunological features. Whole-transcriptome profiling and in vivo single-cell RNA sequencing reveal that NR4A1-SOCS3 DKO specifically upregulates metabolic pathways in CAR-T cells, which show significantly higher metabolic fitness and mitochondrial activity. NR4A1-SOCS3 DKO CAR-T cells and T cells exhibit exceptionally potent antitumour efficacy and long-term tumour control across different tumour models without compromising safety features. NR4A1-SOCS3 DKO outperforms several benchmark single-gene and dual-gene modifications in T cells and CAR-T cells5-9. These data demonstrate high-throughput in vivo CAR-T DKO screening for rapid discovery of combination targets, and establish NR4A1-SOCS3 as a promising pair of intracellular checkpoints to engineer high-performance CAR-T therapies against cancer.

items.title: Observation of prethermal dynamical phase transitions and resonant melting.
items.abstract: The dynamics of isolated quantum systems following a sudden quench has a central role in many areas of material science, high-energy physics and quantum chemistry1-4. Such far-from-equilibrium quantum dynamics-which features complex phenomena with implications for thermalization, non-equilibrium phase transitions and Floquet phase engineering5-8-is challenging to study numerically, in particular, in high-dimensional systems9,10. Here we use a programmable neutral-atom quantum simulator11 to systematically explore quench dynamics in spin models with up to 180 qubits. By initializing the system in a product state and performing quenches across a broad parameter space, we discover several stable, qualitatively distinct dynamical regimes. We trace their robustness to Floquet-like prethermal steady states8 that are stabilized over exponentially long emergent timescales by strong dynamical constraints. We further observe sharp peaks in the dynamical response that are quantitatively explained by the structured melting of prethermalization through resonances. In two dimensions, we uncover a prethermally driven, first-order dynamical phase transition linked to the proliferation of Néel-order defects6,12, and probe it quantitatively using a generalized Clausius-Clapeyron test. Together, these results establish a programmable route to high-energy prethermal phase structure: long-lived dynamical phases, their resonant breakdown and a first-order dynamical phase transition that is not inherited from the equilibrium phase boundaries.

items.title: A conserved flowering-time module underlies double-season cropping.
items.abstract: Adapting crops to intensive cultivation systems under climate change requires varieties that combine yield potential with optimized flowering and maturation1,2. In central and eastern China, barley has long been cultivated in a double-season cropping system, in which early flowering and maturation are critical for escaping presummer terminal heat stress and enabling flexible rotation with summer crops3,4. Here we trace the genomic footprints of 80 years of modern breeding in China using 505 representative cultivars and identify a flowering-time module defined by a single amino acid substitution in PHYTOCHROME C in combination with a winter-type VERNALIZATION 1 haplotype that underpins this adaptation. The derived allele accelerates heading and maturity, and its frequency has risen sharply in modern autumn-sown varieties. Using base editing in barley and wheat, we confirm causality and demonstrate that this flowering-time combination module, PhyC-VRN1, is functionally conserved across Triticeae. Our results identify and experimentally validate a breeding-relevant flowering-time module that has been selected during modern breeding to enable intensive crop rotations, as well as demonstrate how precision genome editing can be used to reconstruct such adaptive modules for climate-resilient crop design.

items.title: Comprehensive mapping of essential-gene interactions in M. tuberculosis.
items.abstract: Mycobacterium tuberculosis, the causative agent of tuberculosis, remains the world's deadliest pathogen1. Despite intensive study, many of its genes remain uncharacterized, which limits the insight that can be gained into tuberculosis biology and constrains drug development. Genetic interaction (GI) mapping is a powerful strategy to define functional relationships between genes by quantifying how the phenotypic effects of combined perturbations deviate from expectations based on single-gene perturbations2,3. Here we develop a dual-sgRNA CRISPR-interference platform that enables high-throughput GI mapping in mycobacteria. We address key technical challenges in library construction and data interpretation by incorporating unique barcodes for each sgRNA pair and implementing a robust statistical pipeline for GI detection. Focusing on essential genes, we generate comprehensive GI maps in the model mycobacterium Mycobacterium smegmatis and the pathogen M. tuberculosis. These maps recapitulate known biology, uncover thousands of previously unrecognized interactions and identify functional connections between essential genes and drug targets. By generating AlphaFold3-based protein-protein interaction predictions4 for all gene pairs in our GI maps, we show that a subset of GIs is likely to reflect underlying physical associations. Validation of selected GIs confirms both novel biological relationships and opportunities for synergistic targeting. Overall, this work establishes a generalizable framework for dual-gene perturbation and defines the architecture of essential-gene networks in mycobacteria, advancing both our understanding of tuberculosis biology and the rational design of combination therapies.

items.title: Aggression experience and observation drive shared behavioural and neural changes.
items.abstract: The ability to observe the social behaviour of others and use observed information to bias future action is a fundamental building block of social cognition1-3. Aggression observation activates hypothalamic neurons relevant for aggression control4,5, but whether observation and experience engage common circuit mechanisms that promote a new shared behavioural policy is unclear. Here we develop a strategy to perform large-scale cell-type-specific recordings across subcortical networks for social behaviour generation and learning. We record longitudinally while animals train through direct aggression experience or observation, then probe shared differences in behaviour and neural activity in a novel aggression context. After training, we detect unique signatures of a shared adaptive behavioural strategy that is absent in animals without training. During aggression observation, observed behaviour recruits widespread activation across subcortical networks for behavioural generation and mimics activity evoked by experienced behaviour, and shared neural changes persist into the novel aggression context. Multiregion modelling reveals shared changes to a core aggression network across both experience and observation, including a widespread reduction in inhibition, which we find is necessary for adaptive behavioural change. Together, this demonstrates that experience-like activity during aggression observation can recruit a shared inhibitory plasticity mechanism that biases behaviour toward adaptive proactive behavioural strategies.

items.title: Synergy in viral-bacterial co-infection expedites algal bloom demise.
items.abstract: Algal bloom demise, often caused by viruses, is a major driver of carbon cycling in the surface ocean1,2. However, although blooms collapse synchronously, fewer than 30% of algal cells are actively infected by viruses3, indicating the involvement of additional mortality agents. Here we quantified tripartite interactions within a synthetic community composed of the abundant coccolithophore Gephyrocapsa huxleyi, bacteria and viruses isolated during a bloom. We found that bacteria significantly enhanced virus-induced algal mortality in G. huxleyi as well as in three other globally widespread microalgae. We quantified this interaction using two new metrics: the synergy index, which measures viral-bacterial interaction strength, and the benefit index, which assesses changes in bacterial fitness. We identified Alteromonas bacteria as drivers of viral-bacterial co-infection, with consistently high synergy index and benefit index. We found that during algal blooms, Alteromonas displayed high chemoattraction towards infected cell extracts, accumulated in aggregates derived from bloom demise, and increased in abundance during oceanic bloom collapse. Viral-bacterial synergy represents a previously unrecognized mortality agent that controls bloom termination, modulating the balance between the carbon-recycling viral shunt and the carbon-exporting viral shuttle pathways, which influence global carbon cycling4-6.

items.title: Ecological and social cues orchestrate concerted courtship in Drosophila.
items.abstract: Mating decisions are often attributed to the sensory signalling between prospective sexual partners. Yet these interactions are also shaped by the broader environmental context in which they unfold, to appropriately align sexual arousal with reproductive opportunities1-6. Here we show that in Drosophila erecta mating is strictly contingent on the ecological and social environment generated as flies densely aggregate in groups on a food patch. We find that food volatiles directly promote male sexual arousal, triggering individuals to sample and pursue potential mates, giving rise to dynamic interactions across the group. The ensuing visual motion transforms each male's visual field, which in turn further amplifies his arousal, generating a multisensory feedback loop that coordinately promotes courtship across individuals. D. erecta's strict dependence on environmental cues appears latent in related species, such as Drosophila melanogaster, where food odour can promote arousal7 but is dispensable for vigorous courtship. Comparative circuit analyses show that species-specific thresholds for sexual arousal reflect variation in how olfactory input modulates conserved nodes controlling courtship drive, rendering food volatiles a strict sensory gate only in D. erecta. Together, our findings highlight how environmental cues not directly tied to sexual signalling can profoundly influence reproductive behaviour and reorganize the social landscape to ensure mating occurs in contexts where reproductive opportunities are abundant.

items.title: Twist-angle-dependent quantum phase diagrams in moiré bilayer MoTe2.
items.abstract: Two-dimensional semiconducting moiré superlattices provide a highly tunable platform for investigating strongly correlated and topological quantum phases1-5. As a prototypical example, twisted bilayer MoTe2 (tMoTe2) has been shown to host fractional topological phases at zero magnetic field6-20. However, their evolution with twist angle and competition with other correlated quantum states remain largely unexplored. Here we report a systematic transport study of twist-angle-dependent phase diagrams in tMoTe2 across a range of 3.79°-5.76°, revealing an evolution from valley-polarized, fractional topological states to valley-degenerate correlated states and superconductivity. At relatively small twist angles, partially filled Chern bands of tMoTe2 host fractional quantum anomalous Hall states following the Jain sequence, together with signatures of an anomalous composite Fermi liquid at moiré hole filling factor νh = 1/2. Increasing twist angle progressively suppresses fractional topological phases and reconstructs the half-filled Chern band into symmetry-breaking integer Chern insulating states. At νh = 1, we observe a transition from robust integer quantum anomalous Hall insulators at small angles to displacement-field-tuned, topologically trivial correlated insulators at larger angles. At twist angles above approximately 5.6°, superconductivity emerges adjacent to the νh = 1 correlated insulator, with a phase diagram closely resembling that recently reported in twisted bilayer WSe2 (refs. 21-24). Our results indicate a unified twist-angle-driven phase evolution linking fractional topology, symmetry breaking, magnetic order and superconductivity, providing new insight into the emergent quantum phenomena in moiré systems.

items.title: Towards observing interstitial hydrogen in solution in metal lattices.
items.abstract: Hydrogen-bearing materials are central to low-carbon energy technologies1, but hydrogen itself is difficult to detect and localize at the nanoscale2-6. This hinders the development of advanced materials with better efficiency. Atom probe tomography (APT) can map hydrogen in three dimensions and at high resolution, yet characterization of dilute, mobile, interstitial hydrogen in metals has remained challenging because of low solubility, the ambiguity owing to hydrogen trapping by structural defects, as well as the artefacts introduced during hydrogen introduction4-6. Here we address whether interstitial hydrogen in solution in materials can be distinguished from defect-trapped hydrogen in APT. Using deuterium as a proxy for hydrogen, together with face-centred cubic (FCC) multi-principal-element alloys (MPEAs) containing coherent FCC precipitates, we show that deuterium atoms reproducibly concentrate in hydrogen-affinitive phases in a manner consistent with theoretical predictions. We further resolve differences in deuterium content between phases with distinct local chemistries and crystal structures, consistent with their different calculated hydrogen solution energies. These findings demonstrate that APT can move beyond identifying hydrides and solute-decorated defects to examine hydrogen in solid solution, providing new insights into hydrogen partitioning in structural alloys and informing materials design for hydrogen-related applications.

items.title: The neural basis of flavour-nutrient learning.
items.abstract: Animals learn about the external world in part through interoceptive signals1,2. For example, the nutrient content of food is first estimated in the mouth, in the form of flavour, and then it is measured again through slower signals from the gut. How these signals from the mouth and gut are integrated to drive learning is unclear. Here we identify a dopamine (DA) pathway that enables learning about the nutrient content of food. We show that DA neurons in the ventral tegmental area are necessary for associating nutrients with flavours, and that post-ingestive nutrients trigger DA release selectively in a small region of the anterior basolateral amygdala (BLA) but not in canonical DA targets in striatum. This nutrient-triggered DA release occurs preferentially in the left BLA in mice, and this same structure is preferentially activated by post-ingestive nutrients in humans. We identify the gut sensors that are responsible for nutrient-triggered DA release; show that they activate BLA-projecting DA neurons defined by expression of cholecystokinin; and demonstrate that stimulation of DA axon terminals in the anterior BLA drives flavour-nutrient learning but not other aspects of feeding behaviour. Two-photon imaging of neurons in the left anterior BLA reveals that they integrate gustatory and post-ingestive cues, and silencing these neurons prevents flavour-nutrient learning. These findings establish a neural basis for how animals learn about the nutrient content of their food.

items.title: An AI-native experimental laboratory for autonomous biomolecular operations.
items.abstract: Developing artificial intelligence (AI)-native experimental laboratories for autonomous scientific exploration with minimal human intervention represents a long-standing goal. Although autonomous experimental systems are emerging1-4, especially in chemical and materials science, they remain largely confined to domains with singular objectives, well-defined workflows and simple instrumentation. This limitation may reflect an 'add-on' architecture that uses AI as a task-specific tool rather than providing it with a global understanding of experiments, especially under engineering-oriented circumstances. Here we present AutoDNA, an AI-native autonomous biomolecular engineering laboratory targeting multi-objective experiments across diverse instruments. Through the co-design of models, experiments and instruments, AutoDNA realizes the co-evolution of AI and the automation system within an end-to-end multi-user framework. The system autonomously orchestrates over 20 types of instruments across more than 11,000 steps to execute core nucleic acid operations including synthesis, transcription, amplification and sequencing, while human intervention is limited to hardware maintenance tasks, such as reagent and labware replenishment. Across four representative applications, AutoDNA matched expert-optimized enzymatic DNA synthesis yields, accelerated concurrent protocol execution by 3.2-fold, completed an end-to-end DNA data storage cycle with exact recovery of the original digital content, and identified and validated a clinically detected KRAS G13D mutation. AutoDNA establishes a blueprint towards science-as-a-service, accelerating biological discovery and advancing various applications in synthetic biology and information storage.

items.title: A spatiotemporal cancer cell trajectory underlies glioblastoma heterogeneity.
items.abstract: Cancer cells show highly heterogeneous and plastic states in glioblastoma, an incurable brain tumour1-5. However, how these malignant states arise and whether they follow defined cellular trajectories across tumours is poorly understood. Here we generated a deep single-cell and spatial multi-omic atlas of human glioblastoma that pairs transcriptomic, epigenomic and genomic profiling of 12 tumours across many regions. We identify that glioblastoma heterogeneity is driven by spatially patterned transitions of cancer cells from developmental-like states towards those defined by a glial injury response and hypoxia. This cellular trajectory regionalizes tumours into distinct tissue microenvironments and manifests in a molecularly conserved manner across tumours as well as genetically distinct tumour subclones. Consistently, using a new deep-learning framework to map cancer cell states jointly with clones in situ, we show that tumour subclones are finely spatially intermixed through glioblastoma tissue microenvironments. We validate this cellular trajectory by using somatic mutation-based hierarchies in vivo and an experimental patient-derived organoid model ex vivo. Finally, we show that this cancer cell trajectory is intimately linked to myeloid heterogeneity and unfolds across regionalized myeloid signalling environments. Our findings define a stereotyped trajectory of cancer cells in glioblastoma and unify glioblastoma tumour heterogeneity into a tractable cellular and tissue framework.

items.title: Nectin-4 mediates rubella virus entry in airway and placental cells.
items.abstract: Rubella virus (RuV) causes rubella and, when acquired during pregnancy, congenital rubella syndrome1. Despite its clinical significance, the cellular entry mechanism of RuV remains poorly characterized, owing to limited identification of host receptors2, which hinders pathogenesis research and therapeutic development. Here, using proximity biotin labelling-based proteomics coupled with CRISPR-Cas9 validation, we identify nectin-4 as a functional RuV entry receptor. Ectopic expression of nectin-4 conferred susceptibility to RuV in non-permissive cells, whereas blocking or genetic ablation of nectin-4 reduced infection, results that demonstrate that nectin-4 is a major entry factor. Mechanistically, nectin-4 directly interacts with the RuV envelope glycoprotein heterodimer and facilitates receptor-mediated endocytosis following initial calcium-dependent viral attachment to cellular lipids. In polarized airway epithelial models, nectin-4 mediates basolateral entry of RuV and supports apical progeny release, a finding that provides a molecular mechanism for respiratory transmission. In placental models, nectin-4 is highly expressed on syncytiotrophoblasts and facilitates infection at the maternal-fetal interface, although additional nectin-4-independent pathways contribute to infection of other trophoblast populations. Together, these data establish nectin-4 as a key factor for respiratory transmission and early placental infection of RuV and highlight it as a promising therapeutic target for the prevention of rubella and related diseases.

items.title: Venousization enables angiogenesis in the absence of VEGFR signalling.
items.abstract: The vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) ligand and its main receptor VEGFR2 are considered to be essential for endothelial differentiation, proliferation, sprouting and survival1. Blood vessels cannot form in growing embryos or tissues when VEGF-VEGFR2 signalling is compromised in all cells2,3. The anti-VEGF antibody, which can block angiogenesis in cancer, wound healing or ischaemic diseases, is among the most widely used antibodies in the clinic. However, vascular resistance to anti-VEGF therapy has been reported4,5. Here we used iFlpMosaics and iSuRe-HadCre to induce and track genetic mosaics of endothelial cells (ECs) lacking VEGFR2 during the entire embryonic and postnatal development. These Vegfr2-knockout (Vegfr2KO) ECs adapted, proliferated normally and competed with wild-type cells over time, eventually forming a substantial portion of the vascular network in most organs. Vegfr2KO ECs could not sprout during the first wave of angiogenesis in most tissues, because this process is highly VEGF-dependent and favours growth and mobilization of wild-type ECs. However, owing to their inability to respond to VEGF, Vegfr2KO ECs became dominant in veins, which represented a long-term and continuous source of ECs for subsequent waves of VEGF-independent angiogenesis. Comparative single-cell RNA sequencing analysis of ECs with acute and long-term loss of VEGFR2 identified both common and organ-specific molecular mechanisms of adaptation and resistance to VEGF signalling loss. These included significant endothelial venousization and upregulation of ligands for VEGFR1 and VEGFR3. VEGFR1 only partially compensated for VEGFR2 loss in capillary ECs, whereas VEGFR3 compensated only in arterial ECs. Loss of the three VEGF receptors did not compromise venous growth. Notably, loss of the master regulator of venous development, NR2F2 (also known as COUP-TFII), significantly compromised expansion of Vegfr2KO ECs. This work has implications for our understanding of the role of VEGF receptors in angiogenesis and demonstrates venousization as a mechanism of adaptation and resistance to VEGF signalling loss during angiogenesis.

items.title: Microbiome-wide PheWAS links gut microbial SNVs to health and exposures.
items.abstract: Alterations in the microbial composition of the human gut have been associated with a wide range of chronic diseases1,2. Yet species-level composition alone can obscure extensive within-species genetic diversity and functional variation. This has driven a shift towards strain-resolved, genetic-level analysis of the microbiome, leveraging microbial genetic variation to identify disease-relevant genes and pathways3-6. Here we conducted a phenome-wide association study (PheWAS) analysing 12.8 million gut microbial single-nucleotide variants (SNVs) with 244 host health phenotypes and environmental exposures in 10,781 individuals from 6 independent cohorts. We identify 940 independent associations across 69 host factors, including age, sex and cardiovascular and metabolic parameters. Structural analyses identified host-phenotype-associated SNVs in functionally important regions of proteins, findings that inform mechanistic hypotheses about how microbial genetic changes relate to environmental and host physiological factors. For example, we identified an age-associated SNV in Faecalibacterium prausnitzii that affects an amino acid within the protein pocket that binds glutathione. To support future efforts, all study summary statistics are provided in an online catalogue ( https://fulab.web.rug.nl/SNV-MWAS/ ). Together, these results identify new biological connections between the human host and microbial genetic variants at base pair resolution and provide a resource for hypothesis generation that will aid future understanding of the strain-level functionality of the gut microbiota.

items.title: An open structure-guided RNA foundation model for generalizable prediction.
