items.abstract: RNA language models have achieved strong performance across diverse downstream tasks by leveraging large-scale sequence data. However, RNA function is fundamentally shaped by hierarchical structure, making structural information important for pre-training. Existing approaches often depend on noisy annotations or task-specific objectives that can limit generalizability. Here we present structRFM, a structure-guided RNA foundation model trained on 21 million RNA sequence-structure pairs by integrating base-pairing interactions into masked language modelling through a pair-matching operation. We also introduce MUSES, a multi-source ensemble of secondary structures designed to mitigate predictor bias, and a dynamic masking ratio that balances structure-guided and nucleotide-level masking. structRFM learns joint sequence and structure representations as sequence-level, nucleotide-level and pairwise features for broad downstream adaptation. It ranks highly in zero-shot homology classification and establishes new benchmarks for secondary-structure prediction. Its tertiary-structure adaptation, Zfold, consistently improves both three-dimensional predictions and their extracted secondary structures, with performance comparable to AlphaFold31 across CASP15-natural, CASP16 and RNA-Puzzles. structRFM also improves performance on function-prediction tasks and generalizes to newly released RNA families and long non-coding RNAs. Together, these results demonstrate the effectiveness of structure-guided pre-training and highlight multimodal RNA language models for robust structural and functional inference. The complete 21-million-pair dataset, model weights and source code are openly available to support multimodal RNA foundation-model development.

items.title: Tracing the spread of Celtic languages using ancient genomics.
items.abstract: Celtic languages are today restricted to Europe's Atlantic fringes but were widely spoken across the continent during the Iron Age1-3. How Celtic achieved this early distribution remains contested4, with alternative archaeological and linguistic models proposing different homelands and dispersal routes. Here we analyse genome-wide data from 4,587 ancient individuals, focusing on Bronze and Iron Age Europe, to test the extent to which these models fit reconstructed demographic histories. We identify three main processes shaping European population structure that are relevant to the Celtic dispersal. First, the arrival of Steppe-related ancestry with Bell Beaker-associated groups after around 4400 BP (calibrated years before present or 1950 CE) across the region in which Celtic and related languages were later spoken. Second, a movement from southwestern Europe into Britain during the Bronze Age (3800-3200 BP), consistent with scenarios in which Celtic formed along the Atlantic façade. Third, a westward expansion of ancestry related to Late Bronze Age Knovíz-Urnfield-associated populations from eastern central Europe (3200-2800 BP), affecting France, the British Isles, northeastern Iberia and Italy and later associated with Iron Age Hallstatt and La Tène contexts5-8. Although all three movements have parallels with proposed models, we argue that the final movement, from eastern central Europe, is most parsimonious for the spread of Celtic. Although human history does not necessarily follow a parsimonious trajectory9 and language shifts need not track genetic change, these results delimit the demographic scenarios that are plausible for the emergence of Celtic in prehistoric Europe.

items.title: Transcriptomic convergence and the female protective effect in autism.
items.abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is highly heritable, and mutations in hundreds of genes have been implicated as individually rare causes of ASD1-3. Understanding how disruptions to these functionally diverse genes lead to the core features of ASD remains a major challenge4. Moreover, ASD is three- to four-fold more common in male than in female individuals5, and female autistic people tend to carry more autosomal risk alleles for ASD compared with their male counterparts6,7; however, the biological basis of this 'female protective effect' (FPE) has remained unknown8,9. Here we show that individual perturbations of 18 ASD genes in human neural progenitor cells converge on shared effects on gene expression, including widespread downregulation of other ASD genes. De novo reconstruction of a gene regulatory network enabled identification of central transcriptional regulators that drive this transcriptomic convergence, including prominent ASD gene CHD8 and candidates including REST. Furthermore, X-linked transcription factor ZFX, which is expressed from both the active and the inactive X chromosomes in female individuals10, emerged as a key activator of many ASD genes: we propose that the higher ZFX expression level observed in the female brain can buffer damaging mutations in diverse ASD genes, contributing to the female protective effect. Together, these results show how key gene regulatory networks can become broadly and similarly dysregulated upon disruption of individual ASD genes and provide molecular insight into the female protective effect in ASD.

items.title: Hard X-ray attosecond metrology.
items.abstract: Sub-ångström spatial resolution combined with attosecond temporal resolution enables direct observation of electron motion in matter1. Attosecond hard X-ray pulses generated at X-ray free-electron laser sources provide the requisite spatiotemporal sensitivity, yet their application has been limited by the absence of precise pulse metrology and control. Here, building on a broadband X-ray split-delay line, we establish metrology of attosecond hard X-ray pulses. Field-correlation measurements provide the first time-domain characterization of the pulse coherence time and demonstrate attosecond synchronization between the generated pulse pairs. By exploiting non-sequential two-photon absorption as a nonlinear probe, intensity autocorrelation quantifies the average pulse duration directly in the time domain to be 170 as. The demonstrated experimental tools and techniques enable systematic attosecond time-resolved experiments, including X-ray pump-X-ray probe spectroscopy and diffraction, and open a pathway to probing electronic phenomena with unprecedented spatial-temporal resolution.

items.title: Conjugation-regulated self-assembled molecules for tandem solar cells.
items.abstract: Perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells on rough textured substrates are at present limited by a critical trade-off in self-assembled monolayer (SAM) design because increasing molecular conjugation enhances conductivity but often leads to unfavourable aggregation that impairs conformal coverage1,2. Here we overcome this challenge using a rationally engineered molecular spatial conjugation that incorporates tailored intramolecular distortion to suppress excess π-π stacking without sacrificing charge-transport efficiency. This steric regulation facilitates the formation of a highly ordered, conformal SAM across rough pyramidal textures. By reconciling molecular packing with interfacial coverage, the tailored interface provides optimized energy-level alignment for ultrafast charge extraction, enables improved defect passivation through adaptive conformational adjustment and acts as a robust template for high-quality perovskite film growth. Making use of this interface, the optimized tandem device achieves a notable fill factor (FF) of 85%, yielding a certified stabilized power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 35.1%. Furthermore, the device demonstrates outstanding stability, retaining more than 94% of its initial performance after 1,500 h of ageing under the ISOS-L-1 protocol. Our findings provide a clear molecular engineering route to reconcile conductivity and film uniformity while maximizing the performance of tandem photovoltaics on textured silicon substrates.

items.title: Cancer-selective gene circuits via intrinsic ribosomal frameshifting.
items.abstract: Ribosomal frameshifting, an uncommon translational recoding event, is best known for its regulatory roles in viral gene expression1,2, whereas its physiological relevance in mammals remains poorly understood. Here we show that specific codon pairs trigger efficient -1 frameshifting preferentially in cancer cells. Mechanistically, this recoding arises from ribosomal pausing associated with tRNA and amino acid availability, and is amplified by impaired ribosome quality control and sustained phosphorylation of ribosomal protein S6. We found that this codon-pair-specific frameshifting represents an intrinsic state of translational dysregulation, which is prevalent across cancer cells and reshapes protein synthesis. Taking advantage of this frameshifting-permissive state in cancer cells, we engineered a frameshifting-activated synthetic therapeutic circuit (FAST) that conditionally expresses the pyroptotic effector gasdermin D. FAST is activated across diverse cancer cell types, inducing potent and selective pyroptosis, while sparing normal tissues from detectable toxicity. As a proof of concept, systemic AAV9-mediated delivery of FAST in mouse models of colorectal and pancreatic cancer elicited pronounced tumour regression, robust immune activation and synergistic effects with immune checkpoint blockade. Collectively, these findings reveal codon-pair-dependent ribosomal frameshifting as a feature of translational dysregulation in cancer cells and establish translation-coupled gene circuits as a strategy for cancer-selective therapy.

items.title: Perioperative respiratory adverse events in children undergoing adenotonsillectomy with laryngeal mask airway versus endotracheal tube ventilation: multicentre, randomised controlled trial.

sections.objective: To assess the effect of ventilation with a laryngeal mask airway (LMA) compared with endotracheal tube (ETT) on perioperative respiratory adverse events (PRAEs) in children undergoing adenotonsillectomy.
sections.methods: Multicentre, randomised, parallel group trial. 400 children aged ≥2 years and <7 years who were scheduled for adenotonsillectomy under general anaesthesia. Participants were randomised 1:1 to receive ventilation with a laryngeal mask airway (n=200) or an endotracheal tube (n=200) during adenotonsillectomy.
sections.results: 400 children (mean age 4.7 (standard deviation 1.0) years; 155 (38.7%) girls) were enrolled between 24 May 2023 and 4 April 2024, with last follow-up on 4 May 2024. LMA was converted to ETT in three participants. Overall, 22.5% (45/200) participants in the LMA group experienced PRAEs versus 57.5% (115/200) in the ETT group (absolute risk difference -35.0 percentage points, 95% confidence interval -43.5 to -25.7; P<0.001). The LMA group had fewer PRAEs in both the intraoperative (9.0% (18/200) v 17.5% (35/200); -8.5, -15.2 to -1.8; P=0.01) and the postoperative period (16.5% (33/200) v 49.5% (99/200); -33.0, -41.2 to -24.0; P<0.001). The LMA group also had a lower proportion of participants with laryngospasm (0.0% v 3.0%; P=0.03), desaturation (15.0% v 28.0%; P=0.002), airway obstruction (3.5% v 12.5%; P<0.001), and severe cough (10.5% v 42.0%; P<0.001). Neither group experienced serious adverse events.
sections.conclusion: Ventilation with an LMA by experienced anaesthesiologists resulted in fewer perioperative respiratory adverse events than ventilation with an ETT in children undergoing adenotonsillectomy.
sections.other: Four tertiary hospitals in China, 2023-24. The primary outcome was the proportion of participants who developed any perioperative respiratory adverse event (PRAE): laryngospasm, bronchospasm, desaturation, airway obstruction, severe cough, or stridor in the intention-to-treat population.

items.title: Interventions for adhesive capsulitis: systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.

sections.objective: To compare the benefits and harms of therapeutic interventions for adhesive capsulitis.
sections.methods: Systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.
sections.results: A total of 189 randomised controlled trials involving 12 988 participants and 59 interventions were included. Most trials contributing to principal outcomes were at high risk of bias (71% for pain, 72% for function, and 71% for range of motion). At short term follow-up, moderate certainty evidence suggested that extracorporeal shockwave therapy probably reduced pain compared with usual care (mean difference -1.97 on a 0-10 scale, 95% confidence interval (CI) -2.97 to -0.97). Low certainty evidence suggested that extracorporeal shockwave therapy may improve function (mean difference -11.42 on a 0-100 scale, 95% CI -16.68 to -6.15), although direct and indirect estimates were limited by important incoherence. For short term range of motion, moderate certainty evidence suggested that manipulation under anaesthesia combined with intra-articular steroid injections probably improved flexion (mean difference 33.29°, 95% CI 11.19° to 55.39°), as did manipulation under anaesthesia alone (26.16°, 8.19° to 44.13°). Low certainty evidence suggested that extracorporeal shockwave therapy may improve flexion (22.42°, 12.99° to 31.84°) and abduction (18.62°, 8.09° to 29.14°), but both comparisons were limited by important incoherence. At mid-term follow-up, evidence for possible improvements in function with extracorporeal shockwave therapy and flexion with passive mobilisation was of low certainty, while evidence for pain reduction with extracorporeal shockwave therapy was of very low certainty. Most other comparative estimates were supported by low or very low certainty evidence. Comparative safety remained highly uncertain because adverse events were incompletely and inconsistently reported; the absence of reported adverse events should not be interpreted as evidence of absence of harm.
sections.conclusion: Moderate certainty evidence suggests short term pain reduction with extracorporeal shockwave therapy and improved short term flexion with manipulation under anaesthesia, with or without intra-articular steroid injections. Most other treatment effects remain uncertain because of low certainty and incoherence, and comparative safety and mid-term effects are poorly established. The available evidence is mainly short term and outcome specific. Longer term comparative effectiveness, overall benefits and harms, and applicability beyond predominantly primary adhesive capsulitis remain uncertain.
sections.other: Medline, Cochrane Library, Embase, Web of Science, and Scopus were searched from inception to 1 May 2025, with an update in November 2025. Randomised controlled trials enrolling adults with adhesive capsulitis, comparing active treatment with another intervention, placebo, or usual care. Pain, function, range of motion, and adverse events. PROSPERO CRD420251070468.

items.title: Carbon radical generation by irreversible metal-to-ligand charge transfer.
items.abstract: Metal-to-ligand charge transfer (MLCT) is a fundamental photoinduced process that underpins a broad range of energy- or electron-transfer events1,2. In the absence of productive substrate engagement, the MLCT excited state typically relaxes to the ground state via photophysical deactivation, reflecting its largely reversible character3,4. Here we report a class of isolable copper-heteroaryl sulfone complexes that, upon visible light irradiation, undergo an irreversible MLCT-driven fragmentation through C-S bond cleavage within the coordinated sulfone ligand, generating carbon-centered radicals. Spectroscopic and computational studies support the formation of MLCT-derived excited states and a low-barrier pathway for C-S bond cleavage. This reactivity is largely independent of the reduction potentials of the corresponding free sulfones, enabling the generation of fluoroalkyl and non-fluorinated tertiary, secondary, and primary (even methyl) alkyl radicals. We demonstrate the utility of this platform in copper-catalyzed C-H fluoroalkylation of arenes and terminal alkynes. Leveraging these MLCT-generated trifluoromethyl radicals to initiate halogen-atom transfer (XAT) from perfluorocyclobutyl iodide (I-FCB), we also achieve radical perfluorocyclobutylation-iodination of alkenes, addressing a longstanding challenge in the incorporation of perfluorocyclobutyl motifs.

items.title: Retinoblastoma.
items.abstract: Retinoblastoma, the most common primary intraocular malignancy of childhood, represents a substantial global health equity concern, exemplifying profound disparities in global burden and outcome despite being a largely curable cancer. Retinoblastoma is thought to arise from cone photoreceptor precursor cells of the developing retina, mainly driven by biallelic inactivation of the RB1 tumour suppressor gene. Fewer than 2% of cases have no detectable RB1 pathogenic variant; approximately half of these cases instead show high-level amplification of the MYCN oncogene. Diagnosis and monitoring currently rely on clinical examination and multimodal imaging. Emerging molecular diagnostic approaches such as aqueous humour liquid biopsy hold promise for minimally invasive tumour characterisation and real-time disease monitoring. Management has shifted towards eye-preserving strategies, with intra-arterial, intravitreal, and intracameral chemotherapy showing efficacy and safety. The global burden and mortality of retinoblastoma remains highest in regions with a low sociodemographic index, highlighting the need for continued interdisciplinary, equity-focused efforts to ensure timely diagnosis and accessible, high-quality care worldwide. This Seminar reviews the advances in retinoblastoma biology, diagnosis, treatment, survivorship, and global efforts to reduce inequities.

items.title: Preparing for responsive management versus renal dialysis in older people living with kidney failure and frailty or multimorbidity in the UK (Prepare for Kidney Care): a two-arm, superiority, parallel-group, open-label, pragmatic, phase 3, individually randomised controlled trial.

sections.objective: The comparative effectiveness of conservative kidney management and dialysis in older people (aged ≥80 years regardless of frailty and comorbidity or aged 65-79 years if frailty or multimorbidity are present) living with kidney failure is unknown. We aimed to assess the relative effectiveness of preparing for responsive management-a protocolised version of conservative kidney management-and preparing for renal dialysis.
sections.methods: Prepare for Kidney Care was a two-arm, superiority, parallel-group, open-label, pragmatic, phase 3, individually randomised controlled trial conducted in 31 kidney centres in England, Wales, Scotland, and Northern Ireland. Eligible patients had an estimated glomerular filtration rate below 15 mL/min per 1·73 m2, confirmed by at least one additional reading in the 12 months preceding consent that was not due to acute kidney injury, and were either aged 80 years or older, or aged 65-79 years with a WHO performance status of at least 3 or a Davies comorbidity score of at least 2. Eligible participants were randomly assigned (1:1) to prepare for responsive management-a patient-centred approach focused on slowing disease progression, active symptom management, and preserving quality of life without the use of dialysis or kidney transplantation-or to prepare for renal dialysis. Randomisation was stratified by centre and minimised by age; a centralised system ensured allocation concealment until randomisation had taken place. The primary outcome was the mean difference in quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs), combining length and health-related quality of life from the patient-reported EQ-5D-5L scale, including all follow-up from randomisation to Aug 31, 2025. The primary outcome was analysed by intention to treat in the full analysis set, which included all randomly assigned participants, with missing EQ-5D-5L values for living participants imputed. Harms (hospital admissions and dialysis access complications) and adverse events (deaths and hospital admissions, by cause) were assessed in the full analysis set. The trial was registered with ISRCTN, 17133653 (completed).
sections.results: From July 1, 2017, to Aug 31, 2024, 6120 patients were screened across 31 kidney centres in the UK, 445 (7%) of whom were eligible and agreed to be randomly assigned. 228 (51%) of 445 participants were randomly assigned to prepare for responsive management and 217 (49%) of 445 participants were randomly assigned to prepare for renal dialysis. Median age was 82 years (IQR 80 to 86) and 137 (31%) of 445 participants were female. After a mean follow-up duration of 4·5 years (SD 2·1), mean QALYs were 1·354 (95% CI 1·201 to 1·508) in the prepare for responsive management group and 1·472 (1·288 to 1·655) in the prepare for renal dialysis group (adjusted mean difference -0·147 [95% CI -0·350 to 0·056] p=0·16). Specific harms outcomes were not prespecified, but hospital admission rates were similar in the two groups and dialysis access complications were significantly lower in the prepare for responsive management group (adjusted incident rate ratio 0·41 [95% CI 0·19 to 0·88]), based on 74 events in 36 participants across both groups. There were 667 serious adverse events in the prepare for responsive management group (157 [69%] of 228 participants died, with 510 hospital admissions) and 578 in the prepare for renal dialysis group (136 [63%] of 217 participants died, with 442 hospital admissions). None of these serious adverse events met the criteria for expedited reporting.
sections.conclusion: Among older people living with kidney failure and frailty or multimorbidity, we found no evidence that either preparing for responsive management or preparing for renal dialysis was superior in terms of QALYs over a mean follow-up duration of 4·5 years. This trial provides novel comparative information for clinical decision making.

items.title: CRISPR mutagenesis of the MYC locus reveals a druggable ultraconserved RNA element.
items.abstract: Noncoding sequences comprise most of the human genome; however, their functional significance remains largely elusive. Using CRISPR tiling mutagenesis with near-PAMless, high-fidelity SpRY-Cas9, we mapped the fitness landscape of an entire human gene, the 10-kb MYC locus, at base-pair resolution. This unbiased interrogation revealed that 67% of functionally essential base pairs are noncoding. Essential noncoding base pairs are under strong constraint in the human population but show limited evolutionary conservation across species. Within this landscape, we identified an ultraconserved noncoding RNA element in the 3' untranslated region (UTR) that promotes perinuclear localization of MYC mRNA and nuclear localization of MYC protein through interaction with hnRNP L. Steric-blocking antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs) targeting this element selectively eliminate diverse MYC-dependent cancer cells and inhibit growth of patient-derived tumor organoids. Together, these findings establish noncoding sequences as major carriers of functional genetic information and identify a therapeutically actionable RNA element whose targeting disrupts MYC-driven cancer.

items.title: The deep Earth origin of the Great Unconformity.
items.abstract: The Great Unconformity marks a globally extensive erosive surface linked to climatic shifts1 and environmental transitions2 that preceded the Cambrian explosion of life. The processes proposed to explain the formation of the Great Unconformity include glacial erosion during the Snowball Earth1,3,4, rifting and plume activity5-7, sea-level fall8 and mantle-driven dynamic topography6,9-11. However, the dynamics of these processes have not been tested. Here we show that continental-scale uplift and subsidence associated with long-wavelength dynamic topography12 due to mantle convection drove the formation and preservation of the Great Unconformity. Our models predict prolonged continental-scale Neoproterozoic uplift and long-term Phanerozoic subsidence for Laurentia, Baltica and North China. This vertical motion scenario is ideal for the formation and preservation of the Great Unconformity, which is a first-order surface expression of deep Earth processes. The predicted prolonged continental uplift throughout Cryogenian times would have resulted in marked erosion due to the action of glaciers13. The large area of Laurentia and limited deformation at its margins explain why the Great Unconformity is best preserved and documented there. Our models predict cycles of dynamic topography that are broadly reflected in preserved sediment volume across continents1,14, and open new avenues for understanding the environments of Cambrian animal diversification.

items.title: Accelerating commercialization and deployment of indoor photovoltaics.
items.abstract: The growing reliance on distributed electronics, such as Internet of Things (IoT) nodes, smart-home devices and portable consumer products, has intensified demand for indoor energy-harvesting technologies that reduce battery replacement and servicing. Consequently, indoor photovoltaics (PVs) have advanced rapidly; however, translating state-of-the-art cells into deployable products requires design principles that reflect real indoor conditions. Here recent progress in perovskite (bulk and quantum dot), organic, amorphous-silicon, III-V and dye-sensitized PVs is examined to identify bottlenecks that arise under low-light conditions and during scale-up. This Review highlights how low-light operation favours wide-bandgap absorbers and reduced non-radiative voltage losses while reshaping module design: lower series-resistance (RS) penalties permit wider subcells and fewer interconnections, increasing geometric fill factor, whereas shunt and leakage pathways consume more of the weak photocurrent. Measurement practices for credible cross-technology benchmarking are discussed, emphasizing the transparent reporting of spectra, illuminance/irradiance, stabilization and uncertainty. Finally, the relationship between device performance and manufacturability and product integration is considered, including power-management requirements and chemical/regulatory constraints (for example, restricted substances and end-of-life handling). These guidelines provide a practical framework for evaluating indoor PVs on the basis of delivered and retained power and for accelerating the transition from laboratory-scale demonstrations to reliable, visually adaptable products for the built environment.

items.title: Imaging exoplanets below the telescope stability limit.
items.abstract: Exoplanet imaging is the main method for detailed characterization of planets orbiting beyond 1 AU (ref. 1) but it requires suppressing the bright glare of the star to see the faint planet light. As well as sophisticated instrumentation2,3, effective image processing is necessary for starlight suppression, which continues to be a substantial limitation4. Standard algorithms use reference images for starlight modelling and thus they are limited by inevitable telescope instabilities that change from reference to science observation5,6. Addressing this challenge will increase the number of planets amenable to direct imaging and will be a notable step towards imaging exo-Earths with future observatories7. Here we present a new physics-based method for starlight subtraction. Our method combines a multistep optimization with a flexible physical model to produce a starlight model, allowing modelling and compensation of instrument instabilities. We use automatic differentiation (autodiff)8 to optimize millions of model parameters. We demonstrate our method on observations from the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) Near-InfraRed Camera (NIRCam)9-11 coronagraph instrument. We achieve sensitivity 2-15 times superior to standard techniques, including the first detection of 51 Eridani b (ref. 12) at 4.3 μm. This is the first time, to our knowledge, that such an approach has demonstrated substantially improved sensitivity on real, on-sky coronagraphic imaging. Our framework can be extended to other current and future ground-based and space-based observatories, including the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope and the Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO), potentially relaxing the unprecedented stability requirements needed to make these a success.

items.title: Multimodal X-ray imaging reveals hierarchical fibre mechanics.
items.abstract: Fibrous materials, ranging from connective tissues1-4 to engineered composites5-8, are vital to many biological and man-made systems, optimized to withstand complex in operando or in vivo loading. The load-bearing capacity of intervertebral discs (IVDs) of the spine depends on a hierarchical extracellular matrix, where plywood-like lamellae of collagen fibres in the annulus fibrosus contain nanometre-scale fibrils built from staggered triple-helical monomers4,9,10. How intact IVDs couple fibril-scale mechanics to fibre-scale organization under load remains unresolved. Here we introduce TomoSAXS, a full-field 3D small-angle X-ray scattering tomography that maps fibril-to-fibre mechanics across an intact tissue. We show that intrafibrillar molecular pre-strain (D-period stagger) is lamellar textured and tightly correlated with microscale fibre strain. Pre-strain is inversely related to fibril strain and its variability, consistent with load-sharing through molecular unwinding. Radial strain bridges and high-curvature zones at the annulus fibrosus-nucleus pulposus interfaces emerge as critical regulators of local mechanics. These findings reveal concerted fibril-fibre interactions that sustain mechanical equilibrium in the IVD, preserving elasticity and shape. More broadly, TomoSAXS establishes a platform to visualize nanoscale-to-microscale matrix mechanics across biological and synthetic fibrous materials, with applications in ageing and disease, therapeutic evaluation and the design of bio-based and bio-inspired materials.

items.title: Alternate eye patching improves long-term alignment stability after surgery for intermittent exotropia: a randomised controlled trial.

sections.objective: Postoperative exodrift remains a major challenge following surgical correction of intermittent exotropia (IXT), and evidence supporting adjunctive strategies to improve long-term alignment is limited. This study evaluated the effect of alternate eye patching on 12-month postoperative alignment stability after successful surgical correction in divergence excess IXT.
sections.results: At 12 months, alignment stability was significantly higher in Group A compared with Group B (83.3% vs 60.0%, p = 0.045). Significant exodrift occurred less frequently in Group A (16.7% vs 40.0%, p = 0.045). Mean postoperative deviation was lower in Group A at all follow-up visits (p < 0.05). No patients in Group A required reoperation compared with 10% in Group B, although this difference was not statistically significant (p = 0.112).
sections.conclusion: Alternate eye patching may improve postoperative alignment stability and reduce postoperative exodrift for divergence excess intermittent exotropia. Early postoperative modulation of binocular visual balance may contribute to improved long-term alignment outcomes.
sections.other: This randomised clinical trial was conducted at an institutional tertiary care centre and included 60 children (3-12 years) undergoing bilateral lateral rectus recession who were randomised only after confirmation of early postoperative alignment ( ≤ 10 prism dioptres [PD]), creating a post-success randomised design to evaluate the effect of alternate eye patching on alignment maintenance. Participants were assigned to alternate eye patching (Group A) or standard postoperative care (Group B). Patching was prescribed for 1 h daily per eye for 3 months. Patients were followed for 12 months. The primary outcome was alignment stability ( ≤ 10 PD). Secondary outcomes included exodrift ( > 10 PD), mean deviation, and reoperation rate. Pan African Clinical Trial Registry (PACTR202505751499770), registered on May 14, 2025. https://pactr.samrc.ac.za/.

items.title: Perioperative Outcomes After Open Versus Endovascular Revascularization for Tissue-Loss Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia in Patients Aged 80 Years or Older: An NSQIP Analysis.

sections.objective: We compared 30-day outcomes of open bypass versus endovascular intervention in patients aged ≥80 years with tissue-loss chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI), in whom trial evidence from younger populations may not apply.
sections.methods: In this retrospective cohort study, patients undergoing infrainguinal revascularization for tissue-loss CLTI in the National Surgical Quality Improvement Program vascular-targeted modules (2014-2024) were classified as open bypass with single-segment saphenous vein (OPEN-GSV) or alternative conduit (OPEN-Other), or endovascular intervention (ENDO). Doubly-robust inverse-probability weighting with regression adjustment estimated 30-day risks of the co-primary outcomes, major adverse limb events (MALE) and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), with bootstrap 95% confidence intervals (CIs).
sections.results: The cohort comprised 4,415 patients (2,573 ENDO; 1,124 OPEN-GSV; 718 OPEN-Other). Adjusted MACE risk was 2.9% after ENDO versus 6.5% after OPEN-GSV (risk ratio [RR] 0.44, 95% CI 0.29-0.61) and 6.0% after OPEN-Other (RR 0.48, 0.33-0.79). MALE did not differ significantly (RR 0.85 and 0.86), with CIs spanning clinically important differences in both directions. Serious complication, any complication, and non-home discharge were lower after ENDO (RR 0.41-0.56); major amputation did not differ. Mortality was lower after ENDO than OPEN-GSV (4.7% vs 6.9%; RR 0.68) but not OPEN-Other (RR 0.87).
sections.conclusion: In this population, endovascular intervention was associated with substantially lower 30-day cardiovascular events and systemic morbidity than open bypass, with no significant difference - though not established equivalence - in early limb outcomes. These findings support weighing perioperative physiologic risk in individualized treatment selection; data beyond 30 days are needed to address durability and limb salvage.

items.title: A National Consultant Information Programme Data Analysis of Deep Venous Interventions in England.

sections.objective: The aim of this study was to characterise contemporary deep venous interventions (DVIs) performed within the English National Health Service (NHS), describing procedural mix, patient heterogeneity, anatomic distribution, and short and midterm outcomes.
sections.methods: National data on DVIs performed between 1 June 2020 and 31 May 2023 were extracted from the National Consultant Information Programme. Percutaneous transluminal venous procedures (PTVs) and venous thrombolysis were identified using pre-defined procedural and diagnostic code hierarchies. All cases underwent structured patient level validation to ensure concordance between indication, treated venous anatomy, and procedural intent. The primary outcomes were ninety day and one year mortality. Secondary outcomes included procedural volume variation. Re-interventions were recorded descriptively.
sections.results: In total, 2 339 DVIs were performed, of which 1 617 PTVs and 604 venous thrombolysis procedures were validated. Patient cohorts were heterogeneous, most commonly chronic kidney disease (CKD) (41.8%), chronic venous insufficiency (CVI) (16.0%), and venous compression syndromes (14.0%). Anatomic distribution differed markedly by indication: CKD procedures predominantly involved upper limb and central veins, whereas CVI and venous compression were overwhelmingly confined to the lower limbs and iliocaval system. Among 650 patients with primary lower limb venous disease (CVI, venous thrombosis, or venous compression), 76.3% underwent iliac or inferior vena cava interventions. Overall mortality varied substantially by indication, being highest in patients with malignant neoplasms and lowest in primary lower limb venous disease. Thrombolysis was most frequently performed for lower extremity venous thrombosis and was associated with low short and midterm mortality in this group.
sections.conclusion: This service level analysis of DVIs in England demonstrates distinct clinical populations with marked differences in anatomy, indication, and outcomes that vary substantially by indication and comorbidity. Mortality was lowest in elective primary lower limb venous disease and highest in patients with advanced systemic illness such as malignancy and renal disease. Future work should focus on indication specific venous registries and risk adjusted outcomes to aid benchmarking, service level organisation, and patient care.

items.title: Propensity Score Matched Analysis of Outcomes of Conservative and Invasive Management of Patients with Chronic Limb Threatening Ischaemia: The PROCLION Study.

sections.objective: Current guidelines recommend revascularisation for patients with chronic limb threatening ischaemia (CLTI). However, revascularisation may be burdensome in these frail patients. The objective of this study was to compare the clinical and patient reported outcomes in patients with CLTI treated with conservative best supportive care versus primary invasive endovascular and/or surgical revascularisation.
sections.methods: This was a multicentre prospective cohort study in the Netherlands. Propensity score matching was used to create similar groups based on known factors influencing the odds of undergoing revascularisation. Twelve month amputation free survival (AFS), major amputation rates, mortality, and patient reported outcomes after primary conservative treatment were compared with primary invasive treatment (intention to treat; ITT). Outcomes after invasive treatment at any time were compared with definitive conservative treatment (per protocol; PP).
sections.results: A total of 365 patients with CLTI were included in 18 centres. In the ITT analysis, patients were matched 1 : 1, resulting in two groups of 121 patients. Twelve month AFS was 73.0% for patients after conservative treatment and 72.1% after invasive treatment (risk difference [RD] -0.9%, 95% confidence interval [CI] -10.2 - 8.4%). There were no significant differences in amputation and mortality rates. In the PP analysis, patients were matched 1 : 2, with 51 in the conservative group and 102 in the invasive group. Again, no significant differences were found for AFS, amputation rate, and mortality. Patient reported outcomes improved after 1 year in both groups (VascuQoL: ITT conservative group from 14 to 16.2, and invasive group from 13.8 to 16.5), but no significant differences were found in ITT or PP comparisons.
sections.conclusion: The current study suggests that the 12 month clinical outcomes of primary conservative and invasive treatment for CLTI are similar. Conservative management may therefore be a viable first choice treatment option in selected patients with CLTI.

items.title: Giving or Taking? Ethical Guidance for Hospital Administrators Involved in Organ Procurement.
items.abstract: Organ procurement from unrepresented decedents is legal in the United States, and some states even designate "the hospital administrator" as having the right to authorize donation. However, there is little guidance for an administrator to consult in their effort to make a socially responsible decision. In this case study, we review the arguments in favor of deferring, deciding against, or deciding in favor of authorization. We contend that that there are three reasons involving uncertainty, inequity, and the risk of mistrust that should give an administrator pause in endorsing organ procurement. We ultimately recommend that organ recovery should not be authorized unless there is (1) strong evidence that a diligent search for surrogates has been undertaken, establishing a reasonable amount of certainty that none are forthcoming, and (2) some evidence suggesting that the decedent would favor organ donation.

items.title: "Bold and necessary experiments:" The redelegation of authority and responsibility to nurses at the origins of cardiac intensive care.
items.abstract: Coronary Care Units (CCUs) were at the forefront of the development of intensive care in the 1960s and 1970s. The development of CCUs, and intensive care more broadly, was enabled by the interplay of expanding medical technology and the evolving role of nurses vis-à-vis physicians. This paper examines the history the CCU at New York Hospital, the teaching hospital of Cornell University School of Medicine and School of Nursing, with a particular focus on role of nurses in the unit's success. Drawing from historical archives of New York Hospital and the Cornell University School of Nursing, this paper argues that that nurses were co-creators, alongside physicians, of the NYH CCU, and demonstrates how nurses drew from the NYH CCU experience to expand critical care services at the local and national level, including by advocating for the creation of the NYH medical intensive care unit (MICU), leading a CCU nurse training program to expand regional CCU capability, and contributing expertise to a federally-sponsored national conference on CCUs. A close reading of this history offers lessons and insights as intensive care medicine moves into an uncertain future, chief among them that work of caring for critically ill patients requires the thoughtful integration of new technologies with hands on care.

items.title: Short-term Risk of Inflammatory Eye Reactions Following Bisphosphonate Use: A nationwide case-case-time-control study.

sections.objective: To evaluate short-term associations between bisphosphonate exposure and uveitis, scleritis, and cystoid macular edema (CME).
sections.methods: Nationwide case-case-time-control (CCTC) study. Patients with incident uveitis, scleritis, or CME identified from Taiwan's national health claims data (2011-2021), with matched future cases serving as controls to adjust for temporal exposure trends. Bisphosphonate exposure during the 30-day hazard window immediately preceding each event was compared with exposure during an earlier 30-day reference window, separated by a 90-day washout period. Each case was matched to a future case to account for temporal trends in bisphosphonate use. Analyses were stratified by administration route and individual agent. Sensitivity analyses varied window lengths, washout periods, and lag structures. Denosumab and teriparatide served as negative-control exposures.
sections.results: We identified 269,545 incident uveitis cases, 132,585 scleritis cases, and 115,914 CME cases; over 96% were matched to a future case and included in CCTC analyses. After accounting for exposure trends, any bisphosphonate use was associated with an increased short-term risk of uveitis (OR, 1.24; 95% CI, 1.00-1.56), driven primarily by anterior uveitis (OR 1.43; 95% CI, 1.10-1.86). In analyses stratified by administration route and individual agent, intravenous bisphosphonates (OR, 1.78; 95% CI, 1.22-2.61), particularly zoledronic acid (OR, 2.82; 95% CI, 1.70-4.67), were associated with increased uveitis risk. Oral bisphosphonates were not associated with uveitis (OR, 0.99; 95% CI, 0.74-1.33). No clear associations were observed for scleritis or CME. Findings were consistent across subgroup and sensitivity analyses, and associations for negative-control exposures were null.
sections.conclusion: Short-term associations between bisphosphonate use and ocular inflammatory events varied by administration route and outcome. Increased uveitis risk was concentrated among intravenous formulations, particularly zoledronic acid, whereas no clear associations were found for scleritis or CME. These findings may inform monitoring for ocular symptoms among patients receiving intravenous bisphosphonates.
sections.other: Incident uveitis, scleritis, and CME, with associations quantified using CCTC odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs).

items.title: Automated perimetry in pediatric neuro-ophthalmic conditions: virtual reality-based vs. standard tabletop platforms.

sections.objective: The game-based virtual reality field (VRF) testing algorithm has shown promise in pediatric neuro-ophthalmic patients, but the faster Humphrey visual field (HVF) equivalent algorithm has not been studied in this population. The purpose of this study was to compare testing outcomes between tabletop HVF and VRF (HVF-equivalent algorithm) in a pediatric neuro-ophthalmic population.
sections.methods: Prospective comparison of diagnostic perimetry testing modalities. Children (<18 years of age) with a known or suspected neuro-ophthalmic condition. Consecutive pediatric patients presenting to one neuro-ophthalmic clinic between January 2025 and April 2026 had clinically indicated visual field testing first with tabletop HVF testing (24-2, Size III, SITA Fast) and then VRF in the HVF-equivalent algorithm (24-2, Size III, AVA Fast). Global parameters, field defect agreement via masked grading, and point-by-point agreement (including total deviation [TD] and pattern deviation [PD] plots) between modalities were evaluated. HVFs with false-negative/false-positive rates >35% or fixation losses >50% were considered unreliable, applying less stringent reliability criteria for this pediatric population.
sections.results: One hundred fourteen patients (210 eyes; mean age 11.4 ± 3.6 years) were enrolled. Ninety-two children (168 eyes) completed both HVF and VRF testing, including 128 reliable and 40 unreliable HVF examinations. Regional defect agreement between HVF and VRF was 65.9% on average, while point-by-point agreement rates for TD and PD plots were 76.6% and 83.7%, respectively. Moderate positive associations were observed between HVF and VRF for mean deviation (R2M = .398, P < .001) and pattern standard deviation (R2M = .576, P < .001). VRF was significantly faster than HVF (2.1 ± 0.17 minutes vs 4.4 ± 1.2 minutes; P < .001) and most queried patients (51/53; 96.2%) preferred VRF to HVF testing.
sections.conclusion: VRF (HVF-equivalent algorithm) testing showed moderate to good concordance with tabletop HVF testing in pediatric neuro-ophthalmic patients, with shorter testing duration and high patient preference, supporting its potential clinical value.
sections.other: Agreement rate between HVF and VRF in both defect detection by region (quadrants, and center) and individual plot points (<0.5% probability defect threshold). Comparisons across patient characteristics, perimetry results, and testing modality (HVF vs. VRF).

items.title: P2RX7 drives inflammatory microglia and pathogenic extracellular vesicle secretion in tauopathy.
items.abstract: P2X purinoreceptor 7 (P2RX7), an ATP-gated ion channel, contributes to Alzheimer's disease (AD) progression, but its molecular mechanisms remain unclear. Here, we show that genetic disruption of P2rx7 mitigates brain atrophy, tau accumulation, and cognitive impairment in PS19 mice. Microglia-specific, but not astrocyte-specific, deletion of P2rx7 suppresses tau propagation. Single-cell RNA sequencing identifies a previously unrecognized first-responding microglial state (FRM) with prominent P2rx7 expression. P2RX7 promotes the transition from FRM to an inflammatory microglial state enriched in extracellular vesicle (EV) biogenesis. P2RX7 increases EV loading of tau and of mitochondrial proteins and DNA, which activate cytosolic DNA sensing and interferon signaling in recipient microglia. Tau-containing microglial EVs disrupt neuronal endolysosomal integrity and facilitate endosomal tau escape and phosphorylation. Thus, P2RX7 regulates the FRM branch point, driving inflammatory microglial transition and EV-mediated spread of tau and toxic mitochondrial molecules and highlighting the P2RX7-EV axis as a therapeutic target in AD.

items.title: Rapid, voxel-based 3D printing with yield-stress fluid inks.
items.abstract: Despite decades of progress, 3D printing still presents trade-offs in what materials can be printed and at what resolutions, speeds, and part volumes. We introduce direct ink additive lithography, or DIAL, to alleviate these trade-offs when printing with yield-stress, complex fluid inks used to print functional materials. DIAL combines translational photopatterning with ink sheet deposition for rapid, voxel-based 3D printing. Using model DIAL inks with kilopascal-scale yield stresses, we evaluate how ink rheology influences printing and compare DIAL against digital light processing (DLP) and direct ink writing (DIW). Since DIAL enables fast, high-throughput, support-free, and large-area printing, we showcase its broad potential for producing functional materials by printing multiscale architected, multimaterial, structural electrolyte, and hydrogel structures that are difficult if not impossible to 3D print today.

items.title: Single-neuron encoding of rapidly learned visual information reshapes human perception.
items.abstract: Humans can swiftly learn to recognize visual objects after minimal exposure. Integrating new information with existing knowledge requires forming enduring neuronal representations to enable future recognition. Yet, the neuronal mechanisms in the human brain underlying such rapid perceptual changes remain unclear. Here we recorded single-neuron activity in occipital cortex (OC) and medial temporal lobe (MTL) regions as participants rapidly learned to recognize degraded images. OC and MTL neurons modulated their activity to encode newly learned visual information and reshape perception. Population decoding revealed that OC neurons required additional processing time to resolve the identity of learned images, with delayed neuronal responses in the MTL. Our findings suggest that OC supports recognition after rapid learning via extensive recurrent processing, potentially involving higher-order neocortical areas, without relying on feedback from MTL. These results provide mechanistic constraints for biologically plausible models of visual recognition and few-shot visual learning.

items.title: Longitudinal single-cell profiling of breast tumors highlights immune and epigenetic mechanisms associated with sensitivity to aromatase inhibitors.
items.abstract: Estrogen receptor (ER)-positive breast cancer treatment is based primarily on endocrine therapy. To dissect mechanisms of sensitivity to aromatase inhibitors in ER-positive breast cancer, we profiled tumor biopsies from 25 patients during neoadjuvant therapy using single-cell RNA sequencing, immune receptor sequencing and enhancer activity mapping. Malignant cells with high ER signaling and elevated activity of enhancers with ER binding sites were sensitive to treatment. Resistance was associated with androgen receptor signaling, dedifferentiation and epithelial-mesenchymal transition. Poor responders preferentially used the androgen receptor cis-regulome under treatment pressure. The baseline tumor microenvironment was associated with tumor downstaging. Poor responders exhibited a 'hot', yet ineffective immune landscape enriched for naive lymphoid and undifferentiated myeloid cells. Good responders showed an active immune microenvironment with sustained clonal expansion of T cells. Our longitudinal single-cell analyses elucidate the genetic, cellular and epigenetic mechanisms driving sensitivity and resistance to neoadjuvant aromatase inhibition in ER-positive breast cancer.

items.title: Operationalising the broad definition of pre-eclampsia: a retrospective cohort study.

sections.objective: Identifying pre-eclampsia within electronic health records (EHRs) is challenged by its complex definition, evolving diagnostic criteria, and the nature of routinely collected data. There is a need to optimise methods for EHR-based definitions of this major cause of maternal and fetal and newborn mortality and morbidity.
sections.methods: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using pseudonymised data from the Early Life Cross Linkage in Research-Born in South London (eLIXIR-BiSL) cohort, linking routine maternity and neonatal records from two trusts in South London, UK, from Oct 1, 2018, to July 11, 2023. We included women with singleton pregnancies and at least one recorded blood pressure measurement from 20 weeks' gestation who gave birth at one of the contributing NHS trusts, Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust. A broad reference definition of pre-eclampsia, which was in line with current International Society for the Study of Hypertension in Pregnancy and UK National Institute for Health and Care Excellence guidelines and included evidence of maternal end-organ dysfunction or uteroplacental dysfunction, or both, that incorporated structured EHR data, was compared with three case-finding definitions: semi-structured EHR data using drop-down menus (EHR semi-structured definition); ICD-10 codes (ICD-10 definition); and combined semi-structured EHR data and ICD-10 codes (EHR semi-structured and ICD-10 definition). Diagnostic test properties and adverse outcome detection rates were assessed.
sections.results: Of 33 040 pregnancies with antenatal booking information, 21 120 pregnancies with booking information, birth outcomes, and blood pressure measurements recorded from 20 weeks' gestation were included. Women at booking had a median age of 33·0 years (IQR 29·0-36·0). Pre-eclampsia prevalence varied by definition: 7·7% (n=1630; reference definition), 4·5% (n=957; EHR semi-structured definition), 3·7% (n=773; ICD-10 definition), and 5·8% (n=1224; EHR semi-structured and ICD-10 definition). Compared with the reference definition, case-finding definitions had inferior detection rates for adverse outcomes, particularly for severe hypertension (26·0% [EHR semi-structured definition], 28·1% [ICD-10 definition], 32·6% [EHR semi-structured and ICD-10 definition]; reference 68·2%) and birthweight <10th percentile (9·7%, 10·6%, 13·3%, respectively; reference 26·2%). Specificity for detection of the reference definition of pre-eclampsia was high (97% [95% CI 97-97]) for all case-finding definitions, whereas sensitivity was poor (29% [26-31] to 37% [35-40]).
sections.conclusion: Compared with a structured EHR definition, pre-eclampsia definitions relying solely on semi-structured EHR data or ICD-10 codes, or both, underperform in identifying pregnancies with adverse outcomes. The findings highlight the need to integrate structured and semi-structured EHR data to improve pre-eclampsia case ascertainment and emphasise the importance of implementing emerging technologies for mining maternity data.

items.title: National, regional, and global trends in adolescent physical activity from 2010 to 2025: a pooled analysis of 389 surveys with 3·2 million participants from 140 countries.

sections.objective: Physical activity during adolescence improves current and future physical and mental health and contributes to preventing non-communicable diseases. We aimed to update national, regional, and global estimates of adolescent physical activity, examine the distribution of activity across days of the week, assess trends from 2010 to 2025, and progress towards the 2030 global target.
sections.methods: We pooled data from population-based surveys of self-reported number of active days (≥60 min of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity) in the past week among adolescents aged 11-17 years collected in or after 2008. Using Bayesian ordinal models, we estimated the distribution of active days per week and mean active days per week, by sex, age, country, and year. Separate models were fitted for boys and girls. We computed the posterior probability that boys' statistics were higher than girls', and that mean active days per week were higher in 2025 than in 2010. We generated projections to 2030 to assess progress towards the global target of a 15% relative reduction in the percentage of adolescents reporting fewer than 7 active days per week.
sections.results: In 2025, 24·9% (95% uncertainty interval [UI] 21·8-28·5) of adolescents globally reported 0 active days per week, and 13·9% (12·6-15·6) reported being active on 7 days per week. The global mean was 2·7 (95% UI 2·6-2·9) active days per week. Globally, there was no change detected between 2010 and 2025. No country is on track to meet the 2030 global target. Girls' mean active days per week were lower than boys' globally (2·4 [2·2-2·7] vs 3·0 [2·8-3·2], posterior probability >0·99) and in all regions (posterior probability was 0·63 in Oceania and ≥0·89 in all other regions). In central and eastern Europe and central Asia, east Asia and the Pacific, and high-income western (comprising western Europe, northern America, Australia, and New Zealand) regions, mean active days per week (3·8-4·1 vs 2·2-2·7 in other regions) and the change in mean active days per week from 2010 to 2025 (small increases of 0·1-0·3 active days vs no change detected) were more favourable than in other regions. However, in these three regions, mean active days per week declined with age (1·2-1·4 and 0·5-0·8 fewer days at age 17 years than at age 11 years for girls and boys, respectively).
sections.conclusion: Globally, adolescent physical activity remains low, especially among girls. Increasing physical activity will require effectively implemented, context-specific actions that prioritise the least active adolescents together with whole-population approaches that address socioeconomic, environmental, and cultural barriers.

items.title: Best practices in communication of environmental health risks due to localised pollution events: a mixed-methods systematic review.
items.abstract: Localised environmental pollution can generate acute concern, particularly when the health effects are uncertain. Media coverage can amplify fear and stress, necessitating transparent risk communication. This mixed-methods systematic Review (PROSPERO registration number CRD42024568007) focuses on strategies for communicating health risks associated with local pollution. We searched PubMed, Embase, Cochrane, Scopus, and PsycArticles on April 19, 2024, (from inception) and May 22, 2026 (Jan 1, 2000 onwards), supplemented by Google Scholar and OAIster (July 9, 2026), Global Index Medicus (July 10, 2026), and backward and forward citation tracking (July 16 and 17, 2026) all from Jan 1, 2000 onwards. Of 29 216 studies identified, 105 were eligible (61 quantitative, 30 qualitative, and 14 mixed-methods); all papers were written in English and included exposed populations. Review articles, animal studies, and in-vitro or in-silico studies were excluded. Quantitative outcomes comprised changes in knowledge, behaviour, stress, or fear, whereas qualitative studies analysed communication preferences or experiences. Study quality was assessed using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool. Qualitative data were analysed through thematic synthesis with CERQual assessment. Quantitative findings were narratively synthesised because of heterogeneity. Results were integrated using a convergent mixed-methods approach. Communities valued clear, plain-language explanations of pollutants, health effects, and exposure-reduction actions, supported by simple visuals and multiple communication channels. Interpersonal and community-embedded communication, especially from trusted local figures, enhanced understanding, reduced distress, and strengthened trust. Timely, consistent updates and transparent discussion of uncertainty were well received when delivered by trusted sources and combined with practical guidance but were less effective or potentially counterproductive when institutional trust was weak. Community collaboration improved the clarity, relevance, and acceptance of messages. Effective communication regarding local pollution depended on trust-building through open, empathic, and community-centred engagement. Clear, accessible messages from multiple media channels, supported by interpersonal dialogue, helped communities to understand risks without generating disproportionate worry.

items.title: Imipenem-cilastatin-funobactam versus imipenem-cilastatin-relebactam in patients with hospital-acquired bacterial pneumonia or ventilator-associated bacterial pneumonia: a phase 3, double-blind, non-inferiority randomised trial.

sections.objective: New antibiotics are urgently needed for hospital-acquired bacterial pneumonia (HABP) and ventilator-associated bacterial pneumonia (VABP). We aimed to compare the efficacy and safety of imipenem-cilastatin-funobactam with imipenem-cilastatin-relebactam in patients with HABP and VABP.
sections.methods: The phase 3, multinational, double-blind, non-inferiority, randomised controlled trial was conducted in 62 hospitals (58 in China, three in the USA, and one in Spain). Patients aged 18 years or older with HABP and VABP caused by clinically documented or suspected Gram-negative pathogens were assigned by stratified block randomisation at a 2:1 ratio to receive 1·25 g imipenem-cilastatin-funobactam or 1·25 g imipenem-cilastatin-relebactam via 30-min intravenous infusion every 6 h for 7-14 days with the dose adjusted according to renal function. Patients with previous use of prohibited antibiotics or conditions that could interfere with efficacy assessment were excluded. Masking was maintained for investigators and patients; emergency unmasking followed standard operating procedures. Missing mortality data were considered as survival in the primary endpoint analysis. The primary outcome was 14-day all-cause mortality in the modified intention-to-treat (mITT) population, with a 10% non-inferiority margin (two-sided 95% CI). This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05204563).
sections.results: Between Oct 29, 2022, and Sept 29, 2024, 534 patients were screened, 450 were randomly assigned, and 449 were included in safety populations. The mITT population also included 449 patients (mean age was 60·8 years [SD 13·9]; 313 [70%] of 449 were male). In the mITT population, 14-day all-cause mortality was 3·0% (nine of 299) for imipenem-cilastatin-funobactam versus 2·7% (four of 150) for imipenem-cilastatin-relebactam (difference 0·2%; 95% CI -3·5% to 4·0%). Grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events occurred in 22 (7%) of 299 patients in the imipenem-cilastatin-funobactam and 16 (11%) of 150 patients in the imipenem-cilastatin-relebactam group. No drug-related deaths were reported.
sections.conclusion: Imipenem-cilastatin-funobactam is statistically non-inferior to imipenem-cilastatin-relebactam for 14-day all-cause mortality in patients with HABP and VABP with a favourable safety profile.
sections.other: For the Chinese translation of the abstract see Supplementary Materials section.

items.title: Global, regional, and national burden of gallbladder and biliary diseases in 204 countries and territories, 1990-2023: a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.

sections.objective: Gallbladder and biliary diseases-including cholelithiasis, cholecystitis, cholangitis, and other non-malignant biliary tract disorders-are important contributors to the global digestive disease burden, but a global, comprehensive, and systematic estimation of their burden is absent. We aimed to quantify long-term trends and current patterns in prevalence, mortality, and disability associated with gallbladder and biliary diseases across geographies, sexes, and ages.
sections.methods: We used estimates from the Global Burden of Diseases, Injuries, and Risk Factors Study (GBD) 2023 to assess the burden of gallbladder and biliary diseases in 204 countries and territories from 1990 to 2023. Mortality was modelled with the Cause of Death Ensemble model and prevalence with the Disease Modelling Meta-Regression tool (DisMod-MR 2.1). Years of life lost (YLLs) were calculated as the number of deaths for each age-sex-location-year multiplied by the standard life expectancy at each age. Severity-specific prevalence values were multiplied by their respective disability weights (with asymptomatic cases assigned zero disability) to estimate years lived with disability (YLDs). Disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs) were computed by summing YLDs and YLLs. We report prevalence, mortality, YLDs, YLLs, and DALYs as counts and age-standardised and age-specific rates per 100 000 population with 95% uncertainty intervals (UIs), stratified by sex, GBD region, and Socio-demographic Index (SDI).
sections.results: In 1990 and 2023, the global counts for prevalence attributable to gallbladder and biliary diseases were 157·4 million (95% UI 134·0 to 183·3) and 264·4 million (226·0 to 309·9), for deaths were 65 800 (95% UI 53 000 to 78 800) and 146 700 (121 800 to 171 300), and for DALYs were 4·8 million (95% UI 3·5 to 6·2) and 8·2 million (6·3 to 10·6), representing substantial increases. However, age-standardised rates declined over the same period, from 3573·2 (95% UI 3045·5 to 4159·1) per 100 000 population to 2990·1 (2561·5 to 3492·5) per 100 000 population for prevalence, from 1·95 (1·58 to 2·31) per 100 000 population to 1·67 (1·39 to 1·95) per 100 000 population for mortality, and from 111·5 (84·1 to 143·3) per 100 000 population to 92·3 (70·9 to 119·6) per 100 000 population for DALYs. Over the past three decades, females had higher age-standardised prevalence and DALY rates than males, while sex differences in mortality rates were smaller. In 2023, age-standardised prevalence and DALY rates were lowest in south Asia and highest in central and western Europe, central Asia, and many regions in Latin America. By contrast, several regions in sub-Saharan Africa had relatively low prevalence and DALY rates but comparatively high mortality rates. National patterns broadly mirrored these regional profiles. In 2023, prevalence and DALY counts peaked in middle to early-older adulthood (ages 55-69 years), but age-specific rates continued to rise into the oldest age groups, with DALYs dominated by YLDs in midlife and early-older adulthood and by YLLs at older ages (≥80 years). The number of deaths peaked in the ninth decade of life, but age-specific rates also peaked in the oldest age groups. Across GBD regions, the association between SDI and age-standardised prevalence and DALY rates generally followed a reversed U-shaped pattern, with the lowest rates at low SDI, peak rates at intermediate SDI, and declining rates at the highest SDI levels. The association between SDI and mortality rate was less clear.
sections.conclusion: The global burden of gallbladder and biliary diseases is rising in absolute terms despite declining age-standardised rates, underscoring the importance of population growth and ageing. Health systems, particularly in settings with rapidly ageing populations and intermediate SDI levels, will need to expand diagnostic, elective, and emergency surgical capacity while investing in prevention of obesity and metabolic risk factors. Marked regional and national heterogeneity, as well as differences in risk factors, might reflect variance in health-system capacity and access to care, including timely diagnosis, availability of surgical services, and perioperative care. The predominance of non-fatal disability in midlife and rising mortality in older age groups indicates that integrated strategies spanning risk-factor control, early diagnosis, elective management, and robust acute care for older adults are essential to reduce both YLDs and YLLs.

items.authors: GBD 2023 Gallbladder and Biliary Disease Collaborators

items.title: Breathlessness mechanisms, measurement, and management in adults: evidence update on behalf of The Dyspnoea Society.
items.abstract: Breathlessness affects an estimated 40% of adults living with chronic disease, with substantial consequences for individuals, carers, and health-care systems. This Dyspnoea Society Research Statement, developed for researchers, clinicians, and adults living with or caring for someone with breathlessness, provides a state-of-the-art synthesis of recent advances in chronic breathlessness mechanisms, measurement, and management, and outlines a research agenda for the next decade. Key advancements include establishment of neural respiratory drive as a mechanistic contributor to exertional breathlessness; neuroimaging evidence that breathlessness arises from integration of peripheral and central processes within a dynamic brain network involving sensorimotor and cognitive-affective regions, supporting behavioural and psychosocial interventions; and improved measurement through responsive multidimensional instruments and approaches to quantify symptom abnormality relative to physical activity. Evidence supports early use of low-risk, non-pharmacological interventions for management of breathlessness, whereas evidence for pharmacological therapies is limited in most situations. Health-care redesign, including symptom-focused diagnostic pathways, integrated care models, and disease-agnostic breathlessness services, might help to improve patient outcomes while reducing health-care costs.

items.title: Cancer in the Commonwealth: a Lancet Oncology Commission.
items.abstract: Cancer is now one of the defining health and development challenges of our time. The 56 nations of the Commonwealth, home to 2·7 billion people, mirror this global burden. Recorded cancer cases across member states rose by 35% in 2008-18 and the number of deaths reached almost 1·7 million in 2018. The Lancet Oncology Commission on cancer in the Commonwealth was convened to ask a deceptively simple question: how can 56 diverse nations act collectively to close the widening gap between the burden of cancer and the capacity of each country to respond? 80 researchers, clinicians, policy makers, and civil society members, organised into five working groups and ten research streams, spent 2 years assembling the evidence base for this report. Using a validated microsimulation model, we estimate that 5-year net survival across eleven common cancers in the Commonwealth stood at just 30·7% in 2020, ranging from 4·1% in low-income countries (LICs) to 59·0% in high-income countries (HICs), driven overwhelmingly by late-stage presentation, which affects 62% of patients in LICs compared with 43% in HICs. This difference in survival is compounded by chronic underinvestment. Infrastructure gaps are equally stark: only 12% of countries meet international benchmarks for CT imaging, 22% for hospital density, and 40% for radiotherapy. Governance is underdeveloped too: barely one-third of Commonwealth countries have a national cancer control plan meeting basic quality criteria. Research investment also mirrors these inequities: between 2016 and 2023, Commonwealth countries collectively invested only US$165 per cancer-related disability adjusted life year. Yet the case for investment is unambiguous. Our modelling shows that a comprehensive scaleup of treatment, imaging, and quality of care could raise 5-year net survival across the Commonwealth from 30·7% to 52·9%, averting an estimated 5·8 million deaths and adding 113 million life-years between 2025 and 2035, at an incremental cost of $36·7 billion, delivering a return of between four and twenty dollars on every dollar invested. Crucially, this investment need not depend chiefly on external aid, which is contracting sharply at present. Our modelling for 38 low-income and middle-income Commonwealth countries suggests that up to $701 billion in additional domestic fiscal space could be mobilised between 2025 and 2030, through budget reprioritisation, macroeconomic growth, targeted taxation, and prudent borrowing. On this evidence, the Commission proposes six priority actions. These commitments are ambitious, set against an unusually turbulent geopolitical backdrop of declining official development assistance, fiscal retrenchment, and contested multilateralism. Yet it is precisely this backdrop that gives the Commonwealth its distinctive advantage: a voluntary association spanning every income level and continent, bound by common legal and regulatory traditions, capable of collective action that neither purely bilateral aid nor multilateral institutions under strain can easily replicate.

items.title: Perivascular macrophages restrict CXCR4-dependent accumulation of stem-like CD8+ T cells in tumors and limit chemotherapy efficacy.
items.abstract: The perivascular (Pv) niche coordinates immune-stromal interactions that facilitate cancer progression. Pharmacological inhibition or genetic inactivation of the enzyme heme oxygenase-1 (HO-1) in LYVE-1+ Pv tumor-associated macrophages (PvTAMs) synergizes with cytotoxic chemotherapy (CCT) to achieve immunological tumor control in murine breast cancer models. We investigated the tumor microenvironment (TME) during the transition to immunological control and identified an increase in stem-like TCF1+PD-1+CD8+ T cells and enrichment of tumor-selective effector T cells. Stem-like CD8+ T cells were clonally diverse and rapidly acquired a TCF1- differentiated phenotype in the TME. Their tumor accumulation depended on CXCR4 and was associated with a treatment-induced expansion of proliferating CXCL12+CD34+ Pv cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs). In human breast cancer, greater abundance of the stem-like CD8+ T cell program was associated with improved outcomes following CCT. These findings identify PvTAM HO-1 activity as a regulator of a stromal-stem-like T cell axis that limits chemotherapy efficacy and anti-tumor immunity.

items.title: Midlife Metabolic Syndrome as Mediator Between Early-Life Insulin Resistance and Later-Life Cardiovascular Diseases.

sections.objective: The cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome framework describes progression from early metabolic dysfunction to clinical cardiovascular disease. Insulin resistance (IR) in young adulthood may contribute to later atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD), but the extent to which this association is mediated through midlife metabolic syndrome (MetS) remains unclear. We aimed to evaluate the association between young-adulthood IR and later-life ASCVD and quantify mediation through midlife MetS.
sections.methods: We analyzed 3,622 Black and White participants in the Coronary Artery Risk Development in Young Adults study who were aged 18 to 30 years at baseline and free of ASCVD through year 20. IR was defined as a Homeostatic Model Assessment of Insulin Resistance value at or above the 75th percentile (≥2.67). MetS was assessed at year 20, and ASCVD events were ascertained through year 35. Parametric g-computation with pooled logistic regression estimated total and mediated effects on cumulative ASCVD risk at the end of follow-up, accounting for midlife lifestyle factors as exposure-induced mediator-outcome confounders.
sections.results: At baseline, 907 of 3,622 participants (25%) had IR. During a median follow-up of 14 years (Q1-Q3: 14-14 years) after year 20, 143 of 3,622 (3.9%) participants experienced an ASCVD event. Young-adulthood IR was associated with a 1.50-fold higher ASCVD risk at the end of follow-up (95% CI: 1.13-2.01), with 63.4% of the association mediated through midlife MetS (indirect risk ratio: 1.29; 95% CI: 1.13-1.48).
sections.conclusion: Young-adulthood IR was associated with higher later-life ASCVD risk, with a substantial proportion mediated through midlife MetS. These findings suggest early identification of IR and prevention of progression to MetS may help reduce long-term cardiovascular risk.

items.title: Extended in vivo activity of VRC01 HIV-1 prophylaxis entails initial protective efficacy and subsequent breakthrough infections.
items.abstract: The two parallel antibody-mediated prevention (AMP) efficacy trials evaluated whether intravenous infusion of the anti-CD4 binding site broadly neutralizing antibody VRC01 prevents HIV-1 acquisition. Here, we analyzed HIV-1 acquisition in AMP through the week 104 final study visit. Against viruses considered highly sensitive to VRC01 [80% inhibitory concentration (IC80) < 1 microgram/milliliter], VRC01 prophylaxis maintained cumulative prevention efficacy of 66.3% (95% confidence interval: 32.4, 83.2%), suggesting that the antibody successfully blocked or cleared these infections. In the post-week 80 period (after the final dose at week 72), HIV diagnosis and resistance to VRC01 were more frequent and greater in the VRC01 groups versus placebo. For instance, more HIV diagnoses with viruses considered moderately sensitive or resistant to VRC01 (IC80 ≥ 5 microgram/milliliter) were made in the VRC01 groups compared with placebo groups (11 versus 1). Plausibly, as in vivo VRC01 concentration waned, suppressed viruses-often evolving greater resistance because of selective pressure-emerged as detectable infections. Our findings suggest that, whereas single antibodies can block sensitive strains, multiple antibodies are likely required to prevent both viral escape and breakthrough infections.

items.title: Survival in patients with renal cell carcinoma and brain metastases: an update of the Renal Graded Prognostic Assessment.

sections.objective: Brain metastases are a common and serious consequence for patients with renal cell carcinoma. This study aimed to determine if survival has changed since the introduction of current therapies, identify prognostic factors, update the prognostic index (the Renal Graded Prognostic Assessment [GPA]) in the context of contemporary multi-modal therapies, compare outcomes with legacy cohorts, and determine whether overall survival correlates with intracranial progression-free survival.
sections.methods: An international consortium of 21 academic institutions contributed uniformly-curated retrospective data from 1049 patients with newly-diagnosed renal cell carcinoma with brain metastases (RCC-BM) treated between Jan 1, 2016, and Dec 31, 2022. Patients treated between 1985-2007 (n=286) and 2006-15 (n=711) were considered legacy cohorts and compared to the current cohort. Significant prognostic factors for survival were identified through combined multivariable analyses and used to update the Renal GPA. Intracranial progression-free survival was defined as the interval from date of initial RCC-BM diagnosis to date of first salvage treatment.
sections.results: Of the 1049 patients, 773 (73·7%) patients were male and 276 (26·3%) were female; the majority (851 [81·1%]) were White, and the median age was 63·9 years (IQR 56·2-70·3). The median overall survival was 20·0 months (95% CI 18·0-23·4), with a median follow-up of 53·4 months (95% CI 50·2-56·8). Overall survival for the legacy cohorts were 9·6 months (95% CI 8-11) and 12·0 months (5-11), respectively. In combined multivariable analyses, significant prognostic factors for inferior survival were lower Karnofsky Performance Status, lower baseline serum albumin, higher number of brain metastases, and presence of extracranial metastases. These factors were incorporated into the updated Renal GPA. Median survival was 4·8 months (95% CI 3·0-8·1) for patients with GPA 0-1·0, 12·4 months (10·6-17·2) for GPA 1·5-2·0, 33·6 months (27·5-40·0) for GPA 2·5-3·0, and 51·2 months (34·1-undefined) for GPA 3·5-4·0. Median intracranial progression-free survival was 9·6 months (95% CI 8·4-10·6). The Spearman's rank correlation between intracranial progression-free survival and overall survival was moderately strong (0·74 [95% CI 0·70-0·78]; p<0·0001).
