sections.conclusion: Survival has improved compared to the legacy cohorts but varies widely by GPA. The updated Renal GPA can be used to estimate survival, intracranial progression-free survival, individualise treatment, design and stratify clinical trials, and refine clinical trial eligibility.

items.title: The Participant Engagement and Cancer Genome Sequencing Network to accelerate research in rare and understudied cancers.
items.abstract: The genomic characterization of cancers has considerably advanced research and clinical practice. However, critical gaps remain, including limited knowledge of tumor profiles in rare cancers and populations understudied in genomic research and insufficient integration of genomic, clinical and epidemiologic data. This Perspective highlights the Participant Engagement and Cancer Genome Sequencing (PE-CGS) Network, established by the US National Cancer Institute to address knowledge gaps in rare and understudied cancers. PE-CGS comprises five research centers supported by a coordinating center and guided by an external advisory panel. Collaborations across PE-CGS are grounded in shared values of participant-centeredness, engagement, access, collaboration and innovation. Activities emphasize participant engagement throughout the research process, including the return of results and collection of clinical and epidemiologic data alongside paired tumor/germline sequencing. PE-CGS demonstrates how engagement, return of results and comprehensive data collection can be integrated to support participant-centered cancer genomics research and accelerate research in rare and understudied cancers.

items.title: A synthetic heparin oligosaccharide decouples anticoagulation from heparin-induced thrombocytopenia risk.
items.abstract: Low-molecular weight heparin (LMWH) remains clinically indispensable for the prevention and treatment of thrombosis in cardiovascular surgery, hemodialysis, and other critical care settings. However, LMWH is constrained by heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT) and supply chain vulnerabilities of animal-derived sources. This study used chemoenzymatic synthesis to engineer homogeneous dodecasaccharide 12G-2, decoupling anticoagulant efficacy from HIT risk via dual structural modulation. Substitution with 2-O-sulfated glucuronic acid conferred conformational rigidity, and engineered sulfation attenuated platelet factor 4 (PF4) binding, whereas the antithrombin-binding domain remained intact. 12G-2 exhibited nanomolar anti-Factor Xa (FXa) activity in vitro, enoxaparin-equivalent venous antithrombotic efficacy, and superior arterial antithrombotic activity in murine thrombosis models, and it showed diminished PF4 binding, attenuated pathological β sheet formation, and minimal recognition by HIT-related antibodies in vitro. Both in vitro and in a murine tail-bleeding model, 12G-2 demonstrated high protamine reversibility, exceeding standard LMWH enoxaparin neutralization efficiency. In washed human platelets, 12G-2-PF4 complexes with the HIT-mimicking antibody KKO failed to induce integrin αIIbβ3 activation or P-selectin release and elicited minimal platelet spreading comparable to resting controls. Safety assessments in mice showed no hepatotoxicity at tested doses and low immunogenicity in a murine PF4-heparin immunization model. In PF4-heparin antibody-positive mice, 12G-2 attenuated platelet activation while exerting stronger FXa inhibition than enoxaparin. These findings established 12G-2 as an alternative to LMWH.

items.title: Long-term outcomes after percutaneous coronary intervention with drug-eluting stents versus coronary artery bypass grafting for left main coronary artery disease: a prospective analysis of the multicentre IRIS-MAIN registry.

sections.objective: Percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with drug-eluting stents has been widely used to treat patients with left main coronary artery disease; however, long-term comparative outcomes versus coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) in real-world populations remain poorly characterised. We aimed to compare long-term all-cause mortality after PCI or CABG in Asian patients with unprotected left main coronary artery disease.
sections.methods: We analysed prospectively collected data from the multicentre IRIS-MAIN registry, conducted at 46 hospitals in South Korea, India, Japan, Indonesia, and Malaysia. The registry enrolled adults aged 18 years or older with unprotected left main coronary artery disease (defined as a stenosis diameter of ≥50% as visually estimated on angiography), who had been treated with PCI, CABG, or medical therapy alone. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality. We used a target trial emulation framework to compare the long-term risk of all-cause mortality between PCI with drug-eluting stents and isolated CABG. We used propensity-score overlap weighting to adjust for measured baseline covariates. The IRIS-MAIN Registry study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT01341327).
sections.results: Between Jan 1, 2003, and Dec 31, 2024, 6900 patients were enrolled in the IRIS-MAIN registry, of whom 5379 (78·0%) underwent coronary revascularisation through either PCI with drug-eluting stents (3836 [71·3%]) or CABG (1543 [28·7%]) and were included in the analysis. The median duration of follow-up for all patients was 10·0 years (IQR 5·0-16·7). In the overlap-weighted population, no statistically detectable difference in 10-year weighted Kaplan-Meier rates of all-cause mortality was observed between PCI and CABG (24·0% vs 22·9%; overlap-weighted hazard ratio 1·00 [95% CI 0·87-1·14]; p=0·99). The confidence interval does not exclude a mortality benefit or harm with either strategy.
sections.conclusion: In this non-randomised registry analysis of patients with left main coronary artery disease, there was no statistically detectable difference in all-cause mortality between PCI and CABG. For patients considered suitable for either strategy, multidisciplinary Heart Team discussion might help patients and clinicians weigh potential trade-offs in the choice between PCI and CABG. These findings are observational and cannot establish causal treatment effects or equivalence in survival.

items.title: Single vs Double ProGlide Devices for Access Site Closure after Transfemoral Aortic Valve Replacement: The SINGLE-CLOSURE Trial.

sections.objective: Despite advances in transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR), access-site vascular complications remain an important source of procedural morbidity. The conventional double-ProGlide strategy may increase the risk of access-site stenosis and other vascular complications, particularly in patients with challenging iliofemoral anatomy. Retrospective studies have suggested that a single-ProGlide strategy may offer an effective alternative, but this strategy has not yet been evaluated in a randomized trial. This trial aimed to determine whether a single-ProGlide strategy could offer a simpler alternative to the conventional double-ProGlide strategy without increasing vascular complications.
sections.methods: The SINGLE-CLOSURE trial was a prospective, multicenter, open-label, randomized trial conducted at 25 centers in China. Patients aged ≥65 years scheduled for transfemoral TAVR were assigned 1:1 to single-ProGlide or double-ProGlide closure for the main access site. The primary endpoint was the in-hospital composite of Valve Academic Research Consortium (VARC)-3-defined access-site or access-related major and minor vascular complications.
sections.results: A total of 876 patients were randomized. In the modified intention-to-treat population, the primary endpoint occurred in 57 of 436 patients (13.1%) in the single-ProGlide group and 65 of 430 patients (15.1%) in the double-ProGlide group, meeting the prespecified criterion for noninferiority (risk difference: -2.2%; 95%: -7.0% to 2.6%; P = 0.013; noninferiority margin: 3.19%). Access-related major vascular complications occurred in 2 patients (0.5%) in the single-ProGlide group and 6 patients (1.4%) in the double-ProGlide group. Among the secondary endpoints, individual components of the primary endpoint, access-related bleeding, time to hemostasis, and all-cause mortality were similar between groups. Access-site stenosis was numerically less frequent with the single-ProGlide strategy (5.0% vs 7.9%), whereas additional closure devices might be used more often (2.5% vs 0.9%).
sections.conclusion: A single-ProGlide strategy was noninferior to conventional double-ProGlide closure for the composite of VARC-3-defined access-site or access-related vascular complications after transfemoral TAVR. Primary endpoint events were predominantly minor vascular complications.

items.title: Percutaneous Transcatheter Mitral Valve Replacement for Symptomatic Mitral Regurgitation: 2-Year Outcomes From the ENCIRCLE Trial.

sections.objective: Transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR) is an approved treatment option for select high-risk patients with symptomatic mitral regurgitation (MR). The main cohort of the ENCIRCLE trial, evaluating fully percutaneous transseptal TMVR with the SAPIEN M3 system, demonstrated 13.9% mortality, significant MR reduction, and improved functional and health status outcomes at 1 year. We report 2-year outcomes from the main cohort of the ENCIRCLE trial.
sections.methods: Eligible symptomatic patients with ≥3+ MR who were not suitable for surgery or transcatheter edge-to-edge repair underwent TMVR with the SAPIEN M3 system. Independent study oversight included an echocardiographic core laboratory and a clinical events committee. Endpoints included the nonhierarchical composite rate of all-cause mortality or heart failure hospitalization (HFH) as well as clinical, echocardiographic, functional, and health status outcomes.
sections.results: A total of 299 patients were treated, with 2-year follow-up data available for 202 of 210 eligible patients (96.2%). Mean age was 75.5 ± 9.3 years, 50.8% were men, and the mean Society of Thoracic Surgeons Predicted Risk of Mortality score for mitral valve replacement was 6.6% ± 4.1%. At 2 years, MR reduction was sustained, with MR ≤1+ in 97.0% patients (P < 0.001). The 2-year composite rate of all-cause mortality or HFH was 35.6% (25.1% all-cause mortality, 23.0% HFH). In a 365-day landmark analysis, 1- to 2-year rates were 13.0% for all-cause mortality and 10.6% for first HFH. At 2 years, the rates of disabling stroke, clinically significant valve thrombosis, and hemolysis requiring intervention were 6.6%, 7.1%, and 7.6%, respectively. There were no instances of clinically significant left ventricular outflow obstruction. Improvements in functional and health status outcomes were sustained with 87.0% of patients in NYHA functional class I/II (P < 0.001) and a mean Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire overall summary score increase of 17.2 points (P < 0.001). The 6-minute walk distance increased by +9.0 ± 97.3 m compared to baseline (P = 0.246).
sections.conclusion: The 2-year results of the ENCIRCLE trial demonstrated durable near MR elimination with sustained improvements in functional and health status outcomes in surviving patients. These findings support transseptal TMVR as a therapeutic option for carefully selected patients with symptomatic MR. (The ENCIRCLE Trial [ENCIRCLE]; NCT04153292).

items.title: Bare-Metal vs Covered Balloon-Expandable Stents for Transplant Renal Artery Stenosis: A Retrospective Comparative Study.

sections.objective: To compare short- and long-term outcomes of bare-metal (BMS) vs covered (CS) balloon-expandable stents in transplant renal artery stenosis (TRAS).
sections.methods: This retrospective study evaluated patients who underwent elective stent placement for TRAS between 2016 and 2023. Short-term efficacy was assessed by clinical improvement (resolution of resistant hypertension/hypervolemia) and reduction in serum creatinine (sCr) within 14 days post-procedure. Long-term outcomes included Doppler ultrasound parameters - peak systolic velocity (PSV), acceleration time (AT) and resistive index (RI) - and restenosis/occlusion rates requiring or not intervention. Graft survival at the latest follow-up was recorded.
sections.results: A total of 40 patients (mean age 58 ± 13 years, 68% male) were treated with BMS (n = 31) or CS (n = 9). Clinical improvement was observed in 71% of BMS and 83% of CS patients (P = 1.00). Median sCr decreased by 26% and 33% in BMS and CS patients, respectively (P = .30). At a median follow-up of 29 months, there were no statistically significant differences between groups in median PSV reduction (47% BMS vs 47% CS; P = .44), AT improvement (36% BMS vs 25% CS; P = .38) or RI increase (15% BMS vs 33% CS; P = .12). In the BMS group, 2 cases of in-stent restenosis occurred (6.5%). In the CS group, 1 stent occlusion occurred (11%), resulting in graft loss. At final follow-up, overall graft survival was 85%.
sections.conclusion: In this pilot study, BMS and CS showed no significant differences in TRAS outcomes. Further studies are warranted to better guide stent selection.Clinical ImpactIn transplant renal artery stenosis, balloon-expandable covered stents achieved clinical, biochemical and Doppler outcomes comparable to bare-metal stents, despite being used in more complex, atherosclerotic and longer lesions. This first direct comparison suggests that covered stents may be a reasonable option when heavy calcification, a friable wall or mural thrombus raise concern for embolisation or rupture, while bare-metal stents remain appropriate for most lesions. The single late covered-stent occlusion with graft loss highlights the need for careful platform selection and antiplatelet management. These pilot data should inform adequately powered multicentre registries rather than directly change practice.

items.title: Ruptured INfrarenal abdominal AneurySm: aortiC repair using the ENduranT Endograft. The R.IN.AS.C.ENT.E. Study.

sections.objective: Ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm (rAAA) represents a vascular surgical emergency with high mortality. Endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) using the bifurcated Endurant stent graft system is widely employed; however, data specifically addressing its performance in infrarenal rAAA remain limited.
sections.methods: We conducted a retrospective, multicenter study including 121 patients with confirmed infrarenal rAAA treated exclusively with bifurcated Endurant II or IIs (Medtronic Inc., Minneapolis, Minnesota) devices across 5 Italian tertiary vascular centers from January 2014 to October 2024. Primary endpoints were technical success and 30-day all-cause mortality. Secondary outcomes included long-term survival, incidence of endoleaks, and reintervention rates. Patients receiving alternative stent grafts or hybrid procedures were excluded to ensure cohort homogeneity.
sections.results: A total of 121 patients were enrolled during the study period. The cohort had a mean age of 75.3 ± 8.2 years, with 91.7% male predominance. Technical success was achieved in 96.7%. The 30-day mortality rate was 15.7%. Multivariate logistic regression identified abdominal compartment syndrome (ACS) (odds ratio [OR], 29.8; 95% confidence interval [CI], 2.8-317.7; P = .005) and use of an aortic occlusion balloon (AOB) (OR, 16.4; 95% CI, 2.5-106.2; P = .003) as independent predictors of early mortality. At a median follow-up of 33.6 months (interquartile range, 4.9-72.3), 5-year survival was 65.4%, freedom from any endoleak was 92.6%, and freedom from reintervention was 91.6%. Late type Ia endoleaks occurred in 2.5% of patients.
sections.conclusion: In this large, strictly defined infrarenal rAAA cohort, bifurcated Endurant stent grafts demonstrated high technical success and favorable early and mid-term clinical outcomes, including in patients with hostile neck anatomy. Early identification and management of ACS and judicious use of AOBs may improve survival. These findings reinforce current EVAR-first guidelines and emphasize the importance of device-specific outcome assessment in emergent rAAA repair.Clinical ImpactThis multicenter study provides one of the largest device-specific evaluations of bifurcated Endurant stent grafts for infrarenal ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysms in a rigorously defined Italian cohort, demonstrating high technical success (96.7%) and low 30-day mortality (15.7%) despite a high prevalence of hostile neck anatomy (54.5%). Abdominal compartment syndrome and the use of an aortic occlusion balloon emerged as independent predictors of early mortality, highlighting the critical role of perioperative management. Mid-term outcomes were favorable, with a 5-year survival rate of 65.4%, a low incidence of type Ia endoleak (2.5%), and high freedom from reintervention (91.6%). Overall, these findings support the use of Endurant devices in emergent settings for anatomically suitable patients and reinforce EVAR-first strategies in the management of ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysms.

items.title: Outcomes of AngioJet™ Rheolytic Thrombectomy for Occluded Lower-Extremity Bypass Grafts: A Single-Center Retrospective Study.

sections.objective: Lower-extremity bypass graft occlusion is associated with recurrent ischemia and potential limb loss. This study evaluated the technical and clinical outcomes of AngioJet™ rheolytic thrombectomy for occluded bypass grafts in a single-center retrospective cohort.
sections.methods: Consecutive patients undergoing AngioJet™ thrombectomy as the primary strategy for occluded bypass grafts (2014-2024) were reviewed. Technical success was defined as <30% residual stenosis. Outcomes included Rutherford category improvement, complications, 30-day mortality, major amputation, target lesion revascularization, and primary patency. Follow-up was available for 38/40 (95.0%) 30-day survivors.
sections.results: Forty-one procedures were analyzed. Technical success was achieved in 38/41 (92.7%; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 80.1%-98.5%). Periprocedural complications occurred in 4 patients (9.8%; 95% CI: 2.7%-23.1%). Thirty-day mortality was 2.4% (1/41; 95% CI: 0.1%-12.9%) and major amputation was 4.9% (2/41; 95% CI: 0.6%-16.5%). Rutherford category improvement at 30 days was 43.9% (18/41; 95% CI: 28.5%-60.3%). Primary patency at final follow-up was 63.4% (26/41; 95% CI: 46.9%-77.9%) in the overall cohort (intent-to-treat) and 68.4% (26/38; 95% CI: 51.3%-82.5%) among technically successful cases.
sections.conclusion: AngioJet™ thrombectomy is a technically feasible endovascular option for occluded bypass grafts with low 30-day mortality (2.4%) and amputation rates (4.9%). Prospective comparative studies are needed to define its role relative to surgical and alternative endovascular approaches.Clinical ImpactOccluded lower-extremity bypass grafts often cause limb-threatening ischemia in patients at high surgical risk. In this single-center cohort, AngioJet rheolytic thrombectomy achieved technical success in 92.7% of procedures, with 30-day mortality of 2.4% and major amputation of 4.9%. These findings support AngioJet-assisted thrombectomy as a minimally invasive option for carefully selected patients with crossable grafts and treatable inflow or outflow disease. Clinicians should anticipate adjunctive interventions, monitor for compartment syndrome, and provide structured surveillance because reintervention remains common. Prospective comparative studies are needed before routine first-line use.

items.title: Treatment Strategies and Outcomes of Aneurysms Affecting Small and Medium Arteries in Neurofibromatosis Type 1. A systematic review.

sections.objective: Neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1)-associated arterial aneurysms are rare and characterized by vessel fragility and heterogeneous presentation. Evidence guiding optimal management remains limited. This systematic review aimed to evaluate treatment strategies and outcomes in NF1-related arterial aneurysms.
sections.methods: A systematic review was conducted according to PRISMA guidelines and registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251169825). PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched for studies reporting management and outcomes of NF1-associated arterial aneurysms. Case reports, case series, and observational studies were included. Data were independently extracted by two reviewers. Primary outcomes included treatment strategies, technical success, complications, and mortality. Isolated aortic aneurysms or aortic dissections were not considered the primary target of the review. However, studies reporting concomitant aortic disease and aneurysmal involvement of non-aortic arteries were retained when relevant data on NF1-associated vasculopathy and its management were available.
sections.results: Eighty-six studies including 99 patients (mean age 42 years; 44.4% male) were analyzed. Aneurysms were most frequently located in cervico-vertebral (45.2%) and visceral arteries (24.0%). Multifocal disease was present in 12.1% of patients. Overall, 65.7% of patients presented with aneurysm rupture or acute hemorrhage. This high proportion should be interpreted cautiously because of the substantial publication bias inherent to a literature predominantly based on case reports and small case series. Endovascular therapy was the most frequently used approach (68.7%), followed by open surgery (19.2%), hybrid repair (5.0%), and conservative management (9.1%). Endovascular treatment showed a reported technical success rate exceeding 90%. Recanalization (6.3%), delayed thrombosis (4.2%), and new aneurysm formation (5.3%) were observed. Open repair was mainly used for anatomically complex or endovascularly inaccessible lesions. Overall mortality was 8.1%, primarily in patients presenting with rupture.
sections.conclusion: NF1-associated aneurysms require an individualized, anatomy-driven management strategy. Endovascular therapy was the most frequently reported treatment and appears to be a viable option in anatomically suitable patients, while open and hybrid techniques remain important for selected complex lesions. However, the available evidence is derived predominantly from case reports and small case series and does not permit comparative assessment of treatment strategies. Lifelong imaging surveillance is mandatory due to the risk of recurrence and new aneurysm formation.

items.title: Transcarotid Artery Stenting Using Flow Reversal for Non-Atherosclerotic Carotid Artery Disease.

sections.objective: We evaluated the use of transcarotid artery revascularization (TCAR) in non-atherosclerotic carotid disease and compared outcomes with transfemoral carotid artery stenting (TFCAS).
sections.methods: The Vascular Quality Initiative registry was queried for all TCAR and TFCAS procedures performed from 2017-2024. Patients with lesion types categorized as atherosclerosis or restenosis were excluded. The study cohort included dissection, trauma, fibromuscular dysplasia (FMD), and other non-atherosclerotic etiologies. Primary outcomes included major adverse events, including stroke, death, and composite endpoints. Propensity score matching was performed to adjust for baseline differences.
sections.results: A total of 541 TCAR and 2,348 TFCAS patients met inclusion criteria. TCAR was associated with lower contrast usage and fluoroscopy time across all lesion types. In unadjusted analyses, stroke or death rates were higher with TFCAS than TCAR for dissection (7.1% vs 1.9%, p=0.006), other lesions (8.7% vs 2.1%, p<0.001), and symptomatic (8.1% vs 2.2%, p=0.001) and asymptomatic patients (6.4% vs 1.6%, p<0.001). After propensity matching (527 pairs), TCAR was associated with significantly lower rates of stroke (4.4% vs 1.7%, p=0.0118), death (4.4% vs 0.4%, p<0.001), stroke or death (7.6% vs 1.9%, p<0.001), and stroke, death, or MI (8.0% vs 2.7%, p<0.001) compared with TFCAS (TFCAS vs TCAR, respectively).
sections.conclusion: This study supports consideration of TCAR for non-atherosclerotic carotid pathology when carotid stenting is indicated and suggests that TCAR may offer important advantages over TFCAS, particularly in reducing the risk of perioperative stroke or death.

items.title: Beyond Risk Scores: Concordance of a Multidisciplinary Decision Support Instrument with Real Life Treatment Decisions for Patients with Ruptured Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm.

sections.objective: Treatment decisions for patients with ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm (rAAA) are ethically complex and must be made under time pressure. This prospective observational study assessed how a previously developed decision support instrument (DSI) for rAAA aligns with real life treatment decisions and determined a reference threshold for interpreting its output. The DSI estimates the proportion of experts from the original multidisciplinary expert panel who would be expected to favour operative treatment (OT) for a given patient profile.
sections.methods: Consecutive rAAA patients were included between March 2024 and January 2026 from two Dutch hospitals. Treating vascular surgeons completed the DSI after the actual treatment decision (OT or palliative care). DSI outputs were analysed in relation to observed treatment decisions. A threshold sweep analysis was performed to identify a contextual reference threshold reflecting the level of DSI estimated expert support at which OT was generally pursued. Post-operative outcomes were assessed in OT patients for clinical context.
sections.results: Fifty patients were included; OT was chosen in 43 patients (86%). DSI estimated expert support was higher for patients receiving OT compared with palliative care (median 98% [interquartile range 97, 99%] vs. 83% [59, 89%]; p < .001). The contextual reference threshold was 93%, with concordance of 94% (95% confidence interval 83.8 - 97.9%). Case analysis highlighted challenges in capturing unresponsiveness due to profound hypovolaemic shock and assessing cardiac burden acutely Among patients surviving OT, relatively high health related quality of life was observed.
sections.conclusion: The DSI shows concordance with real life treatment decisions for rAAA. A contextual reference threshold above which operative treatment was generally pursued could be empirically derived. Although refinement is needed to better identify certain high risk patients, these findings represent an important first step in the validation pathway and provide proof of concept for behavioural artificial intelligence technology methodology.

items.title: A New Dedicated Platform in the Treatment of Iliac and Femoropopliteal Lesions via Transradial Access.

sections.objective: The results of a clinical study with a new dedicated platform comprising a guiding sheath, balloon catheter, and stent delivery system designed for transradial access for lower limb transluminal angioplasty are reported.
sections.methods: The RADIANCY trial is a European, multicentre, prospective, single arm study evaluating the RADIANZ Vascular Stent System (Cordis) in patients with symptomatic iliac or femoropopliteal disease. The primary safety endpoint was major radial access complications through discharge. The primary efficacy endpoint was technical success of the index procedure. Using the Clopper-Pearson method, a cohort of 129 patients provided 88% power to show technical success > 93% and complication rate < 7%. After a roll in phase, safety and efficacy were assessed in the main cohort. Adverse events were adjudicated by an independent clinical events committee.
sections.results: Across 12 European centres, 151 patients were enrolled, including 22 roll in patients and 129 in the main cohort. Patients were aged 68.2 ± 9.4 years, 26.4% were women, and their Rutherford classification score was 2.78 ± 0.74. Multiple vessel segments were treated, mainly in the common iliac and superficial femoral arteries. Through discharge, there were no major radial access site complications (0%, 95% confidence interval [CI] 2.30%), and the technical success in patients receiving the study stent system was 99.2% (95% CI 96.20%). Thus, the primary safety and efficacy endpoints were achieved. The thirty day peri-procedural adverse event rate was 18.6% (24 of 129), with transradial access site haematoma (n = 10) being the most common. Four (3.1%) serious device or procedure related adverse events through thirty days were reported, including one ischaemic stroke that recovered (0.8%), one superficial femoral artery dissection (0.8%) ultimately requiring index limb amputation (0.8%), and one grade II haematoma (0.8%). Patient discharge within twenty-four hours was 76.0% (98 of 129).
sections.conclusion: This new dedicated platform for transradial access in lower limb interventions met its primary safety and efficacy endpoints in this first clinical evaluation.

items.title: Safety and Effectiveness of the GORE VIABAHN FORTEGRA Venous Stent for the Treatment of Symptomatic Inferior Vena Cava Obstruction With or Without Combined Iliofemoral Obstruction.

sections.objective: This prospective, non-randomised, clinical investigational trial investigated the safety and effectiveness of the GORE VIABAHN FORTEGRA Venous Stent for treatment of symptomatic inferior vena cava obstruction, with or without combined iliofemoral obstruction.
sections.methods: Subjects were enrolled at 17 sites across the USA, Europe, Australia, and New Zealand. The primary endpoint was a composite measure including primary patency and freedom from stent embolisation at 12 months, and 30 day freedom from pulmonary embolism and device or procedure related death, major bleeding, and vascular injury requiring surgical or endovascular intervention. The hypothesis driven secondary endpoint was change in revised venous clinical severity score (rVCSS) pain score from baseline to 12 months.
sections.results: Eighty nine subjects were treated with an investigational iliocaval venous stent. Fifty nine (75%) of 79 evaluable subjects experienced freedom from a primary endpoint event, exceeding the performance goal of 58% at 12 months (90% confidence interval 66.6 - 82.7%) (p < .001). Of the 63 subjects reporting any pain at baseline, 51 (81%), saw an improvement in rVCSS pain score at 12 months, with a median difference of -2.0 (p < .001).
sections.conclusion: Endovascular treatment of symptomatic iliocaval obstruction with the purpose designed investigational venous stent is safe and effective. Results demonstrate robust primary patency rates, an acceptable safety profile, and reduced pain.

items.title: Incidence and Risk Factors of Surgical Site Infections in Vascular Surgical Procedures in the Groin.

sections.objective: Vascular procedures in the groin are common and carry a high risk of surgical site infection (SSI). Several risk factors have been established but others are less clear, not least due to the heterogeneity of studies. This study aimed to provide generalisable data on SSI and associated factors after open vascular procedures in the groin.
sections.methods: This was a retrospective, dual centre cohort study including all patients undergoing open vascular surgery in the groin during a twelve year period at two centres. The primary endpoints were SSI rates at thirty and ninety days. Secondary endpoints were mortality at thirty days and 1 year.
sections.results: After exclusion of 165 early peri-operative deaths (5.6%) from the original 2 968 patients, 2 803 were analysed of which 1 424 (50.8%) included a bypass and 1 130 (40.4%) an endarterectomy, while 570 patients (20.3%) underwent minor procedures. The incidence of SSI was 6.3% (176 of 2 803) at thirty days and 8.2% (170 of 2 087) at ninety days. Of these, 40.1% (n = 83) were superficial, 32.8% (n = 68) involved the fascial layer, and 27.1% (n = 56) involved the vessels. All cause mortality was 6.6% (197 of 2 968) at thirty days and 14.1% (418 of 2 968) at 1 year, the latter significantly associated with SSI at thirty days (hazard ratio 2.23, 95% confidence interval 1.32 - 3.75; p = .003). On multivariable regression analysis, higher body mass index (odds ratio [OR] 1.08; p < .001), previous percutaneous interventions on the index vessels (OR 1.47; p = .030), use of a bovine pericardium patch (OR 1.98; p = .007), and creation of a supra-inguinal bypass (OR 1.91; p = .008) were associated with increased odds of SSI. Furthermore, lymphatic complications were strongly associated with subsequent SSI on univariable analysis (OR 3.766; p < .001).
sections.conclusion: The odds of experiencing SSI depend on several patient and procedure related factors. Lymphatic complications were strongly associated with subsequent SSI. Therefore, future prospective studies should investigate whether strategies to reduce lymphatic complications also reduce SSIs.

items.title: Hypothalamus-driven brain health through metabolic flexibility.
items.abstract: Organismal physiology depends on continuous, non-hierarchical communication among cells, tissues, and organs. We argue that this communication rests on metabolic flexibility-the capacity of cells and tissues to adapt substrate use to changing energetic demands-and that the hypothalamus serves as the central hub coordinating this flexibility across the body. Using hypothalamic agouti-related protein (AgRP) and pro-opiomelanocortin (POMC) neurons as a model, we show these melanocortin neurons do more than regulate hunger and satiety: by integrating metabolic, hormonal, and immune signals, they shape reward, learning, executive function, and social behavior, while imposing coordinated metabolic states on peripheral tissues. When this flexibility is lost, as with aging or overnutrition, body-brain communication becomes rigid, driving cognitive decline, chronic inflammation, and neurodegenerative disease. We propose that signals from the body are not peripheral modifiers of brain function but fundamental determinants of it, with direct implications for hypothalamus-centered strategies to preserve brain health across the lifespan.
keywords: hypothalamus, synaptic plasticity, mitochondria, metabolic flexibility, aging, Alzheimer’s disease, Parkinson disease, multiple sclerosis

items.title: Redox-dependent remodeling of mitochondrial nucleoids contributes to bioenergetic decline during neuronal aging.
items.abstract: Why mitochondria progressively fail in aging neurons remains a fundamental question in neurobiology. Although bioenergetic decline and oxidative stress are hallmarks of aging, whether redox signaling remodels mitochondrial nucleoids (mt-nucleoids) to impair neuronal bioenergetics remains unclear. Using aged mouse neurons and human induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived neurons, we demonstrate that redox-driven mt-nucleoid remodeling underlies reduced mtDNA transcript abundance and bioenergetic decline. Combining minimal photon fluxes (MINFLUX) nanoscopy with single-molecule transcription mapping, we identify distinct mt-nucleoid architectures governed by mitochondrial transcription factor A (TFAM)-mediated mtDNA compaction. Aging-associated oxidative stress drives mt-nucleoid remodeling from compact, transcriptionally active structures toward decompacted forms with reduced mtDNA transcript abundance and impaired mitochondrial ATP production. This remodeling involves species-specific TFAM redox mechanisms: cysteine oxidation promotes human TFAM polymerization, whereas methionine oxidation weakens mouse TFAM-mtDNA interactions. Notably, expressing an oxidation-resistant TFAM variant restores mt-nucleoid organization, mtDNA transcript abundance, and ATP production in aged neurons, identifying mt-nucleoid architecture as a potential target for preserving neuronal bioenergetics during aging.

items.title: Targeting ALDOA Lactylation Reverses Vascular Remodeling in Pulmonary Hypertension by Disrupting Actin Polymerization and YAP Activation.

sections.objective: Maladaptive vascular remodeling is a hallmark of pulmonary hypertension (PH), and therapeutic strategies directly targeting the pathological activity of smooth muscle cells remain limited. Metabolic and epigenetic dysregulation are established drivers of PH, and lysine lactylation has emerged as a novel posttranslational modification implicated in diverse diseases; however, its direct contribution to PH progression remains undefined.
sections.methods: Integrated lactylomic and proteomic profiling was performed in hypoxic human pulmonary arterial smooth muscle cells. The functional role of ALDOA (aldolase A) lactylation at lysine 42 (K42) was assessed using site-specific mutant virus and smooth muscle cell-specific inducible ALDOA knockout mice in 2 established PH models: SU5416+hypoxia in mice and monocrotaline in rats.
sections.results: We identified ALDOA as a prominent lactylation target in hypoxic pulmonary arterial smooth muscle cells, with K42 lactylation consistently elevated in primary pulmonary arterial smooth muscle cells derived from PH rodent models and human PH tissues. Mechanistically, AARS1 (alanyl-tRNA synthetase 1)-mediated ALDOA K42 lactylation enhanced its binding to γ-actin, independent of glycolytic activity. This lactylation-enhanced interaction promoted F-actin polymerization and activated YAP (Yes-associated protein) signaling via LATS1 (large tumor suppressor kinase 1) inhibition, thereby driving pulmonary arterial smooth muscle cell proliferation and phenotypic switching. Moreover, YAP/TEAD4 (TEA domain transcription factor 4)-mediated transcriptional upregulation of AARS1 established a positive feedback loop reinforcing ALDOA K42 lactylation under hypoxia. In vivo, ALDOA inducible knockout or reconstitution with the lactylation-deficient K42R (lysine 42 mutant to arginine) mutant attenuated experimental PH progression, with suppressed F-actin/YAP activation and reduced vascular remodeling. Furthermore, competitive inhibition of lactylation through β‑alanine reduced ALDOA K42 lactylation and ameliorated vascular remodeling in ALDOA-overexpressing rodent PH models. Translationally, pharmacological disruption of the ALDOA/γ-actin interaction by raltegravir suppressed cytoskeletal reorganization and YAP signaling, mitigating PH progression in both mouse and rat models.
sections.conclusion: AARS1-mediated ALDOA K42 lactylation drives pulmonary vascular remodeling through a mechanism independent of ALDOA's catalytic activity, promoting F-actin polymerization and YAP activation. Precision targeting of this modification selectively inhibits pathological signaling while preserving metabolic homeostasis, highlighting a translational potential for precision intervention in PH.

items.title: Long-Term Impact of Vutrisiran in Patients With TTR Amyloidosis With Cardiomyopathy: 1-Year Efficacy and Safety Outcomes From the HELIOS-B Open-Label Extension.

sections.objective: In HELIOS-B (A Study to Evaluate Vutrisiran in Patients With Transthyretin Amyloidosis With Cardiomyopathy), vutrisiran reduced the risk of all-cause mortality (ACM) and recurrent cardiovascular events and slowed disease progression measures versus placebo in patients with TTR (transthyretin) amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy after 33 to 36 months. We report the long-term efficacy and safety of vutrisiran from an ongoing open-label extension of HELIOS-B.
sections.methods: Patients who completed HELIOS-B could enroll in the open-label extension, continuing with vutrisiran 25 mg every 3 months (continuous vutrisiran) or, if previously receiving placebo, initiating vutrisiran 25 mg every 3 months (placebo/vutrisiran). Prespecified end points assessed in the open-label extension are the composite of ACM and cardiovascular events, ACM, Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire-Overall Summary score, New York Heart Association class, and NT-proBNP (N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide) and troponin I levels. Outcomes were assessed through month 48 in this analysis.
sections.results: Of 654 participants in HELIOS-B (vutrisiran, n=326; placebo, n=328), 478 completed double-blind treatment and 466 (vutrisiran, n=243; placebo, n=223) entered the open-label extension. In the continuous vutrisiran group, the risk of first cardiovascular event or ACM was reduced by 37% (hazard ratio, 0.63 [95% CI, 0.51, 0.79]; P=0.0001) and ACM by 37% (hazard ratio, 0.63 [95% CI, 0.46, 0.84]; P=0.0023) versus the placebo/vutrisiran group. Through month 48, patients in the continuous vutrisiran group had preserved health status and quality of life per Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire-Overall Summary score (least squares mean difference, 9.0 [95% CI, 5.3, 12.6]; P<0.0001) and more patients had improved or stable New York Heart Association class (odds ratio, 1.6 [95% CI, 1.1, 2.2]; P=0.0084) versus the placebo/vutrisiran group. Benefits in the continuous vutrisiran group were maintained for NT-proBNP and troponin I levels (adjusted geometric mean fold change ratios, 0.66 [95% CI, 0.58, 0.74]; P<0.0001; and 0.71 [95% CI, 0.64, 0.79]; P<0.0001, respectively) versus the placebo/vutrisiran group. Similar benefits were observed in the vutrisiran monotherapy population. No new safety signals were observed.
sections.conclusion: Long-term vutrisiran resulted in clinically meaningful benefits across mortality, cardiovascular events, cardiac biomarkers, functional status, and quality of life in patients with TTR amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy through month 48. Patients initially treated with vutrisiran had better outcomes than those first receiving placebo, highlighting the importance of early diagnosis and treatment in TTR amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy.

items.title: Impact of Undertreated Antithrombotic Therapy on Adverse Patient Outcomes: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association.
items.abstract: Antithrombotic therapy undertreatment includes omission, nonadherence, underdosing, and clinical circumstances that result in subtherapeutic antithrombotic levels. Antithrombotic undertreatment has profound implications for patient safety, public health, and healthcare costs. Due to deviation from evidence-based clinical practice, misperceptions of bleeding versus thrombotic risk, and inequities in healthcare access, many patients with atrial fibrillation, venous thromboembolism, or peripheral artery disease remain untreated or receive suboptimal anticoagulant dosing. Antithrombotic undertreatment has been shown to increase rates of ischemic stroke, systemic embolism, recurrent thrombosis, and mortality. Real-world data continue to highlight substantial gaps in care, which appear to be magnified in patients with inequity in social determinants of health. The emergence of antithrombotic stewardship, in concert with growing bodies of literature on antithrombotic agent underdosing, represents a transformative opportunity to address these gaps through structured, interprofessional, and evidence-based approaches. Through interdisciplinary collaboration, healthcare professionals are well positioned to enhance patient health and safety by recognizing and recommitting to reducing antithrombotic undertreatment.

items.title: Cardiovascular Disease Mortality by County, Race and/or Ethnic Population, United States, 2000-2019.

sections.objective: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains the leading cause of death and an important contributor to U.S. health disparities. In this study, the authors sought to assess county-level CVD mortality and trends by race and/or ethnicity as well as by detailed CVD cause of death.
sections.methods: We estimated age-standardized mortality rates (ASMRs) for 5 racial and/or ethnic groups (American Indian or Alaska Native [AIAN], Asian or Pacific Islander [Asian], Black or African American [Black], Hispanic or Latino [Latino], and White), 3,110 counties, 21 causes of CVD death, and 20 years (2000-2019) using small-area estimation methods and death certificate data from the U.S. National Vital Statistics System. Estimated mortality rates were adjusted for misreporting of race or ethnicity on death certificates and age-standardized to the 2010 census. Counties were classified into persistently high mortality, persistently low mortality, and intermediate strata based on age-adjusted CVD mortality rates, stratified by race and/or ethnicity.
sections.results: The ASMR for total CVD was 237.8 (95% uncertainty interval: 237.2-238.4) deaths per 100,000 in 2019. Mortality was highest for the Black population for total CVD and 12 of 17 detailed CVD causes, and lowest for the Asian population for total CVD and 13 of 17 detailed causes. From 2000 to 2019, mortality declined for total CVD and 12 of 17 detailed causes; however, mortality increased for 3 detailed causes. Mortality also varied widely among counties-much more than among states-both within and among racial and/or ethnic populations. Spatial mortality patterns varied considerably by CVD cause and by race and/or ethnicity.
sections.conclusion: While declining CVD mortality reflects meaningful clinical and public health progress, persistent and pervasive disparities demand solutions-oriented, place-informed research to drive further progress. Critically, these pre-Covid data establish a baseline essential for isolating Covid-era-attributable shifts from preexisting trends. These granular county-level data stratified by CVD cause, race, and/or ethnicity offer a scalable, repeatable framework for agencies to tailor health interventions and rigorously track disparities over time.

items.title: Intestinal Serotonergic Vagal Signaling as a Mediator of Microbiota-Induced Hypertension.

sections.objective: Hypertension is a pervasive global health challenge, impacting more than 1 billion individuals worldwide. Despite strides in therapeutic strategies, a significant proportion of patients remain resistant to the currently available therapies. Although conventional treatments predominantly focus on cardiac, renal, and cerebral targets, emerging research underscores the pivotal role of the gut and its microbiota. Yet, the precise mechanisms governing interactions between the gut microbiota and the host blood pressure remain unclear.
sections.methods: We combined fecal microbiota transplantation between normotensive and hypertensive rats, an intersectional genetic strategy in a serotonin receptor 3a (5HT3a) receptor Cre rat line to activate, ablate, and restore serotonin-sensing colonic vagal neurons, in vivo calcium imaging and radiotelemetric blood pressure recordings, and measurements of intestinal serotonin (5-hydroxytryptamine [5-HT]) and 5HT3a receptor signaling in rats and in colonic biopsies from normotensive and hypertensive human subjects (N=5 per group; 36 to 75 years of age).
sections.results: A marked decrease in both intestinal 5-HT and vagal 5HT3a receptor signaling was observed in hypertensive rats and humans, and in rats subjected to fecal microbiota transplantation from hypertensive rats. Leveraging the intersectional genetic strategy in a Cre rat line, we demonstrate that intestinal 5HT3a receptor vagal signaling is a crucial link between the gut microbiota and blood pressure homeostasis and that recovery of 5-HT signaling in colon-innervating vagal neurons can alleviate hypertension.
sections.conclusion: Here, we describe a neural host-microbiota interaction that is mediated by intestinal serotonin (5-HT) signaling via the vagal 5HT3a, which is crucial for maintenance of blood pressure homeostasis. This finding enhances our comprehension of hypertensive pathophysiology and unveils a promising new therapeutic target for combating resistant hypertension associated with gut dysbiosis.

items.title: Impaired Glycolysis Leads to Defective Efferocytosis and Impaired Plaque Resolution in Tet2 Clonal Hematopoiesis.

sections.objective: Clonal hematopoiesis (CH) arising from mutations in hematopoietic genes has been identified as an important risk factor for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. Despite the established role of some CH mutations in promoting atherosclerosis progression, their role in clinically relevant LDL (low-density lipoprotein) lowering-induced plaque remodeling or regression has not been extensively studied.
sections.methods: To assess the effects of TET2 (tet methylcytosine dioxygenase 2) CH on plaque resolution, we prepared control or chimeric Tet2+/- CH mice with conditional deletion of Tet2 in hematopoietic stem cells during LDL lowering-induced plaque remodeling. After establishing atherosclerosis by Western diet feeding for 12 weeks in Ldlr-/- mice, Tet2 was deleted by tamoxifen injection, and hypercholesterolemia was either normalized to simulate clinical lipid management, or mice were continued on the Western diet.
sections.results: Unlike control mice, Tet2+/- CH mice failed to significantly reduce necrotic core area or increase fibrous cap thickness and showed impaired macrophage efferocytosis during LDL lowering. Single-cell RNA sequencing and gene set enrichment analysis of aortic cell populations revealed that Tet2 deficient monocyte/macrophage populations were defective in glycolysis, phagocytosis, and actin polymerization. Tet2-deficient bone marrow-derived macrophages and Tet2+/- induced pluripotent stem cell-derived human macrophages showed defective ability to sustain continuing rounds of efferocytosis. Bone marrow-derived macrophages displayed reduced apoptotic cell binding and internalization and impaired activity of Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome protein and SCAR (suppressor of cyclic AMP receptor) homolog complex mediated actin polymerization. We linked these defects to reduced anaerobic glycolysis and lactate levels and rescued them by lactate supplementation or by treatment with the HIF-1α (hypoxia-inducible factor 1α) activator molidustat. Molidustat treatment reversed the defects in necrotic core and fibrous cap formation during LDL lowering-induced plaque remodeling in Tet2+/- CH mice. Reduced plasma lactate levels were also shown in TET2 clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential carriers in the UK Biobank.
sections.conclusion: Our data identify impaired efferocytosis and glycolysis-lactate-actin polymerization pathways in advanced atherosclerosis as potential therapeutic targets to induce proresolving restructuring of the plaque immune cells and to promote beneficial atherosclerosis remodeling in subjects with TET2 CH.

items.title: Macrotroponin Complexes and Risk of Cardiovascular Events.

sections.objective: Cardiac troponin is increasingly used for cardiovascular risk prediction. While abnormal values often reflect subclinical cardiovascular disease, they can be raised due to interference, where antibodies influence the assay or clearance of troponin from the circulation by forming macrotroponin complexes. The frequency of macrotroponins and its association with future risk are unknown.
sections.methods: In a general population cohort, participants with both cardiac troponin I and T measurements available (n=19 499, median 49 [25th-75th percentile, 36-58] years of age, 58.3% women) were categorized into 3 groups: no myocardial injury (neither cardiac troponin I or T was elevated), suspected macrotroponin (either cardiac troponin was elevated and discordant with a >3-fold difference in concentration), and myocardial injury (either cardiac troponin was elevated without discordance). Macrotroponin complex formation was verified in a subset of samples (n=203) using immunoglobulin depletion and ultracentrifugation. Associations with future myocardial infarction, ischemic stroke, or cardiovascular death were evaluated using Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for known cardiovascular risk factors. The generalizability of our findings was determined through replication in a second general population cohort study.
sections.results: Elevated cardiac troponin I was present in 1% (193 of 19 499) of participants and elevated cardiac troponin T in 6% (1159 of 19 499). Among those, 48% and 57% were discordant, respectively. Biochemical testing attributed 92.5% of discordant troponin I and 15.4% of discordant troponin T to macrotroponin complexes. Participants with myocardial injury were at increased risk of future cardiovascular events compared with those without (cardiac troponin I: adjusted hazard ratio [HR], 2.90 [95% CI, 1.99-4.22]; cardiac troponin T: adjusted HR, 1.99 [95% CI, 1.63-2.42]), whereas those with suspected macrotroponin had similar risk as those without elevated values for suspected macrotroponin I (adjusted HR, 1.59 [95% CI, 0.94-2.70]) and T (adjusted HR, 1.27 [95% CI, 1.00-1.61]). Findings were similar in the replication cohort.
sections.conclusion: Assay interference due to macrotroponin complex formation is common in individuals with elevated cardiac troponin concentrations in the general population, particularly for cardiac troponin I. This has important implications for the use of cardiac troponin testing for cardiovascular risk assessment in the general population.

items.title: Clinical Considerations for the Care of the Tactical Athlete With Cardiovascular Abnormalities: A Scientific Statement From the American College of Cardiology and the American Heart Association.

sections.objective: The American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association Scientific Statement, "Clinical Considerations for the Care of the Tactical Athlete With Cardiovascular Abnormalities," was written to provide guidance and education for clinicians caring for the tactical athlete (ie, firefighters, law enforcement officers, military) with cardiovascular disease or risk for cardiovascular disease, and for the organizations overseeing the care and wellness of these athletes. The considerations are shaped by the interaction between occupational demands and fit for full duty assessments, including risk discussions about how a cardiovascular event in a tactical athlete could impact teammates' well-being, community safety, and overall mission success.
sections.methods: This scientific statement is organized into 11 sections focused on cardiovascular disease processes and other topics that are relevant when considering the potential risks and benefits of performing tasks specific to the tactical athlete. Task forces, comprised of experts in tactical athlete domains, sports cardiology, and the respective topics covered, were assigned to each section, and specific "Clinical Considerations Tables" for clinicians to reference were prepared. Comprehensive literature reviews and an emphasis on tactical athlete-focused data, as available, were integral in the writing of all clinical considerations presented. The framework mirrors that of the recently published, "Clinical Considerations for Competitive Sports Participation for Athletes With Cardiovascular Abnormalities: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association and American College of Cardiology."
sections.other: The specific sections in this document include: Section 1: Tactical Tasks Classification; Section 2: The Tactical Athlete Preparticipation Cardiac Evaluation; Section 3: Ethical and Legal Aspects of Tactical Clinical Management; Section 4: Genetic Cardiomyopathies; Section 5: Myocarditis and Other Acquired Cardiac Conditions; Section 6: Congenital Heart Disease; Section 7: Aortopathy, Bicuspid Aortic Valve, and Spontaneous Coronary Artery Dissection; Section 8: Syncope, SCA, Arrhythmias, and Devices; Section 9: Cardiac Channelopathies; Section 10: Older Tactical Athlete; Section 11: Environmental Exposures, PED/S, and Additional Cardiac Conditions and Considerations. Each section provides a summary detailing the rationale for key clinical considerations and the respective Clinical Considerations Table(s).

items.title: A Coordinated Community- and Family-Based Intervention to Control Blood Pressure in Rural China: A Cluster-Randomized Trial.

sections.objective: Current hypertension prevention strategies predominantly focus on identifying and treating individuals with established hypertension. Whether a coordinated community- and family-based intervention can shift the population distribution of systolic blood pressure (SBP) remains uncertain. The purpose of this study was to evaluate whether a coordinated, community- and family-centered intervention could shift the distribution of SBP at the population level in rural China.
sections.methods: In this cluster-randomized trial conducted in rural China, village clusters comprising adults aged 40 to 80 years, irrespective of blood pressure (BP) level or hypertension status, were randomly assigned (1:1) to a multifaceted intervention or usual care. The intervention included community instructor support, potassium-enriched low-sodium salt substitute, home BP and weight monitoring, physical activity promotion, and facilitation of antihypertensive treatment during an initial 6-month active intervention phase, followed by continued digital BP monitoring support through 12 months. Office BP was measured at baseline and at 6 and 12 months by trained staff independent of the intervention team. The primary outcome was the between-group difference in change in SBP from baseline to 6 months. Analyses followed the intention-to-treat principle using linear mixed-effects regression models.
sections.results: A total of 80 village clusters, comprising 8,001 participants, underwent randomization. Baseline mean SBP was 133.1 mm Hg in the intervention group and 131.4 mm Hg in the control group. At 6 months, mean SBP fell by 6.0 mm Hg in the intervention group and increased by 5.1 mm Hg in the control group, resulting in an adjusted between-group difference of -10.7 mm Hg (95% CI: -11.8 to -9.6 mm Hg). BP <130/80 mm Hg was achieved in 46.2% of participants in the intervention group vs 23.6% in the control group (adjusted OR: 5.3; 95% CI: 4.3-6.6). At 12 months, the adjusted between-group difference in SBP was -3.7 mm Hg (95% CI: -4.9 to -2.6 mm Hg). Serious adverse events occurred in 2.8% of participants in the intervention group and 2.3% in the control group.
sections.conclusion: In rural China, a coordinated community- and family-based intervention significantly shifted the population distribution of SBP toward lower levels over 6 months. Attenuation of the treatment effect over time suggests that sustained population BP reduction may require ongoing implementation infrastructure and continued community support. (Effect of Healthy Family Program on Population Blood Pressure; NCT06427096).

items.title: Cardiovascular Health Change Patterns After Multifaceted Antihypertensive Intervention and Cardiovascular Outcomes: A Post Hoc Analysis of CRHCP Trial.

sections.objective: Cardiovascular health (CVH), as defined by the American Heart Association, provides a multidimensional framework for cardiovascular risk assessment. An increasing number of studies have developed intervention strategies based on CVH metrics. However, the multidimensional health change patterns resulting from these interventions and their relationship with clinical outcomes remain unclear. The purposes of this study were to characterize patterns of change in CVH after intervention and to examine how multidimensional response domains derived from Life's Simple 7 (LS7) components relate to subsequent cardiovascular outcomes.
sections.methods: This post hoc analysis of the China Rural Hypertension Control Project included 26,700 participants. The intervention consisted of intensive blood pressure (BP) management delivered by nonphysician community health care providers, targeting <130/80 mm Hg. Changes in CVH over 0-36 months were longitudinally characterized across the LS7 components and grouped into BP, metabolic, and behavioral domains. Associations between domain-specific change patterns and subsequent cardiovascular outcomes (36-48 months) were evaluated using Cox proportional hazards models.
sections.results: Among 26,700 participants (age 62.5 ± 9.0 years; 63.0% women), the intervention improved LS7 scores at 36 months (net difference: 0.52; 95% CI: 0.38-0.66), with cardiovascular risk reduction observed among participants with improved CVH (HR: 0.71; 95% CI: 0.54-0.89). Longitudinal analyses showed sustained separation in BP between groups, with only modest and less-differentiated changes in other components. Across multidomain patterns, the greatest reduction in cardiovascular risk was observed among participants with BP improvement plus concurrent behavioral or metabolic gains (HR: 0.57; 95% CI: 0.30-0.84), followed by BP improvement alone (HR: 0.76; 95% CI: 0.55-0.98), with no significant benefit in other patterns. Net benefit analyses showed a consistent gradient across patterns. Mediation analyses indicated that BP accounted for the majority of the observed effect (67.5%), with modest contributions from behavioral (8.0%) and minimal contributions from metabolic domains. Results were consistent across sensitivity analyses.
sections.conclusion: In this large community-based randomized trial, a scalable intervention delivered by nonphysician providers reduced cardiovascular risk, with the benefit primarily driven by BP, alongside modest contributions from behavioral and metabolic domains. This asymmetry highlights heterogeneous, domain-specific responses and provides a quantitative framework for understanding how multifaceted interventions translate into cardiovascular outcomes. (China Rural Hypertension Control Project (CRHC); NCT03527719).

items.title: Non-invasive oral magnetoelectric vagus nerve neuromodulation for Parkinson's disease therapy.
items.abstract: Vagus nerve stimulation has shown promising neuroprotective and anti-inflammatory effects in progressive neurodegenerative disorders such as Parkinson's disease. However, its invasive nature introduces procedural and device-related risks. Here we introduce a magnetoelectric particulate system for oral delivery and non-invasive vagus nerve stimulation through the gut. The system comprises a magneto-responsive nickel ferrite core and a piezoelectric barium titanate shell, conjugated with capsaicin to specifically target TRPV1 receptors, ensuring effective adherence to the stomach lining after oral administration. Upon magnetic field stimulation, the particles generate electrical pulses that activate vagal afferent fibres, engaging the nucleus tractus solitarius in the brainstem via the gut-brain axis. This activation enhances norepinephrine production in the locus coeruleus and dopamine synthesis in the substantia nigra. Vagal efferent activation triggers the cholinergic anti-inflammatory pathway, mitigating both neuroinflammation and systemic inflammation. This non-invasive approach demonstrates potential for alleviating motor symptoms and non-motor anxiety in Parkinson's disease, offering valuable insights into its mechanisms and clinical applications.

items.title: Estimating the population-level non-respiratory burden of severe influenza: a systematic review of methods and estimates.
items.abstract: Influenza is widely recognised as a respiratory infection, although the condition can also exacerbate or trigger serious non-respiratory outcomes that are often overlooked in burden assessments. Previous reviews have separately evaluated how methodological choices affect influenza-associated mortality and hospitalisation estimates and have covered non-respiratory outcomes in part, although these studies were restricted to select causes or severe outcomes, specific populations, or particular geographical settings. A more comprehensive synthesis focused specifically on severe non-respiratory influenza burden has been missing. To address this gap, we conducted a systematic review of 238 studies from 52 countries or regions examining both the burden of severe influenza beyond respiratory disease and the estimation methods used. We found that non-respiratory outcomes represent a substantial component of the total influenza burden, with a pronounced age gradient disproportionately affecting older adults (≥65 years). Cardiovascular events were particularly notable, contributing to more than 50 deaths and 60 hospitalisations per 100 000 older adults. Burden estimates also varied by analytical method, cause, and study period, and most evidence was concentrated in high-income settings, leaving important geographical gaps. Our findings highlight that influenza burden assessments and prevention strategies should extend beyond respiratory presentations, particularly for older populations, and emphasise upon the need for standardised methods and broader geographical coverage to generate estimates that are more comparable across studies and settings that better inform public health policy and resource allocation.

items.title: Could the next pandemic be fungal and could we respond effectively? From plausible pathways to operational preparedness.
items.abstract: Fungal diseases cause substantial morbidity and mortality worldwide, yet they have been persistently neglected in pandemic preparedness plans, largely because no sustained human-to-human fungal pandemic has been documented to date. However, multidisciplinary evidence challenges the assumption that fungi are irrelevant to pandemic risk. Wildlife fungal pandemics show that mycoses can emerge on a global scale with catastrophic and irreversible consequences. Moreover, climate change is narrowing the mammalian thermal barrier against fungi, favouring heat-tolerant species, reshaping their global distribution, and thus facilitating zoonotic spillover. Rising human susceptibility-driven by ageing populations, immunomodulatory therapies, and increasingly complex health care-is intersecting with a substantial therapeutic gap, characterised by the absence of licensed vaccines, a limited range of antifungal agents, and increasing antimicrobial resistance. In this Personal View, we move beyond a synthesis of evidence to propose an operational framework for fungal pandemic preparedness, outlining plausible routes to pandemic-scale impact and the surveillance, diagnostic, therapeutic, One Health, and outbreak-response capacities needed to detect and contain emerging fungal threats before they become unmanageable.

items.title: Presentation, management, and outcomes of ectopic Cushing syndrome: an international, multicentre, retrospective, cohort study.

sections.objective: Ectopic Cushing syndrome is a rare condition with scarce outcome data. We sought to characterise its course and determinants of complications and mortality.
sections.methods: In this international, multicentre, retrospective, cohort study, 49 high-volume endocrine referral centres across Asia, Europe, North America, South America, and New Zealand identified consecutive eligible patients. We included patients with a clinical diagnosis of ectopic Cushing syndrome, defined by expert adjudication at the treating institution with at least one of the following criteria: inferior petrosal sinus sampling or dynamic testing supportive of ectopic Cushing syndrome, biochemical remission of hypercortisolism following treatment of the ectopic Cushing syndrome source (surgical excision, radiotherapy, or cryoablation), evidence of a non-metastatic tumoural source of ectopic Cushing syndrome, either on initial or subsequent imaging, or evidence of a metastatic tumoural source of ectopic Cushing syndrome either on imaging or from chart notes. Data collection was completed between May 31, 2024 and April 22, 2025. Clinical features, biochemical severity, management, complications, and mortality were assessed. The primary outcome was Cushing syndrome-related mortality (investigator-adjudicated). Secondary outcomes were overall mortality and incidence of complications. Outcomes were stratified based on biochemical remission and timeline since diagnosis. Early (within 6 months of diagnosis) and late (>6 months after diagnosis) outcomes were analysed using landmark methods.
sections.results: Among 1463 patients (median age 51 years [IQR 37-64; range 3-87], 824 [56·3%] women, 639 [43·7%] men, and 1021 [69·8%] of White race), 836 (57·1%) had metastatic disease. Severe hypercortisolism (1204 [91·1%] of 1321) and hypokalaemia (1111 [79·4%] of 1399) were common. Median duration of follow-up was 57 months (IQR 19-124). Cushing syndrome-related death occurred in 196 (13·4%) patients. 626 (42·8%) patients died overall. Infection occurred in 464 (31·7%) patients, venous thromboembolism in 124 (8·5%), cardiovascular events in 93 (6·4%), and cerebrovascular events in 37 (2·5%). Achievement of complete biochemical remission within 6 months of diagnosis was independently associated with lower risk of late complications (adjusted HR 0·55 [95% CI 0·38-0·80]) and Cushing syndrome-related mortality (0·49 [0·27-0·89]), whereas no association was observed with non-Cushing syndrome-related mortality.
sections.conclusion: Outcomes in ectopic Cushing syndrome are driven by early control of hypercortisolism. Failure to achieve remission within 6 months is associated with markedly worse complications and mortality, supporting ectopic Cushing syndrome as a time-critical endocrine emergency.

items.title: Acquired cytomegalovirus in children: pathogen, bystander, or immune trainer?
items.abstract: Cytomegalovirus (CMV) is one of the most common infections worldwide, with acquisition occurring predominantly in early childhood (younger than 5 years). Although congenital CMV is a recognised cause of neurodevelopmental impairment, the consequences of postnatally acquired CMV in children remain poorly defined and are often assumed to be benign. However, accumulating evidence suggests that acquired CMV infection is biologically active even when clinically silent, with the capacity to shape immune ontogeny, influence immune responses to other pathogens and vaccines, and alter health trajectories across the life course. In this Review, we examine the epidemiology, transmission pathways, immune responses, and clinical consequences of acquired CMV infection in childhood. We synthesise evidence to evaluate whether acquired CMV acts as a driver of pathology, a neutral bystander, or a beneficial immune trainer. The effects of CMV are highly context-dependent, determined by the timing of acquisition, host immune maturity, maternal health, co-infections, and broader social and environmental factors. Evidence of harm is strongest in infants with heightened biological or contextual risk, such as infants born preterm and those living with or exposed to HIV, whereas effects in children who are immunocompetent are heterogeneous and often clinically silent. Acquired CMV should be understood as a context-dependent immune modifier rather than a uniformly benign or pathogenic infection. This reframing of acquired CMV has important implications for policy and research. Universal intervention is unlikely to be appropriate; instead, targeted CMV prevention and treatment strategies for populations at high risk of CMV infection and severe disease integrated into maternal and child health programmes could offer the greatest benefit. Defining high-risk populations and critical windows for intervention should be prioritised to translate emerging evidence into improvements in childhood morbidity and equity.

items.title: Intracellular Staphylococcus aureus in human infections: evidence from clinical specimens.
items.abstract: Staphylococcus aureus is a major human pathogen causing extensive morbidity and mortality. In vitro and animal studies show that S aureus can invade and survive within host cells. Such intracellular reservoirs might impair antibiotic and immune clearance, yet their clinical relevance in humans remains controversial. Here, we review 33 human studies published between 1984 and 2025 that assess the occurrence of intracellular S aureus across diverse disease conditions. We critically evaluated the methods used to detect intracellular S aureus in human biopsies and evidence across different tissues and diseases. Although the strength of evidence varies across studies, the overall findings strongly suggest the presence of S aureus within diverse human cell types. These findings could have important implications for diagnosis, treatment, and prevention. We identify key knowledge gaps, including the relative proportions of intracellular and extracellular S aureus, viability of intracellular bacteria, and persistence of these bacteria during antibiotic exposure. Thus, our analysis highlights intracellular states as a relevant part of S aureus biology in human infections and identifies future research directions.

items.title: Frailty as a determinant of mRNA vaccine efficacy.
items.abstract: Frailty, an age-related state of increased vulnerability, is associated with greater susceptibility to infection and impaired vaccine response. In this Review, we examine how frailty-associated immunosenescence, including altered haematopoiesis, chronic inflammation, and dysfunction of innate and adaptive immune responses, can affect the immunogenicity, efficacy, and safety of lipid nanoparticle mRNA vaccines. Evidence from COVID-19 lipid nanoparticle mRNA vaccines and other vaccines suggests that people living with frailty can mount weaker or less durable responses than non-frail peers, although findings remain heterogeneous and frailty-specific evidence is scarce. The high customisability of lipid nanoparticle mRNA platforms creates opportunities for frailty-tailored vaccination. We discuss optimisation of lipid nanoparticle composition, targeting and dosing, mRNA cargo and combination-vaccine approaches, alongside host-directed measures addressing comorbidities, nutrition, and immune dysfunction. Integrating frailty into vaccine design, evaluation, and deployment could support safer, more effective, and more individualised vaccination strategies for older adults.

items.title: Epiblast complementation enables generation of live offspring from pluripotent stem cells.
items.abstract: Blastocyst complementation enables the generation of donor pluripotent stem cell (PSC)-derived tissues in vivo, but its application has largely been limited to individual organs. Here, we establish epiblast complementation, a robust strategy for generating mice from donor PSCs. By creating an empty developmental niche in the host epiblast, we show that both wild-type and genetically modified naive PSCs can fully replace the host epiblast, contribute to all epiblast-derived tissues, and generate live offspring. Formative PSCs can also fully reconstitute the epiblast and support development to term, demonstrating developmental potential comparable to that of naive PSCs. Notably, a single naive PSC is sufficient to reconstitute the epiblast and give rise to live offspring. Together, these findings establish epiblast complementation as a functional assay for assessing PSC developmental potential and provide a strategy for generating genetically defined animals directly from cultured PSCs.

items.title: Subsistence transition preceded population turnover in the eastern Colombian Andes.
items.abstract: The Altiplano Cundiboyacense in the eastern Colombian Andes preserves one of the Americas' most continuous archaeological sequences, recording cultural and demographic change. We generated genome-wide data from 212 individuals spanning over 7,000 years, including early-middle and middle Holocene hunter-gatherers, initial late Holocene groups with mixed economies and the earliest isotopic evidence of maize consumption, and increasingly sedentary Herrera and Muisca populations. Individuals predating the Herrera Period form a lineage that persisted for five millennia, structured by drift in small groups without external gene flow. Two individuals dating ∼2,800 years before present (BP) retain autochthonous ancestry while showing isotopic signatures consistent with maize consumption, decoupling subsistence change from population replacement. The emergence of Herrera culture ∼2,200 BP coincided with a sharp genetic break by ∼2,000 BP, which reflects migration by people descended from admixture ∼4,000 BP between groups with Chibchan- and Amazonian-Andean-related ancestries. Herrera and Muisca Period individuals show north-south genetic substructure paralleling archaeological differentiation.

items.title: Convergent genomic evolution of human gut bacteria along an industrialization gradient.
items.abstract: Whether human-associated environments drive adaptive genome evolution in gut commensal bacteria remains largely unknown. Here, we investigate how genomic adaptation in gut bacteria differs between industrialized and non-industrialized human populations. We generated a collection of isolate genomes spanning diverse host geographies, lifestyles, species, and strains. We first found that, compared with metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs), paired isolate genomes recover more functional elements and signals of horizontal gene transfer (HGT). Leveraging isolate genomes from multiple species, we find that strains from industrialized hosts experience an expansion of proteome size and harbor greater pangenome fluidity, driven by recent HGT events. Gene- and variant-level analyses reveal convergent patterns of lifestyle-specific adaptation in functions that are critical for ecological adaptation, such as the stress response, cell-envelope remodeling, and central metabolism. Our results demonstrate that industrialization drives convergent genome evolution in gut bacteria, providing a framework for understanding the mechanisms of microbial adaptation to rapidly changing human environments.

items.title: TECR palmitoylation triggers a necrotic cell death program driving acute liver injury.
items.abstract: Acute liver injury caused by drug toxicity or immune activation remains a major clinical challenge with limited mechanistic understanding and few effective therapies. Here, we identify a previously unrecognized form of regulated cell death driven by palmitoylation of the endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-resident enzyme trans-2,3-enoyl-coenzyme A (CoA) reductase (TECR). We show that multi-site palmitoylation of TECR, redundantly catalyzed by the palmitoyl acyltransferases ZDHHC5 and ZDHHC2 and dynamically reversed by the depalmitoylase ABHD10, activates PERK-dependent ER stress signaling to trigger cell death. This cell death pathway is a TECR-dependent, palmitoylation-induced, ER stress-mediated necrotic cell death program (TPNCD). TPNCD contributes to liver injury in mouse models of acetaminophen- and concanavalin A-induced hepatotoxicity and is attenuated by hepatocyte-specific TECR ablation or by pharmacological inhibition of palmitoylation or ER stress signaling. Together, these findings establish TPNCD as a distinct, necrotic cell death pathway underlying acute liver injury and highlight new therapeutic entry points for hepatoprotection.

items.title: Industrialization drives convergent microbiome and host physiological shifts in the human metaorganism.
items.abstract: Understanding how industrialization reshapes the human metaorganism requires integrating microbiome ecology with host physiology across globally diverse populations. Here, we generate multivariate data from the Global Microbiome Conservancy cohort, including gut microbiome, immunoglobulin A (IgA) sequencing, host genotyping, diet, lifestyle, and fecal biomarker profiles, to investigate host-microbiome interactions across gradients of industrialization and geography. We show that industrialization is associated with homogenized microbial compositions, reduced microbial diversity, and lower community stability, independent of host confounders. We further show that industrialization is linked to elevated markers of gut stress, increased IgA secretion, and altered patterns of IgA-bacteria interactions.
