sections.conclusion: This current study reports that bronchiectasis prevalence continues to increase in the US compared with previous studies, with a consistently higher prevalence in females and Asians, and that a lower proportion of individuals have CF-related bronchiectasis compared with non-CF-related bronchiectasis.
sections.other: What is the prevalence of bronchiectasis in the United States?

items.title: Age-dependent structural evolution of a functional amyloid contributes to memory impairment in Drosophila.
items.abstract: Cryogenic electron microscopy has revealed endpoint structures of ex vivo amyloid filaments, but how amyloids assemble and evolve in living organisms-and how these transitions affect physiology-remains poorly understood. Here, we map the age-dependent structural landscape of Orb2 amyloid, a synaptic translation regulator required for long-term memory, across the adult lifespan of Drosophila melanogaster. By determining multiple Orb2 amyloid structures, we uncover a dynamic, age-linked progression of amyloid states. Translation-promoting assemblies predominate early in life, whereas aging shifts the Orb2 amyloid ensemble toward structurally distinct, destabilization-resistant assemblies with reduced translational activity, coinciding with memory impairment. Manipulating memory-related chaperones in the brain shifts Orb2 toward youthful, translation-promoting states and improves memory in old flies; conversely, shifting Orb2 toward aged-like, translation-deficient states in young adults is associated with premature memory impairment. These findings define an in vivo trajectory of amyloid evolution and link amyloid structural dynamics to synaptic translation and memory.

items.title: Pediatric Endothelial Keratoplasty: A Modified Delphi Consensus by the EKLG Study Group on Indications, Surgical Techniques, and Postoperative Care.

sections.objective: To identify areas of consensus among global experts on the clinical management of pediatric endothelial keratoplasty (EK), including patient selection, timing, preoperative evaluation, technique selection, intraoperative standards, and postoperative care, and to provide a practical framework for surgeons earlier in their pediatric EK learning curve.
sections.methods: Modified Delphi-based global consensus study. International ophthalmologists with expertise in endothelial keratoplasty and pediatric corneal diseases. A series of consensus statements on pediatric EK were developed from iterative rounds of structured questions and statements posed to a panel of experts. Two rounds of asynchronous electronic questionnaires were followed by a structured hybrid discussion of unresolved items. Experts responded anonymously to statements assessing consensus and to revised items addressing indications, contraindications, timing, preoperative workup, technique selection, intraoperative standards, and postoperative management. Results are reported using item-specific denominators because occasional non-response occurred across the survey items.
sections.results: The consensus supported pediatric EK for congenital hereditary endothelial dystrophy, aphakic or pseudophakic corneal edema, persistent corneal edema in congenital glaucoma, X-linked endothelial corneal dystrophy, iatrogenic endothelial decompensation, and trauma-related decompensation. EK was inappropriate for severe anterior segment dysgenesis with keratolenticular or extensive iridocorneal adhesions. In Round 2, experts further endorsed EK for failed penetrating keratoplasty due to endothelial failure, congenital glaucoma with visually significant Haab's striae, and forceps injury involving the visual axis. There was a consensus that the timing of intervention should be guided primarily by amblyopia risk rather than by a specific age cut off. Essential preoperative assessments included examination under anesthesia, B-scan ultrasonography, anterior segment optical coherence tomography, intraocular pressure measurement, ultrasound biomicroscopy, and refraction. Experts agreed that ultrathin-DSAEK and DSAEK are the predominant techniques, whereas DMEK is currently selectively reserved, usually for older children with uncomplicated anterior segment anatomy. Preferred intraoperative principles included air tamponade, anterior chamber maintenance, and donor graft under-sizing relative to the corneal diameter. Postoperative recommendations included early intraocular pressure assessment, topical corticosteroid therapy for > 6 months, regular monitoring for steroid response, selective contact lens use, and individualized long-term follow-up.
sections.conclusion: The consensus statements provide globally endorsed recommendations for the clinical management of pediatric EK. These guidelines are relevant for corneal specialists providing a practical framework to benchmark practice, reduce variability, and guide future multicenter investigations.
sections.other: Consensus was defined as ≥70% agreement among the experts. Agreement between 60% and 69.9% was considered to be near consensus.

items.title: Corneal versus refractive surgically induced astigmatism: vector analysis of their dissociation and implications for toric IOL planning.

sections.objective: To determine whether tomographically measured surgically induced astigmatism (SIA) is reflected in the manifest refraction, and whether the ocular residual astigmatism (ORA) precedes surgery and is stable per eye.
sections.methods: Single-center, longitudinal, comparative vector analysis. Eyes underwent non-toric intraocular lens (IOL) or phakic implantable collamer lens (ICL) implantation. Total corneal refractive power (Pentacam) and manifest subjective refractive astigmatism at the corneal plane were expressed as Cartesian double-angle power vectors before and 3 months after surgery, yielding tomographic SIA (tSIA), refractive SIA (rSIA), their vector difference ΔSIA, and the pre- and postoperative ORA. Each SIA was decomposed into its flattening effect and torque at the incision meridian. Centroids were tested against the null by eye side.
sections.results: Of 290 eyes (256 IOL; 34 ICL), tSIA magnitude was small (IOL 0.47D; ICL 0.34-0.39D) with centroids near null. ΔSIA had a large mean magnitude (IOL 0.74-0.88D) but a near-origin centroid, significant only in IOL right eyes. Mean corneal flattening effect (+0.008D right, +0.140D left eyes) did not predict its refractive counterpart. ORA did not differ between cohorts (-0.11D, 95%-CI -0.25 to +0.02) and remained significant postoperatively, yet per eye only half the offset persisted in phakic and less in pseudophakic eyes.
sections.conclusion: The per-eye tSIA was uncorrelated with the refractive SIA and carried no systematic direction, as power vectors or flattening effect, which stayed below a quarter of a toric cylinder step. ORA preceded surgery and remained systematically stable. Individually measured tSIA has only limited value for toric IOL planning.

items.title: Thoracic Outlet Syndrome in Athletes: A Narrative Review of Diagnostic Challenges, Management Strategies, and Return-to-Play Outcomes.

sections.objective: Thoracic outlet syndrome (TOS) is a compression disorder involving the brachial plexus, subclavian artery, or subclavian vein within the thoracic outlet. Athletes represent a distinct population in whom delayed diagnosis may result in career-threatening injuries. This review aimed to: (i) identify diagnostic pitfalls in athletes not captured by conventional provocative tests; (ii) evaluate conservative and operative management by TOS subtype; (iii) synthesize return-to-play (RTP) rates, timelines, and clearance criteria; and (iv) highlight methodological limitations and propose minimum reporting standards for future athlete-specific studies.
sections.methods: PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Google Scholar were searched from inception to July 2026 using controlled vocabulary and free-text terms for TOS, its subtypes, Paget-Schroetter syndrome, and athletic populations. Reference lists were hand-searched. Studies addressing TOS diagnosis, classification, pathophysiology, management, or RTP in athletes were eligible regardless of design, reflecting limited randomized evidence. Journal legitimacy was screened using the Kscien's list.
sections.results: nTOS is the predominant form in athletes and usually improves with 4-6 months of rehabilitation, whereas refractory cases may require surgery. vTOS/Paget-Schroetter syndrome requires urgent thrombolysis and early first-rib resection; aTOS is rare but limb-threatening and requires prompt surgery. Mixed presentations occur in up to 23% of surgical cases.
sections.conclusion: Outcomes are favorable with subtype-specific diagnosis and objective RTP criteria. However, evidence is limited by retrospective, single-center studies with pooled subtypes, inconsistent RTP definitions, and selective reporting. Prospective, sport-specific studies using standardized outcomes are needed.

items.title: Acute-on-chronic liver failure: A global multisociety consensus on definitions.
items.abstract: The acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF) multisociety harmonisation initiative represents a global collaborative effort to establish a unified, evidence-based framework for the definition, diagnosis, grading, and management of ACLF. Building on the strengths of existing regional definitions and integrating diverse international perspectives, this consensus provides a pragmatic, globally applicable foundation for clinical practice, research, and education. It also establishes a common framework for patient stratification, organ dysfunction and failure assessment, critical care management, liver transplantation, and the design of future phase II/III trials. Standardised, regulatory-aligned endpoints are expected to improve cross-study comparability, strengthen collaboration, and accelerate development of effective ACLF therapies.
items.authors: European Association for the Study of the Liver (EASL)

items.title: Intralesional cemiplimab for patients with early-stage cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma: Results from a dose-escalation study with expansion cohorts.

sections.objective: Non-surgical treatment of patients with early-stage (1-2 cm diameter) cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (CSCC) remains an unmet need. This study investigates low-dose intralesional cemiplimab for these patients. The primary objective was safety of low-dose intralesional cemiplimab. Efficacy was a secondary objective.
sections.methods: This was an open-label, phase 1 pilot study with dose escalation and expansion cohorts (NCT03889912). One lesion was injected per patient. Cemiplimab was initially administered at 5, 15, and 44 mg weekly, for 12 weeks. Subsequently, Expansion Cohorts A and B received 5 mg intralesional cemiplimab weekly or every 2 weeks, respectively, for 6 weeks. Visual response assessments were performed at Weeks 7 and 13, and surgery at Week 13.
sections.results: Across 41 patients, cemiplimab showed an acceptable safety profile. In Expansion Cohorts A and B, treatment-emergent adverse events were all grade ≤2. Week 13 visual and pathologic complete response rates were both 58.3% in Cohort A and 41.7% and 66.7%, respectively, in Cohort B.
sections.conclusion: Low-dose intralesional cemiplimab demonstrated efficacy against early-stage CSCC, with an acceptable safety profile. These data support further study of 5 mg intralesional cemiplimab weekly.
sections.other: The small number of participants limits generalizability. Intralesional cemiplimab administration may have been variable.

items.title: 52-Week Safety and Disease Control With Ruxolitinib Cream in Children Aged 2 to 11 Years With Atopic Dermatitis: Results From the Phase 3 TRuE-AD3 Study.

sections.objective: Ruxolitinib (selective Janus kinase [JAK]1/JAK2 inhibitor) cream demonstrated efficacy and safety vs vehicle during 8 weeks of continuous use in a phase 3 study of children with atopic dermatitis (AD). To evaluate long-term safety (LTS) and disease control with as-needed ruxolitinib cream use in children.
sections.methods: Children aged 2-11 years with mild-to-moderate AD initially randomized to ruxolitinib cream (0.75% or 1.5%) in the 8-week study continued the same twice-daily (BID) regimen for an additional 44 weeks but only applied cream as needed BID; patients initially on vehicle were rerandomized (1:1) to apply either ruxolitinib cream strength as needed. Safety and disease control were assessed.
sections.results: No new safety signals emerged among children who applied ruxolitinib cream in the LTS period (N=282). Application site reactions were infrequent (1.1%), and no serious treatment-related adverse events were observed. Among patients initially randomized to ruxolitinib cream (0.75%/1.5%), disease control was maintained to Week 52 (Investigator's Global Assessment score 0/1, 79.5%/72.3%; affected body surface area, 2.0%/1.9%).
sections.conclusion: Ruxolitinib cream applied as needed over 44 weeks was well tolerated and demonstrated disease control in children aged 2-11 years, consistent with findings in adolescents and adults.
sections.other: No vehicle control in LTS period.

items.title: Contralateral Major Amputation Following Diabetes- and Peripheral Artery Disease-Related Limb Loss: A Systematic Review and Pooled Meta-Analysis.

sections.objective: Major amputation remains a devastating and understudied outcome in patients with peripheral artery disease (PAD), chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI), and diabetes mellitus (DM)-related limb disease. Although modern vascular care emphasizes index and symptomatic limb surveillance, the population-level risk of non-index limb (NIL) major amputation remains incompletely defined. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to quantify NIL major amputation incidence and evaluate factors associated with contralateral limb loss.
sections.methods: A systematic search of PubMed (MEDLINE), Embase, and Scopus through January 2026 was conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines. Studies reporting contralateral above- or below-knee amputation in adults with PAD, CLTI, DM-related limb disease, or prior ipsilateral major amputation were included. Single-arm random-effects meta-analysis using the restricted maximum likelihood (REML) estimator was performed with log-transformed effect sizes. Subgroup analyses were conducted by clinical phenotype, geographic location, study era, and DM prevalence. Secondary outcomes included overall mortality, bilateral major amputation, NIL minor amputation, NIL revascularization, and development of NIL CLTI.
sections.results: Seventeen cohorts encompassing 30,359 patients were included. The pooled incidence of NIL major amputation was 6 per 100 person-years (95% CI, 3-9), with substantial heterogeneity (I2=98.93%). Meta-regression showed no significant differences by clinical phenotype (P=.622), geographic region (P=.662), study era (P=.893), or DM prevalence (P=.127). Clinical phenotypes included CLTI versus non-CLTI PAD or DM versus post-ipsilateral major amputation. Geographic region was divided into United States and international studies. Study era was divided into modern (2010-2025) and legacy (pre-2010) studies. Longer follow-up duration was inversely associated with reported incidence (P<.001). Pooled mortality rate was 38% (95% CI, 30-47%), and the pooled rate of bilateral major amputation was 12% (95% CI, 8-18%). Other secondary outcomes included a pooled NIL minor amputation rate of 11% (95% CI, 3-37%), NIL revascularization rate of 19% (95% CI, 6-47%), and NIL CLTI development rate of 32% (95% CI, 11-64%).
sections.conclusion: NIL major amputation remains a persistent risk in PAD and DM-related limb disease. These findings support the need for structured bilateral limb surveillance and early NIL risk stratification to inform comprehensive limb preservation care.

items.title: Index Below-Knee Endovascular Intervention for Intermittent Claudication Is Associated with Increased Amputation Risk.

sections.objective: Guidelines advise against infrapopliteal peripheral vascular intervention (PVI) for intermittent claudication (IC) due to potential harm with unclear benefit. We hypothesized that below-knee intervention at index PVI for IC confers higher future amputation risk than above-knee-only treatment.
sections.methods: From the VQI PVI registry (2015-2025), we identified elective, initial PVIs for IC and compared those patients undergoing above-knee-only treatment (AK) to those having any below-knee intervention (BK). Using our previously described methodology, long-term amputation data were obtained by linking the PVI and amputation registries via unique patient identifiers. Demographic and procedural data were analyzed descriptively. Kaplan-Meier Analysis estimated risk of major and any (major+minor) amputation, with independent predictors of amputation identified by multivariable Firth logistic regression.
sections.results: Among 92,899 treated limbs (81,338 AK; 11,561 BK), BK patients had increased rates of diabetes (54% vs. 41%), CHF (18% vs. 13%), and ESRD/dialysis (4.7% vs. 1.7%, p<0.001). BK patients were more likely to be Black (21% vs. 13%, p<0.001), Hispanic (8.8% vs. 4.3%, p<0.001), and Asian (1.5% vs. 1.0%, p<0.001). Smoking history predominated in AK (89% vs. 67%, p<0.001). 16,086 limbs required repeat PVI, 13,831 (17%) in the AK group vs. 2,255 (20%) in the BK group (p<0.001). At reintervention, BK patients were more likely to have progressed to CLTI (41% vs. 25%; p<0.001) and undergo ≥2 repeat interventions (32% vs. 27%; p<0.001). Initial below-knee intervention was associated with greater ipsilateral major (OR 2.39;1.70-3.35) and any (OR 2.36;1.75-3.18) amputation. Kaplan-Meier showed increased major [1-year (0.3% vs 0.1%);5-years (0.4% vs 0.1%)] and any amputation risk [1-year (0.5% vs 0.1%); 5-years (0.7% vs 0.2%).
sections.conclusion: Index below-knee intervention for IC portends greater risk of progression to CLTI, repeat PVI, and ipsilateral amputation, highlighting the potentially dangerous treatment trap of infrapopliteal intervention in patients with intermittent claudicants.

items.title: The neurobiology of menopause: Implications for brain aging and Alzheimer's risk.
items.abstract: A growing body of evidence implicates the menopausal transition as a neurobiological inflection point in women's brain aging and Alzheimer's disease (AD) vulnerability. Menopause is a midlife neuroendocrine transition characterized by a decline in sex steroid hormones and widespread systemic effects. The brain is not a passive recipient of ovarian hormones but an active endocrine-sensing organ. Menopause, however, does not act in isolation: the ovarian-brain axis is established embryonically, activated at puberty, remodeled during pregnancy and postpartum, and reconfigured during the menopausal transition, with implications for later-life brain aging. This review places menopause within a lifespan neuroendocrine framework, examining mechanisms by which the transition may influence the brain, including altered hormone signaling, bioenergetics, synaptic plasticity, neurovascular function, inflammation, and AD-related pathology. It then reviews evidence linking menopausal timing to neurobiological and AD vulnerability, discusses estrogen therapy, and considers menopause as a biologically plausible window for risk stratification and prevention.

items.title: Effect of Endostaple Configuration and Oversizing on Endograft Displacement Force: An In Vitro Evaluation of the Aortoseal Endostapling System.

sections.objective: Proximal endograft fixation remains a key determinant of long-term durability of endovascular aortic repair (EVAR). The Aortoseal Endostapling system consists of a nitinol frame with 6 welded endostaples at the proximal end, intended to enhance fixation and seal of an endograft by mimicking the hand-sewn anastomosis of open aortic repair. This study evaluates the effect of different distributions of activated endostaples on endograft displacement force (EDF), while considering various endograft oversizing options.
sections.methods: An in vitro silicone tube model was used to assess EDF at 2 mm endograft displacement and pull-out force across 11 activated staple configurations of the Aortoseal Endostapling system with 10%, 20%, and 30% endograft oversizing. Interobserver agreement was assessed using the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC), based on a 2-way mixed-effects model for absolute agreement.
sections.results: Intraclass correlation coefficient for interobserver agreement was 0.987. Endograft displacement force ranged from 8.8 N ± 0.15 N to 39.6 N ± 2.96 N across all configurations and oversizing conditions. Incorporation of the Aortoseal frame alone, without staple activation, substantially increased EDF compared with no Aortoseal frame at 10% and 20% oversizing. Furthermore, EDF was mostly influenced by the number of activated staples and the maximum unstapled circumferential angle (MUCA). The 6-activated-staple configuration consistently yielded the highest EDF. The effect of oversizing on EDF was inconsistent across configurations at 10% and 20%, whereas 30% oversizing was associated with lower EDF in most configurations. Pull-out force exceeded EDF in all tested configurations except the 1-activated-staple configuration.
sections.conclusion: In this in vitro study, Aortoseal frame incorporation alone substantially increased EDF relative to the graft-only configuration at 10% and 20% oversizing. Ten percent endograft oversizing yielded EDF values comparable with 20% oversizing across most configurations. Circumferential staple distribution was the primary determinant of EDF in the Aortoseal Endostapling system, with EDF decreasing with increasing MUCA and increasing with staple number across all endograft oversizing conditions, consistent with circumferential load sharing as a potential underlying mechanism. These findings may serve as a mechanistic reference framework for preoperative planning in anatomically challenging cases and warrant further experimental and clinical evaluation.Clinical ImpactThe Aortoseal Endostapling system (Endoron Medical Holdings Ltd., Dublin, Ireland) represents a novel approach to proximal endograft fixation, enabling simultaneous circumferential single-stage activation of 6 nitinol endostaples via balloon activation, providing a uniform and reproducible fixation pattern intended to mimic the longitudinal and radial anchoring of a surgical anastomosis. To support clinical implementation, this study systematically evaluated endograft displacement force across a range of activated staple configurations, including suboptimal deployment scenarios. The findings provide physicians with a mechanistic reference framework for preoperative planning, supporting procedural decision-making in anatomically challenging cases.

items.title: Five-Year Prognostic Outcomes After Paclitaxel-Coated Balloon Treatment According to Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischaemia Status: Insights From the BIOLUX P-III Registry.

sections.objective: Chronic limb-threatening ischaemia (CLTI) carries a high risk of death, limb loss, and impaired functional recovery despite revascularisation. Drug-coated balloons may reduce restenosis and repeat intervention after infrainguinal endovascular therapy, but long-term safety and effectiveness data in patients with CLTI remain limited.
sections.methods: We performed a prespecified subgroup analysis of BIOLUX P-III, a prospective international post-market all-comers registry evaluating the Passeo-18 Lux paclitaxel-coated balloon for infrainguinal peripheral artery disease. Outcomes were compared between patients with and without CLTI through 60 months. Endpoints included freedom from major adverse events, clinically driven target-lesion revascularisation, major target-limb amputation, amputation-free survival and all-cause mortality. Time-to-event outcomes were analysed using Kaplan-Meier methods. Because follow-up completeness declined substantially by 60 months, late estimates were interpreted in the context of censoring, attrition and competing mortality.
sections.results: Among 877 treated patients, 328 (37.4%) had CLTI. Technical success exceeded 98% in both groups. Patients with CLTI had greater baseline comorbidity, more advanced limb threat and more frequent below-the-knee disease. At 60 months, freedom from clinically driven target-lesion revascularisation was 85.3% in patients with CLTI and 78.3% in those without CLTI (P = .59), and freedom from major adverse events was similar (76.5% vs 74.3%; P = .13). In contrast, 5-year survival was substantially lower in patients with CLTI (47.9% vs 76.7%; P < .001). Freedom from major target-limb amputation was lower (93.3% vs 99.3%; P < .001), and amputation-free survival was reduced (47.1% vs 75.7%; P < .001). Patients with CLTI received a lower cumulative paclitaxel dose despite higher mortality.
sections.conclusion: Passeo-18 Lux treatment was associated with preserved lesion-level durability through 5 years, but CLTI identified a high-risk prognostic phenotype with poor survival and limb outcomes. These findings suggest that long-term outcomes in CLTI are influenced by systemic comorbidity, early limb vulnerability, competing mortality and wound-related factors beyond lesion-level device performance alone.Clinical ImpactThis study provides clinically relevant insights into the long-term outcomes of patients with chronic limb-threatening ischaemia (CLTI) undergoing endovascular revascularisation with drug-coated balloons. Despite high procedural success, patients with CLTI experience substantially greater long-term mortality and adverse limb outcomes than those with intermittent claudication. These findings highlight the importance of recognising CLTI as a high-risk clinical phenotype requiring comprehensive cardiovascular risk reduction, multidisciplinary management, and structured postprocedural surveillance. The study's principal contribution is its evaluation of five-year outcomes in a real-world, all-comers population, providing valuable evidence to inform patient counselling, individualised treatment strategies, and long-term clinical decision-making.

items.title: Multimodality Imaging Across the Lifespan in Repaired Tetralogy of Fallot: Current Evidence and Future Directions.
items.abstract: Repaired tetralogy of Fallot (rTOF) is a common condition encountered across pediatric and adult congenital heart disease clinics. Although childhood survival is excellent, patients remain at risk for late complications, including exercise intolerance, arrhythmias, heart failure, and sudden death. Residual lesions, most notably pulmonary regurgitation and right ventricular outflow tract obstruction, drive progressive right and secondary left ventricular remodeling, often necessitating repeat interventions such as pulmonary valve replacement. Multimodality imaging is central to management, enabling risk stratification and informing the optimal timing of reintervention. This State-of-the-Art Review summarizes the current state of the art in multimodality imaging for rTOF across the lifespan, highlighting established and emerging techniques. The authors discuss the roles of 2- and 3-dimensional echocardiography, cardiac magnetic resonance, strain and exercise imaging, ultrafast ultrasound, and advanced cardiac magnetic resonance methods in characterizing ventricular function, remodeling, mechanics, flow dynamics, fibrosis, stiffness, and electromechanical interactions. The authors explore developments in image-based machine learning and computational modeling that support patient-specific intervention planning and personalized care.

items.title: Risk-Stratified Outcomes of Prophylactic Laser Versus Observation for Pediatric Peripheral Retinal Lesions.

sections.objective: To compare clinical characteristics and outcomes of pediatric eyes with peripheral retinal breaks or lesions managed with prophylactic laser retinopexy versus observation, including outcomes within a predefined high-risk subgroup.
sections.methods: Retrospective cohort study. Intervention, or Testing: Electronic medical records were reviewed to extract demographic data, lesion characteristics, presence of subretinal fluid (SRF), symptom status, traumatic etiology, refractive error, management strategy, and follow-up outcomes. Eyes were classified as high-risk if SRF, symptoms, or trauma were present at baseline. Outcomes were compared between observation and laser groups overall and within the high-risk subgroup.
sections.results: Of 273 included eyes, 172 (63.0%) were observed and 101 (37.0%) underwent prophylactic laser. Laser-treated eyes had significantly higher baseline risk features, including SRF, symptomatic presentation, traumatic etiology, high myopia, and complex lesion types (all p < 0.05). Over a median follow-up of 18.5 months, RD occurred in 5.0% of lasered eyes and 1.2% of observed eyes (p = 0.105). Among high-risk eyes, RD rates did not differ significantly between laser and observation groups (11.4% vs 4.2%, p = 0.413). Final BCVA and rates of epiretinal membrane or cataract formation did not differ between groups. Retinal detachment was uncommon across lesion subtypes, including lattice degeneration and atrophic holes.
sections.conclusion: Prophylactic laser retinopexy in pediatric eyes was preferentially applied to lesions with greater anatomic and clinical risk but was not associated with a statistically significant reduction in retinal detachment rates compared with observation. These findings suggest that many pediatric peripheral retinal lesions may be safely managed with observation and highlight the need for pediatric-specific evidence to guide treatment decisions.
sections.other: Participants, and/or Controls: A total of 273 eyes from patients younger than 18 years diagnosed with peripheral retinal tears, holes, or lattice degeneration at a tertiary pediatric ophthalmology center. Eyes with retinal detachment at initial presentation were excluded. Observed eyes served as the comparison group for laser-treated eyes. Development of retinal detachment (RD) during follow-up. Secondary outcomes included best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) and development of complications such as epiretinal membrane or cataract during follow-up.

items.title: Efficacy and safety of oral orforglipron in Japanese participants with obesity disease (ATTAIN-J): a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, phase 3 trial.

sections.objective: Orforglipron, a small-molecule, non-peptide, oral GLP-1 receptor agonist, has shown bodyweight reduction and cardiometabolic benefits in adults with obesity across phase 3 trials globally. We aimed to assess the efficacy and safety of orforglipron versus placebo for treating obesity disease in Japanese adults.
sections.methods: ATTAIN-J was a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, phase 3 trial conducted across 16 medical research centres and hospitals in Japan and included adults aged 18 years or older with a BMI between 27 kg/m2 and less than 35 kg/m2 and two or more obesity-related health disorders, or a BMI of 35 kg/m2 or higher and one or more obesity-related health disorder, with one or more of the obesity-related health disorders being hypertension, dyslipidaemia, or type 2 diabetes (targeted at about 25% of participants), consistent with Japanese indications for tirzepatide and semaglutide for obesity disease; and at least one unsuccessful dietary attempt to lose weight. Participants were randomly assigned (1:1:1:1) via a computer-generated sequence to once-daily oral orforglipron (6 mg, 12 mg, or 36 mg) or placebo. Co-primary endpoints were mean percentage change in bodyweight and percentage of participants with at least 5% bodyweight reduction from baseline to week 72. Efficacy endpoints were primarily evaluated by the treatment regimen estimand in all randomly assigned participants. Safety was assessed in participants who received at least one dose of study treatment. This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05931380 (completed).
sections.results: Between July 31, 2023, and June 19, 2025, 291 participants were screened, of whom 238 (144 [61%] males and 94 [39%] females; mean age 54·1 years [SD 11·2]) were randomly assigned to receive orforglipron 6 mg (n=61), 12 mg (n=57), or 36 mg (n=60), or placebo (n=60); 214 (90%) participants completed the study. At week 72, mean percentage change in bodyweight was -5·9% (95% CI -7·6 to -4·2) with orforglipron 6 mg, -8·7% (-10·9 to -6·5) with 12 mg, and -7·9% (-10·0 to -5·8) with 36 mg, compared with -0·6% (-2·1 to 0·8) with placebo (all p<0·0001 vs placebo). At week 72, a bodyweight reduction of at least 5% was seen in 15·2% (SE 4·8; nine of 60) of participants in the placebo group compared with 45·6% (6·1; 28 of 61; p=0·0001) of participants in the orforglipron 6 mg group, 60·8% (6·4; 35 of 57; p<0·0001) of participants in the orforglipron 12 mg group, and 58·8% (6·5; 35 of 60; p<0·0001) of participants in the orforglipron 36 mg group. Adverse events with orforglipron were mostly mild-to-moderate gastrointestinal symptoms. Across all orforglipron groups, treatment-emergent adverse events that most frequently led to study treatment discontinuation were nausea (one [2%] of 61 in the 6 mg group, one [2%] of 57 in the 12 mg group, and five [8%] of 60 in the 36 mg group vs none with placebo) and vomiting (none in the 6 mg group, two [4%] in the 12 mg group, and one [2%] in the 36 mg group vs none in the placebo group).
sections.conclusion: In Japanese adults with obesity disease, once-daily orforglipron resulted in statistically superior reductions in bodyweight versus placebo, with a safety profile consistent with that of other GLP-1 receptor agonists.
sections.other: For the Japanese translation of the abstract see Supplementary Materials section.

items.title: Clinical and metabolic subtypes of recent-onset adult type 1 diabetes: a prospective cohort study.

sections.objective: Adult-onset type 1 diabetes exhibits substantial heterogeneity. We aimed to investigate whether this variability reflects distinct disease entities or different temporal stages of a shared autoimmune process.
sections.methods: In this prospective cohort study, we analysed data from adults (aged 18-69 years) in the German Diabetes Study who had clinically diagnosed type 1 diabetes within the preceding 12 months, and from individuals who were positive for glutamic acid decarboxylase antibody (GADA) but had originally been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes. We used unsupervised machine learning based on GADA status, fasting C-peptide, glucose, triglycerides, and HDL cholesterol to characterise clinical and metabolic type 1 diabetes subtypes. The resulting subtypes were compared for aetiological traits (polygenic risk scores for type 1 diabetes and type 2 diabetes, partitioned type 2 diabetes polygenic risk scores, human leukocyte antigen [HLA] profiles, and islet-directed autoantibodies), insulin sensitivity, glucagon-stimulated C-peptide trajectories as a measure of residual β-cell function, and complications during prospective follow-up. Reproducibility was assessed in adults with type 1 diabetes from the German Diabetes Prospective Follow-up Registry (Diabetes-Patienten-Verlaufsdokumentation [DPV]).
sections.results: Analysed participants in the German Diabetes Study cohort were recruited between June 27, 2005, and Jan 20, 2025 (n=600), and were followed up for a mean of 6·1 (SD 4·7) years. We identified three type 1 diabetes subtypes: two GADA-positive subtypes, and one GADA-negative subtype. A similar clinical and metabolic subtype structure was observed in the DPV cohort, whose participants were recruited between 2000 and 2025 (n=483) and were followed up for a mean of 3·1 (SD 5·0) years. One GADA-positive subtype was characterised by lower BMI, higher insulin sensitivity, and severe β-cell dysfunction (classic type 1 diabetes), whereas the second showed higher BMI, lower insulin sensitivity, and better β-cell function (mixed type 1 diabetes). The two GADA-positive subtypes did not differ in autoimmunity or type 1 diabetes polygenic risk scores, whereas the GADA-negative subtype had lower genetic type 1 diabetes risk, despite no clear subtype-specific differences in HLA risk haplotypes. Longitudinal modelling indicated that the mixed type 1 diabetes group was positioned 6·1 years (95% CI 4·6-7·8) earlier along the β-cell function decline trajectory compared with the classic type 1 diabetes group. The risks of hypoglycaemia (log-rank p=0·0019), retinopathy (mixed type 1 diabetes vs classic type 1 diabetes: adjusted hazard ratio 4·93 [95% CI 1·71-14·24]), and cardiovascular autonomic neuropathy (log-rank p=0·028) differed across the groups.
sections.conclusion: Our results indicate that individuals with combined autoimmunity and lower insulin sensitivity present with clinical diabetes earlier than classic type 1 diabetes along the β-cell decline trajectory, identifying a potential timeframe for disease-modifying interventions in specific type 1 diabetes subtypes.
sections.other: For the German translation of the abstract see Supplementary Materials section.

items.title: Pharmacological treatment of patent ductus arteriosus and mortality risk in preterm infants: a Bayesian meta-analysis across gestational age groups.

sections.objective: Recent randomised controlled trials and meta-analyses have questioned the safety of early pharmacological treatment of patent ductus arteriosus in preterm infants, suggesting possible increases in the risk of mortality and bronchopulmonary dysplasia. Whether these risks vary by gestational age remains uncertain. We aimed to compare the effects of pharmacological patent ductus arteriosus treatment in infants with a gestational age less than 26 weeks versus those with a gestational age of 26 weeks or greater.
sections.methods: For this Bayesian model-averaged meta-analysis, we searched PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) for randomised controlled trials enrolling infants with a gestational age less than 32 weeks and echocardiographically confirmed patent ductus arteriosus who were randomly assigned either to pharmacological treatment or to placebo or expectant management. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality before 36 weeks' postmenstrual age and secondary outcomes were moderate-to-severe bronchopulmonary dysplasia and the composite of death or moderate-to-severe bronchopulmonary dysplasia at 36 weeks' postmenstrual age. Pooled risk ratios (RRs) with 95% credible intervals (CrIs) were estimated. RRs greater than 1 indicated harm. We calculated the posterior probability of harm (Prharm=P[logRR>0]) and Bayes factors comparing harm versus benefit (BFharm/benefit). This study is registered on PROSPERO (CRD42024622527).
sections.results: Ten randomised controlled trials including 2365 infants (1133 female and 1232 male) were analysed; 1045 had a gestational age less than 26 weeks. Pharmacological treatment was associated with increased mortality in infants with a gestational age less than 26 weeks (RR 1·12 [95% CrI 0·90-1·41], Prharm=0·85, BFharm/benefit=5·48), in those with a gestational age of 26 weeks or greater (1·22 [0·90-1·77], Prharm=0·89, BFharm/benefit=7·82), and in the overall population (1·23 [95% CrI 1·00-1·54], Prharm=0·97, BFharm/benefit=36·04). For bronchopulmonary dysplasia and the composite outcome of death or moderate-to-severe bronchopulmonary dysplasia, analyses explicitly incorporating the possibility of no effect indicated that the data were more consistent with the no-effect model than with either the benefit or the harm model.
sections.conclusion: The currently available randomised evidence is consistent with an increased mortality risk associated with pharmacological patent ductus arteriosus treatment, without evidence of a compensatory reduction in bronchopulmonary dysplasia. This association was evident both below and above the 26-week gestational age threshold. These findings question the safety of routine pharmacological treatment and underscore the need for more selective, evidence-based approaches for patent ductus arteriosus management.

items.title: The present and future of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease prevention, diagnosis, and management in China: a Lancet Respiratory Medicine Commission.
items.abstract: For the Chinese translation of the abstract see Supplementary Materials section.

items.title: Performance of 0/1 h versus 0/3 h pathways in patients with suspected myocardial infarction: a systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.

sections.objective: In patients with suspected myocardial infarction, the 0/1 h pathway (blood draws at 0 h and 1 h) is recommended in current guidelines for early risk stratification. However, individual trials used different safety outcomes, and efficacy outcomes were inconclusive or not assessed. We conducted a systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis of all randomised controlled trials to synthesise the totality of the evidence, assess heterogeneity across trials, and evaluate clinically relevant outcomes using harmonised definitions across trials.
sections.methods: In this systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis, we searched PubMed, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, Scopus, and the International Clinical Trials Registry Platform from inception to July 6, 2026, without language restrictions, for randomised trials comparing the safety and efficacy of 0/1 h versus 0/3 h pathways (blood draws at 0 h and 3 h, ie, standard care). Individual participant data were obtained and outcome definitions were harmonised. The primary analysis used a two-stage random-effects meta-analysis. After receipt of the individual participant data but before data harmonisation or analysis, the primary safety outcome was refined to a composite of all-cause death or new type 1 myocardial infarction within 30 days, from the originally specified composite of all-cause death or any new myocardial infarction. The primary efficacy outcomes were emergency department length of stay and direct discharge from the emergency department. This meta-analysis is registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261383452).
sections.results: Our systematic review identified five randomised trials, all of which provided individual participant data. Among these, the definition of the primary safety outcome varied, and in four trials emergency department length of stay was not reported for the whole analysis population. We included 110 933 patient presentations (55 489 managed with the 0/1 h pathway and 55 444 managed with the 0/3 h pathway). Within 30 days, all-cause death or new type 1 myocardial infarction occurred in 446 patient presentations (0·8%) with the 0/1 h pathway versus 562 patient presentations (1·0%) with the 0/3 h pathway (random-effects pooled odds ratio [OR] 0·83 [95% CI 0·45-1·53]; I2=62·9%; τ2=0·143). Emergency department length of stay was 314 min (IQR 211-481) in the 0/1 h pathway group versus 308 min (209-453) in the 0/3 h pathway group (random-effects pooled geometric mean ratio 1·03 [95% CI 0·85-1·25]; I2=99·2%; τ2=0·024). Direct discharge from the emergency department occurred in 37 190 patient presentations (67·0%) with the 0/1 h pathway versus 36 485 patient presentations (65·8%) with the 0/3 h pathway (random-effects pooled OR 1·31 [95% CI 0·79-2·16]; I2=97·8%; τ2=0·156).
sections.conclusion: Across the available randomised trials, short-term adverse event rates were low with both pathways, but the pooled safety estimate remained imprecise. On average, earlier cardiac troponin retesting did not reduce emergency department length of stay or clearly increase direct discharge, and substantial between-study heterogeneity indicates that treatment effects might not translate uniformly across health-care systems. For hospitals considering transitioning from a 0/3 h to a 0/1 h pathway, implementation decisions should take broader diagnostic and organisational considerations into account.

items.title: Irritable bowel syndrome and related disorders of gut-brain interaction.
items.abstract: Irritable bowel syndrome, chronic constipation, and functional diarrhoea are disorders of gut-brain interaction, the symptoms of which include abnormal stool consistency or frequency accompanied by varying degrees of abdominal pain, discomfort, bloating, or distension. These conditions affect 20% of the global population with a relapsing and remitting course. Risk factors include female sex, younger age, a history of common mental disorders, and acute enteric infection. The pathophysiology of irritable bowel syndrome, chronic constipation, and functional diarrhoea remain incompletely understood, but are thought to be secondary to aberrant interactions throughout the gut-brain axis, resulting in disordered gut motility and visceral hypersensitivity. These conditions are diagnosed with a combination of clinical history, absence of alarm symptoms-such as weight loss or rectal bleeding-and targeted investigations. An empathetic management approach improves quality of life and symptoms, reduces health-care use, and enhances treatment adherence. Mainstays of treatment include education, dietary and lifestyle advice, modifying fibre intake, and drugs directed towards predominant symptoms. For severe symptoms, other treatments include specific medical devices, biofeedback, or psychological therapies. However, the effectiveness of most treatments is modest and there is an ongoing need to expand available treatments for bowel disorders, with several novel drugs currently in development.

items.title: Genetic coupling of floral rewards and signals underlies pollinator attraction.
items.abstract: Animal pollinators underpin biodiversity and global agriculture, yet the molecular mechanisms that coordinate floral rewards and signals to attract pollinators remain poorly understood. Through phenotyping melon genetic diversity, we identified nectarless1 (nls1), encoding the YABBY-family transcription factor YABBY5 (YAB5), as a central integrator of pollinator-attracting traits. YAB5 interacts with CRABS CLAW (CRC) during nectary initiation to specify nectary identity by repressing alternative floral organ fates. As flowers mature, YAB5 directly activates 4-α-glucanotransferase 2 (DPE2) to promote starch remobilization required for nectar secretion and promotes petal growth and flower opening. In petals, YAB5 directly engages an MYB111-dependent flavonoid pathway that generates UV nectar guides, while indirectly influencing floral volatile emission. Disrupting YAB5, DPE2, or MYB111 reduces pollinator visitation. Together, these findings reveal how a developmental regulator couples organ specification with organ-specific metabolic programs to synchronize floral rewards and signals at anthesis.

items.title: Innate sensor responses set a supra-unitary threshold for viral replication.
items.abstract: Cells resist viral infection by triggering rapid and sensitive innate immune responses, initiated by cytoplasmic viral sensor proteins (CyVSP), retinoic acid-inducible gene I (RIG-I), melanoma differentiation-associated protein 5 (MDA-5), and protein kinase R (PKR). Our single-cell analysis reveals that viral replication requires a supra-unitary viral genome input, significantly more than one, which we define as the virion input threshold for replication (VITREP). This threshold varies depending on viruses and cell types, independently of viral protein synthesis. Through mathematical modeling and experimental testing, we uncover that supra-unitary viral genome quantities activate negative feedback regulators (NFR) of CyVSP, including death-associated protein kinase 1 (DAPK1), Rio kinase 3 (RIOK3), and protein phosphatase 2 regulatory subunit alpha (PPP2R2A), that suppress innate immune responses and allow replication. We validate key predictions of our model, namely that downregulating NFR reduces replication, whereas upregulating NFR or coinfecting cells promotes replication. Together, these findings reveal a fundamental mechanism governing viral infectivity and tissue tropism.

items.title: Toward planetary microbial systems biology.
items.abstract: Microorganisms underpin Earth's biosphere, sustaining life, shaping biogeochemical cycles, and maintaining ecosystem stability. In an era of scientific and geopolitical fragmentation, we advocate for a "planetary microbial systems biology" (PMSB) framework to uncover the mechanisms and organizational principles governing Earth's interconnected microbial systems across scales of matter, space, and time and in relation to underlying natural and anthropogenic drivers. PMSB combines molecular and cellular technologies, multi-omics data, artificial intelligence (AI), and integrated transdisciplinary research across ecosystems. By federating open data and combining field observations, experimentation, and modeling, PMSB enables predictive understanding of microbiome dynamics across planetary scales, thus filling a critical knowledge gap in our understanding of the co-evolution of life and the Earth-system.
keywords: Tara Europa, mobile laboratories, pan-European research collaboration
global connectivity, environmental cell biology, scientifc and geopolitical fragmentation

items.title: Roads not taken: The mismatch between safety and regulation of plant breeding innovation.
items.abstract: Meeting global food security goals while reducing agriculture's environmental impact requires continued crop improvement and innovation. Advances in transgenesis, cisgenesis, and genome editing now enable increasingly precise genetic modification with risks comparable to those of conventional breeding, yet regulatory frameworks remain focused on the method used rather than the product. We highlight recent examples, including immune receptor transfer, cisgenesis-based disease resistance stacking, photosynthesis engineering, and AI-guided protein design, that illustrate innovations constrained by current regulatory approaches. A decisive shift toward science-based, proportionate, and product-focused regulation is needed so that improved crops are evaluated on the basis of their properties, not how they were made.

items.title: Gram-Negative Bacterial Resistance.
items.abstract: The rapid worldwide spread of antimicrobial resistance among gram-negative bacteria is driven by a complex interplay of human, environmental, and health care-associated factors and accelerated by mobile genetic elements that facilitate the dissemination of resistance genes. Resistance in gram-negative bacteria arises primarily through reduced drug entry, active drug efflux, modification of antibiotic targets, and enzymatic drug inactivation, most notably through β-lactamase production. Clinically important resistant pathogens include extended-spectrum β-lactamase-producing Enterobacterales, carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales, Pseudomonas aeruginosa with difficult-to-treat resistance, and carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii. Limited access to effective antibiotics and the continued emergence of resistance to available agents pose substantial challenges to the management of these infections. Appropriate management requires timely and accurate diagnostics, targeted use of newer β-lactam agents, effective source control, and judicious selection of treatment durations.

items.title: Continuous Glucose Monitoring in Non-Insulin-Treated Type 2 Diabetes.

sections.objective: Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) has been shown to be beneficial in persons with type 1 diabetes and others with insulin-treated type 2 diabetes, but its role in the treatment of persons with type 2 diabetes not being treated with insulin has needed further study.
sections.methods: In a 26-week trial conducted at 22 primary care practices in the United States, we randomly assigned adults with type 2 diabetes who were not using insulin to either CGM or routine care (control). The primary outcome was the glycated hemoglobin level at 26 weeks. Key CGM-measured secondary outcomes were tested hierarchically to control the type I error rate.
sections.results: A total of 145 participants were assigned to the CGM group, and 138 to the routine-care group. Participants ranged in age from 21 to 84 years. The mean (±SD) glycated hemoglobin level decreased from 8.8±1.3% at baseline to 7.2±1.1% at 26 weeks in the CGM group and from 8.7±1.2% to 8.0±1.4% in the routine-care group (adjusted mean difference, -0.9 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -1.1 to -0.6; P<0.001). The mean percentage of time that the CGM-measured glucose level was in the glucose-level range of 70 to 180 mg per deciliter was 21 percentage points higher (95% CI, 16 to 26) with CGM than with routine care (P<0.001). The between-group difference in the percentage of time that the glucose level was below 54 mg per deciliter was -0.17 percentage points (95% CI, -0.27 to -0.11; P<0.001 for noninferiority); the difference in the percentage of time that the glucose level was below 70 mg per deciliter was -0.20 percentage points (95% CI, -0.43 to -0.09; P<0.001 for noninferiority; P = 0.004 for superiority). No severe hypoglycemia events were reported.
sections.conclusion: Among adults with type 2 diabetes that was not being treated with insulin and was being managed in a primary care setting, the use of CGM led to a greater reduction in the glycated hemoglobin level and to a lower risk of hyperglycemia than routine care. (Funded by Dexcom; CONNECT ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06601166.).

items.title: Intermittent or Continuous Renal-Replacement Therapy in Acute Kidney Injury.

sections.objective: The preferred method of renal-replacement therapy for acute kidney injury in critically ill patients remains uncertain.
sections.methods: In this multicenter, open-label, noninferiority trial, we randomly assigned critically ill adults with acute kidney injury who had indications for renal-replacement therapy to undergo intermittent hemodialysis or continuous renal-replacement therapy as the initial treatment. The primary outcome was a major adverse kidney event - defined as death, dependence on renal-replacement therapy, or a serum creatinine concentration more than 25% above the baseline value - by day 90.
sections.results: The trial was stopped early after sequential interim analyses showed a sustained signal of higher mortality with intermittent hemodialysis than with continuous renal-replacement therapy. A total of 554 patients underwent randomization, with 272 patients assigned to undergo intermittent hemodialysis and 282 to undergo continuous renal-replacement therapy; 535 patients (260 in the intermittent group and 275 in the continuous group) were included in the intention-to-treat population. A major adverse kidney event occurred by day 90 in 203 patients (78.1%) in the intermittent group and in 197 patients (71.6%) in the continuous group (adjusted absolute risk difference, 6.28 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -1.22 to 13.79). Death by day 90 occurred in 164 patients (63.1%) and in 147 patients (53.5%), respectively. Kaplan-Meier mortality estimates at day 90 were 63.3% and 53.6% (hazard ratio, 1.30; 95% CI, 1.04 to 1.63). The most common complication potentially related to acute kidney injury or renal-replacement therapy was hypotension, which occurred in 179 patients (68.8%) in the intermittent group and in 183 patients (66.5%) in the continuous group.
sections.conclusion: Among critically ill patients with acute kidney injury who had indications for renal-replacement therapy, intermittent hemodialysis as the initial treatment approach was not shown to be noninferior to continuous renal-replacement therapy with respect to major adverse kidney events by day 90 and was associated with higher mortality. (Funded by the French Ministry of Health; ICRAKI ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06032884.).

items.title: A fluctuation test for gastruloid heterogeneity.
items.abstract: Stem cells self-organize into models of early development, but even under carefully controlled conditions, the resulting organoids exhibit substantial "inter-individual" heterogeneity. To explore its origins, we generated monoclonal gastruloids, each derived from a single mouse embryonic stem cell (mESC). Molecular profiling revealed extensive heterogeneity: some gastruloids failed to develop, others were biased toward mesodermal or neural fates, and yet others contained cell types atypical of conventional polyclonal gastruloids. Applying DNA Typewriter, a cell lineage recorder, we identified heritable fate biases arising prior to gastruloid induction and found that more closely related founder mESCs give rise to more phenotypically similar gastruloids. Linking mESC subclones to their descendants' fates revealed cryptic, fate-predictive differences in gene expression and chromatin accessibility, including at imprinted, methylation-sensitive loci linked to developmental potency. Intrinsic, heritable fluctuations in mESC state are therefore an important source of organoid heterogeneity, and DNA Typewriter enables high-resolution lineage trees in stem cell models.

items.title: Comprehensive lineage tracing maps the landscape of cell fate decisions in mouse embryogenesis.
items.abstract: A comprehensive cell fate map of mammalian embryogenesis has remained out of reach given the scale, cellular diversity, and non-deterministic nature of development in utero. Here, we use PEtracer to continuously install heritable genetic marks as development progresses, reconstructing lineage trees that resolve ∼75% of cell divisions across >1.4 million cells from 16 replicate embryos. We pair these trees with deep transcriptional profiling to resolve cell fate biases, restriction timing, progenitor pool sizes, and lineage relationships throughout embryogenesis. Using this quantitative reference, we uncover strikingly reproducible lineage architecture between replicate embryos and chart the lineage dynamics driving fate specification across diverse tissues. Specific biological insights include the progressive restriction of neural crest fate, the relative contributions of distinct mesodermal origins to endothelium, and the dynamics of axial elongation. This work provides a foundation for a quantitative and predictive understanding of mammalian development.

items.title: Opposing functions of gut immunomodulatory metabolites on CAR-T therapy.
items.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cell therapy has transformed hematological cancer treatment, yet nearly half of patients still relapse or progress. Increasing evidence implicates the gut microbiome and antibiotic exposure as key modulators of clinical outcomes. In a cohort of 129 patients across three German centers, shotgun metagenomics and targeted mass spectrometry revealed that reduced short-chain fatty acids, particularly valeric acid, prior to CAR-T cell therapy correlated with increased risk of disease progression. Conversely, high levels of indole metabolites, including indole-3-carboxaldehyde and indole-3-acetic acid as well as the branched-chain fatty acid isovaleric acid, were linked to adverse outcomes. Functional validation in human and murine CAR-T cell models demonstrated that valeric acid supplementation enhanced, while indole-3-carboxaldehyde and isovaleric acid impaired, CAR-T cell efficacy. These findings reveal the opposing roles of immunomodulatory metabolites on CAR-T cell therapy, carrying significant implications for the design of metabolite-guided, microbiome-based therapeutics.

items.title: Copper ion-induced MYH9 polymerization executes cuproptosis.
items.abstract: Cuproptosis is a recently identified form of copper-dependent cell death implicated in various physiological and pathological processes. However, the executive proteins involved and the role of physiological intracellular copper in cuproptosis remain unclear. Herein, we identified myosin heavy-chain 9 (MYH9) as a cuproptosis executioner. Copper binding induced MYH9 polymerization, which disrupted the actin cytoskeleton and led to cuproptotic cell death. Hexyl 2-(3,4,5-trihydroxy-phenyl) acetate (HThPA) was shown to induce cuproptosis by binding to the nuclear receptor Nur77, leading to depletion of copper chelate glutathione (GSH) and release of free copper from intracellular copper stores. Acetylation of MYH9 by acetyltransferase dihydrolipoamide S-acetyltransferase (DLAT) facilitated copper binding, regardless of its extracellular or intracellular origin. Physiological copper levels were higher in drug-resistant tumor cells and clinical samples, which increased the likelihood of HThPA-induced cuproptosis. These results elucidate the mechanisms underlying cuproptosis, establish MYH9 as an executioner, and propose a treatment strategy for drug-resistant tumors.

items.title: Glycocalyx-edited mesenchymal stem/stromal cell therapy in advanced osteoporosis.
items.abstract: Mesenchymal stem/stromal cells (MSCs) are osteoregenerative; however, their therapeutic efficacy for skeletal conditions is hampered by poor bone-homing ("osteotropism"). In preclinical models, this deficit is correctable by MSC glycocalyx editing to enforce sialylated Lewis X (sLeX) expression, thereby programming osteotropism. We conducted a first-in-human clinical trial (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT02566655) involving a single intravenous infusion of glycocalyx-edited autologous bone marrow-derived MSCs in ten women with advanced-stage osteoporosis. The protocol-mandated evaluation spanned 2 years and included clinical assessments, radiographic studies, and measurements of bone turnover markers (BTMs), bone tissue area (BTA), and bone mineral density (BMD). Thereafter, fracture and safety monitoring continued for >3 additional years for each patient. No serious adverse events occurred. Fragility fractures were markedly and durably reduced, amidst increased osteoanabolic BTM levels, BTA, and volumetric BMD. These findings indicate that glycocalyx editing effectuates MSC-based osteoporosis therapy and also refute notions that MSCs derived from older persons and/or diseased-tissue sites are biologically compromised.

items.title: Metax enables accurate cross-domain taxonomic profiling of metagenomes.
items.abstract: Taxonomic profiling is fundamental to microbiome research, yet achieving high species-level accuracy remains challenging for complex communities that span bacteria, viruses, eukaryotes, and archaea, and these limitations are exacerbated in low-biomass, host-dominated samples. We introduce Metax, a cross-domain taxonomic profiler that integrates coverage-based probabilistic modeling with an expectation-maximization framework to distinguish true microbial signals from artifacts. Across >600 samples from host-associated, environmental, wastewater, and low-biomass clinical settings, including benchmarks with limited reference representation, Metax improved profiling accuracy, achieving on average 55% higher F1 scores and 45% lower Bray-Curtis dissimilarity than other methods. Moreover, this broad evaluation demonstrated that Metax resolved bacterial and viral signatures of peri-implantitis in oral microbiomes and revealed signals suggestive of reagent-borne contaminants and reference misassemblies in plasma-cell-free DNA. By leveraging genome-wide coverage evidence, Metax enables robust cross-domain profiling across diverse sample types and sequencing depths, including settings where reference databases are highly incomplete.

items.title: Caloric restriction modulates genome-wide somatic mutation in mice.
items.abstract: Somatic mutations accumulate throughout life in every cell, and this process constitutes one of the hallmarks of aging-genomic instability. Caloric restriction (CR) has been shown to extend lifespan across diverse species. Using high-fidelity duplex DNA sequencing of bulk liver, bulk kidney, hepatocytes, and cerebellar neurons, we found that CR in mice reduces genome-wide somatic mutation burdens across multiple tissues and cell types. CR reduced both substitution and insertion/deletion burdens, with the magnitude of these effects varying across sample types. CR also decreased the activity of the enigmatic single-base substitution (SBS) mutational process SBS5 that gives rise to most mutations in mammals. Surprisingly, the mutation burden reduction from CR was greatest in transcriptionally inactive regions. This work illuminates links between diet, aging, and genomic integrity and establishes genomic integrity as a modifiable axis of aging.

items.title: Structural basis of a SWI/SNF-associated transcription pre-initiation complex.
items.abstract: The mating type switching/sucrose non-fermenting (SWI/SNF) chromatin remodeling complex removes and repositions nucleosomes at promoters for the initiation of transcription. Though long thought to function independently, we find that SWI/SNF is an integral component of the transcription machinery. SWI/SNF associates with an RNA polymerase II pre-initiation complex (PIC), Mediator, and a nucleosome, and the entire assembly dimerizes to form a giant 7-megadalton complex. We present high-resolution cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) structures of both PIC-Mediator-SWI/SNF and PIC-Mediator-SWI/SNF-nucleosome complexes, together with results of cross-linking and mass spectrometry. The structures reveal how SWI/SNF enhances the initiation of transcription through stabilization of PIC organization and concerted remodeling of the so-called +1 nucleosome. The structural model suggests the coordinated actions of two DNA translocases, Snf2 of SWI/SNF and Ssl2 of TFIIH, for the initiation of transcription.

items.title: Tozorakimab to Prevent COPD Exacerbations.

sections.objective: Many patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) have exacerbations despite receiving standard-of-care inhaled maintenance therapy. Dysregulated interleukin-33 signaling is implicated in the pathogenesis of COPD. Tozorakimab is a monoclonal antibody that inhibits the activity of interleukin-33.
sections.methods: In two replicate phase 3 trials (OBERON and TITANIA), we enrolled adults with COPD who were current or former smokers and had a history of exacerbations in the previous year despite receiving stable standard-of-care inhaled maintenance therapy. There were no eligibility criteria related to blood eosinophil count. Patients were randomly assigned to receive add-on subcutaneous tozorakimab (300 mg) or placebo every 4 weeks for 52 weeks. The primary end point was the annualized rate of moderate or severe exacerbations that occurred over a 52-week period among former smokers, and the first key secondary end point was the annualized rate of moderate or severe exacerbations in the overall population. Safety was also assessed.
sections.results: The overall population in OBERON included 446 patients in the tozorakimab group and 431 in the placebo group, and in TITANIA included 438 in the tozorakimab group and 435 in the placebo group. The annualized rate of moderate or severe exacerbations among former smokers was 1.34 events in the tozorakimab group and 1.90 events in the placebo group (rate ratio, 0.71; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.57 to 0.88; P = 0.002) in OBERON, and 1.37 events and 2.07 events, respectively (rate ratio, 0.66; 95% CI, 0.55 to 0.80; P<0.001), in TITANIA. In the overall population, the annualized rate of moderate or severe exacerbations was 1.41 events in the tozorakimab group and 2.00 events in the placebo group (rate ratio, 0.70; 95% CI, 0.58 to 0.85; P<0.001) in OBERON, and 1.44 events and 2.03 events, respectively (rate ratio, 0.71; 95% CI, 0.59 to 0.84; P<0.001), in TITANIA. Adverse events occurred in 70.4% of the patients in the tozorakimab group and in 77.2% of those in the placebo group in OBERON, and in 80.1% and 79.8%, respectively, in TITANIA.
sections.conclusion: Among patients with COPD, treatment with tozorakimab resulted in a significantly lower rate of moderate or severe exacerbations than placebo in the cohort of former smokers and in the overall population of current and former smokers. (Funded by AstraZeneca; OBERON ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05166889; TITANIA ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05158387.).

items.title: Identification of the tendon/ligament stem cell in mice and humans.
items.abstract: Ligamentum flavum (LF) hypertrophy resulting in spinal cord compression is a key cause of lumbar spinal stenosis (LSS). There are no medical therapies for LSS, in part because the identity of the tendon/ligament stem cell (TLSC) mediating LSS remains unclear. Here, we identify the TLSC present in all tendons and ligaments in humans and mice as Lin-Thy1.2-Sca-1-CD73+CD140α- cells that display self-renewal and give rise to all other tenocyte lineage cells. This TLSC also sits at the apex of their differentiation hierarchy, as determined by in vivo somatic-variant-based lineage tracing. LSS induction led to druggable, calcium signaling-dependent, cell-intrinsic reprogramming of the TLSCs to increase their tenocyte output. Overall, this work identifies the TLSC and establishes dysregulated differentiation of this cell as a mechanism contributing to LSS. This TLSC is anticipated to play a central role in other disorders of tendons and ligaments.

items.title: Tabula Sapiens 2.0: A comprehensive transcriptomic atlas of human cell types.
items.abstract: The Tabula Sapiens is a reference human cell atlas containing single-cell transcriptomic data from more than two dozen organs and tissues. Here, we report Tabula Sapiens 2.0, which includes data from nine new donors, doubles the number of cells, and adds four new tissues. These new data include four donors with multiple organs contributed, thus providing a unique dataset in which genetic background, age, and epigenetic effects are controlled for. We illustrate applications of the Tabula Sapiens data in areas as diverse as gene regulation and aging. The Tabula Sapiens contains transcripts from nearly all human transcription factors, thereby providing putative cell-type specificity for nearly every human transcription factor and insights into their potential regulatory roles. We also analyze the transcriptomes of cells expressing canonical genes relating to cellular senescence, revealing the heterogeneity and context-dependent nature of senescence and providing new hypotheses into senescence-associated pathways.
items.authors: Tabula Sapiens Consortium. Electronic address: steve@quake-lab.org

items.title: De novo pan-rhodamine binders for fluorescence microscopy from mammalian cells to extremophiles.
items.abstract: Fluorescent imaging in live cells is a cornerstone of life sciences. While natural fluorescent proteins have been engineered to enhance individual features, no existing tag combines ideal properties into a single system: high brightness, reversible binding, compact size, and stability across diverse conditions. Here, we achieve this through de novo design of rhodamine binders (Rhobin). To harness the broad repertoire of rhodamine fluorophores, we developed a generalizable design strategy for a pan-rhodamine binder compatible with diverse wavelengths and applications. Rhobin enables live- and fixed-cell imaging of various subcellular targets in mammalian cells, showing brightness surpassing existing tags. Its reversible fluorophore binding supports super-resolution stimulated emission depletion (STED) and live-cell single-molecule imaging for extended durations compared with HaloTag. Beyond conventional systems, Rhobin enables live imaging of the extremophile Sulfolobus acidocaldarius at 75°C, previously inaccessible with current tags. Together, these results establish Rhobin as a versatile platform for next-generation imaging and biosensor design.

items.title: Immediate Ambulatory Electrocardiographic Monitoring in Syncope.

sections.objective: In patients with syncope who present to the emergency department for evaluation, diagnosing an underlying cardiac arrhythmia remains difficult.
sections.methods: We conducted an open-label, randomized, controlled trial at 45 hospitals in the United Kingdom to assess the effects of 14-day cardiac monitoring on diagnosis, treatment, and outcomes among patients with syncope. Adults with syncope that remained unexplained after an evaluation in the emergency department were assigned in a 1:1 ratio to undergo 14-day ambulatory electrocardiographic (ECG) monitoring (the intervention group) or to receive the standard care provided for patients with unexplained syncope at each participating site (the standard-care group). The primary outcome was the mean number of patient-reported episodes of syncope at 1 year.
sections.results: A total of 2234 patients underwent randomization: 1123 were assigned to the intervention group and 1111 to the standard-care group. The mean age of the patients was 58.3 years, and 52.1% were male. After the exclusion of patients who did not complete any follow-up, a total of 1970 patients (1004 in the intervention group and 966 in the standard-care group) were included in the primary analysis. The mean (±SD) number of patient-reported syncope episodes at 1 year was 1.37±5.10 in the intervention group and 1.58±8.56 in the standard-care group (incidence rate ratio, 0.89; 95% confidence interval, 0.68 to 1.18; P = 0.42). A total of 49 adverse events were reported in the intervention group, and 8 adverse events were reported in the standard-care group, with 1 serious adverse event in each group.
sections.conclusion: Among patients with syncope that remained unexplained after evaluation in the emergency department, the use of 14-day ambulatory ECG monitoring did not result in significantly fewer patient-reported syncope episodes at 1 year than standard care. (Funded by the British Heart Foundation and National Health Service Research Scotland; ASPIRED ISRCTN Registry number, ISRCTN10278811.).

items.title: Genome-scale perturb-seq in primary human CD4+ T cells maps context-specific regulators of T cell programs and human immune traits.
items.abstract: Gene regulatory networks encode the fundamental logic of cellular functions, but systematic network mapping remains challenging, especially in cell states relevant to human biology and disease. Here, we perturbed all expressed genes across 22 million primary human CD4+ T cells from four donors and developed a probe-based perturb-seq platform to measure the transcriptome effects in cells at rest and after stimulation. These data allowed us to map genes regulating immune pathways, including previously uncharacterized regulators of cytokine production. Importantly, active regulators and the gene programs they control changed dramatically across stimulation conditions. Perturbation signatures enabled us to model T cell states observed in population-scale transcriptomic atlases, nominating regulators of T cell polarization and of age-related phenotypes. Finally, we leveraged perturb-seq to implicate context-specific gene regulatory pathways in autoimmune disease risk. Our study provides a foundational resource and new approaches to decode T cell function and human immune traits.

items.title: Integrative spatial profiling of 3D genome organization and gene expression in tissue.
items.abstract: Three-dimensional genome organization shapes transcriptional regulation, yet measuring its spatial coordination in situ within intact tissues remains challenging. We present Spatial Hi-C-RNA, a multimodal platform that simultaneously maps genome-wide chromatin contacts and transcriptomes from the same tissue section at near-single-cell resolution. Across the mouse brain, developing embryos, and human melanoma, Spatial Hi-C-RNA generated multimodal maps that aligned with tissue anatomy while revealing complementary chromatin- and RNA-defined spatial patterns. Multiscale features, including A/B compartments, topologically associating domains, and chromatin loops, were associated with region- and cell-type-specific transcriptional programs. In mouse embryos, Spatial Hi-C-RNA resolved coordinated chromatin and transcriptional remodeling during neuronal maturation across developmental stages. In human melanoma, chromatin architecture delineated intratumoral subregions not detected by RNA alone and linked tumor-state transitions to changes in compartments, domain boundaries, and regulatory programs. Spatial Hi-C-RNA thus provides a broadly applicable framework for investigating genome structure-function relationships in development and disease within native tissue environments.

items.title: Gut microbiota generate dinitrosyl iron complexes with cardiometabolic benefits.
items.abstract: Gut bacteria affect host physiology, but the underlying mechanisms are not completely understood. We identify a pathway whereby gut microbes convert inorganic nitrate and non-heme iron into mobile bioactive dinitrosyl iron complexes (DNICs) that are distributed systemically and affect host metabolism. Electron paramagnetic resonance detected DNICs in tissues of conventional but not germ-free mice. Mouse and human feces and E. coli generated DNICs from nitrate and iron citrate, whereas a nitrate-reductase-deficient mutant did not. Dietary supplementation with nitrate+iron citrate or synthetic DNICs increased tissue DNIC levels and ameliorated cardiometabolic dysfunction in Western diet-fed mice. Additionally, in HepG2 cells and human hepatocyte spheroids, DNIC reduced fatty acid-induced steatosis. DNIC bioactivity is mediated by the Fe(NO)2 entity, rather than by free nitric oxide (NO), and involves activation of soluble guanylyl cyclase (sGC), inhibition of leucine uptake, and mTORC1 signaling normalization. Modulating DNIC formation by the gut microbiota could be a strategy to support cardiometabolic health.

items.title: RNA structures regulate norovirus life cycle and enable rational attenuation in vivo.
items.abstract: Viral genomes encode regulatory RNA structures that orchestrate key steps of viral replication and gene expression. Although these structures are increasingly recognized as critical regulators of viral function, their systematic characterization in an infection context and roles in regulating viral fitness and immune recognition in vivo remain limited. Here, we systematically map and functionally interrogate structured RNA elements across the murine norovirus genome using orthogonal in-cell chemical probing, revealing conserved motifs that regulate viral function. Targeted disruption of specific structural elements reduces viral replication in cell culture, modulates translation in cis, and decreases viral RNA levels in animal infection models. These findings enabled the rational design of a genetically stable, attenuated virus that elicits protective immunity and limits viral replication upon secondary challenge. Together, this work uncovers essential roles for RNA structure in norovirus biology and establishes a generalizable framework for RNA structure-guided design of antiviral vaccines and therapeutics.

items.title: Multimodal brain cell atlas across the adult macaque lifespan.
items.abstract: High-throughput single-cell omics of non-human primate brain tissue provides a powerful platform to investigate the molecular basis of brain aging.
