Here, we present a comprehensive transcriptomic and chromatin accessibility atlas of 2,955,873 nuclei from eight brain regions of 23 female cynomolgus macaques spanning the adult lifespan, including exceptionally old individuals. Our analyses reveal dynamic, cell-subtype- and region-specific age-related changes in core brain functions, including synaptic communication and axon myelination. We identify multicellular networks in the pons and medulla as a previously unrecognized hotspot of primate brain aging, highlighting white matter vulnerability as a central feature of aging. Integration with human brain aging and neurodegeneration datasets reveals both shared and divergent molecular mechanisms. We further define transcription factors and age-related chromatin remodeling programs linked to longevity and neurodegeneration. This spatiotemporal atlas establishes a foundational framework for understanding the cellular and regulatory architecture of primate brain aging and its links to disease.

items.title: Brain perivascular macrophages regulate endothelial cell function via a cMAF-dependent transcriptional program in mouse and human.
items.abstract: Brain perivascular macrophages maintain brain physiology, yet their transcriptional regulators and functions in health and disease remain unclear. Using single-cell multi-omics and functional experiments, we identify cellular musculoaponeurotic fibrosarcoma oncogene (cMAF) as a key transcription factor for brain perivascular macrophages, and conditional deletion of cMAF disrupts their phenotype in vivo. Functionally, cMAF drives insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF1) expression in perivascular macrophages, enabling communication with endothelial cells. Consistently, cMAF deletion in perivascular macrophages causes transcriptional alterations in cerebral arteries, affecting vascular functions. Notably, cMAF emerges as the main transcription factor for human perivascular macrophages, suggesting conservation of this transcriptional module. During Alzheimer's disease (AD), human perivascular macrophages upregulate cMAF and IGF1 to enhance communication with vascular cells, and this response is abrogated in APOE4 carriers. Lastly, we explore an uncharacterized polymorphism in cMAF, providing evidence that the cMAF program is protective against AD. Targeting cMAF in perivascular macrophages may offer new therapeutic strategies for neurodegenerative and cerebrovascular diseases.

items.title: Alloimmune risk stratification for kidney transplantation.
items.abstract: Alloreactivity after kidney transplantation occurs via both memory responses resulting from prior sensitization and de novo responses that develop due to donor-recipient disparity for the human leukocyte antigen (HLA) complex. HLA compatibility (absence of HLA-DSA) and the degree of HLA matching inform on the likelihood of allorecognition that can cause allograft rejection and allograft loss, and are therefore the two pillars of alloimmune risk assessment. Over the past decades, the detection of anti-HLA antibodies has become more sensitive and specific through single antigen bead testing, and advances in HLA typing from serology to DNA level have been instrumental for more detailed analysis of HLA compatibility. Nonetheless, alloimmune risk stratification using antigen-level HLA data has limited ability to accurately predict the risk of de novo anti-HLA responses and long-term graft outcome after transplantation, especially on the individual patient level. Aiming to improve long-term outcomes by improving HLA matching, HLA molecular mismatch algorithms have been developed. In this review, we discuss the advances, clinical evidence, limitations and clinical implementability of HLA molecular mismatch analysis to increase precision in alloimmune risk stratification in kidney transplantation. In addition, we provide an overview of the different molecular mismatch tools and their potential application in personalized medicine, such as organ allocation, criteria for donor acceptance and individualized immunosuppression.

items.title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists Decrease the Rate of Rupture, Cardiac Events, and Death in Patients with Abdominal Aortic Aneurysms.

sections.objective: Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is a degenerative condition involving several processes including inflammation, matrix remodeling, disruptions of vascular smooth muscle cells, and thrombus formation all leading to progressive dilatation of the aorta and eventual rupture. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RA) are now considered part of the frontline therapeutic options to treat type 2 diabetes mellitus and have also been validated as having compelling anti-inflammatory and cardiovascular protective properties. Data is limited on the impact of GLP-1RA on outcomes of patients with AAA. The aim of this study is to examine the association and possible impact of GLP-1RA on patients with AAA.
sections.methods: Data was sourced from the TriNetX research network, encompassing 123 health care organizations. Utilizing ICD-10 and CPT codes, we identified patients with AAA who received abdominal imaging every six months. Group 1 was comprised of patients who were treated with GLP-1RA while Group 2 patients were not. Propensity-score-matching (PSM) was used in a 1:1 fashion using age, sex, diabetes, metformin use, hypertension, cardiac disease, tobacco use, chronic kidney disease, and pulmonary disease as covariates. Primary outcomes were aneurysm rupture or repair. Secondary outcomes include mortality and major adverse cardiac events (MACE; myocardial infarction, stroke, and heart failure). Standard statistical methods were used as appropriate.
sections.results: We identified 412,490 patients with diagnosis of AAA who were undergoing 6-month surveillance between June 1, 2010 and April 16, 2024. After PSM, the GLP-1RA group (N=13,722) underwent fewer elective repairs at each timepoint (1.5% vs 2.3% at 2 years, 2.1% vs 3.0% at 5 years, P<.01) and had significantly fewer ruptures at two years (1.1% vs 1.8%, P<.01) and five years (1.6% vs 2.4%, P<.01) when compared to Group 2 (N=13,722). Group 1 also experienced significantly fewer MACE and all-cause mortality at two and five years. On multivariate analysis, GLP-1RA significantly reduced the risk of undergoing elective repair (HR 0.757, 95% CI [0.636-0.902], P<.01), rupture (HR 0.538, 95% CI [0.418-0.691], P<.01), all-cause mortality (HR 0.474, 95% CI [0.439-0.511], P<.001), and MACE (HR 0.825, 95% CI [0.794-0.857], P<.01) at 5 years.
sections.conclusion: The use of GLP-1RA in patients with AAA is associated with fewer ruptures, elective repairs, and improved rates of MACE and death. A prospective analysis may further elucidate if GLP-1RA should be prescribed to reduce the rate of aneurysm growth.

items.title: Outcomes of Calcanectomy in Diabetic Foot Ulcers and Calcaneal Osteomyelitis: A Systematic Review.

sections.objective: Diabetic Foot Ulcers (DFU) and calcaneal osteomyelitis present a formidable management challenge in limb reconstruction and preservation. Calcanectomy has emerged as an intermediate limb-preserving option. It aims to eliminate infection and allows wound closure without a need for major amputation. The aim of this review is to evaluate the outcomes of calcanectomy performed for DFU and osteomyelitis.
sections.methods: A systematic search of MEDLINE and Embase. Studies were restricted to English-language publications from 2020 onwards. The primary outcomes were limb salvage and major amputation rates. Secondary outcomes included wound healing, time to complete healing, post-operative complications, re-operation and mortality.
sections.results: Fifteen studies published between 2020 and 2025 were included, encompassing 503 patients undergoing partial, total, or vertical contour calcanectomy. Calcanectomy was associated with favourable rates of limb preservation with limb salvage exceeding 80% in 9 of the 15 studies (range: 40.0% to 100%). The highest reported major amputation rate was 60.0%. Complete wound healing rates ranged from 33.4% to 100%, with healing times ranging from 3.6 weeks to 7 months. Re-operation rates ranged from 0% to 62.8%, while postoperative infection spanned from 0% to 83.3%. Mortality ranged from 0% to 37.5%, reaching 43.3% at the five-year mark. Included literature carried a low-to-moderate risk of bias.
sections.conclusion: These findings support calcanectomy as a potentially valid alternative to major lower-limb amputation. Considerable heterogeneity in technique, outcome definitions and follow-up limits direct comparison. Prospective, multicentre studies with standardised reporting are needed to refine patient selection, optimal technique and confirm long-term functional benefit.

items.title: The prevalence and long-term clinical significance of left common iliac vein compression by the right common iliac artery in an asymptomatic population.

sections.objective: To investigate the prevalence of left common iliac vein (LCIV) compression between the right common iliac artery and L5 vertebra in an asymptomatic cohort, and determine whether individuals with ≥50% LCIV stenosis develop chronic venous insufficiency (CVI) or deep venous thrombosis (DVT).
sections.methods: Retrospective cohort study with prospective long-term clinical follow-up METHODS: Iliac venous anatomy was analysed on protocolised computed tomography (CT) in healthy individuals assessed for live related kidney donation at a tertiary referral centre between January 2012 and January 2019, with follow-up until January 2026. Scripted phone interviews assessed left leg venous symptoms, signs, investigations and treatment.
sections.results: Of 102 participants, 60 were female (58.8%), median age was 38 years (IQR 30-45), mean body mass index was 26.6 ± 4.2. Mean LCIV compression was 39.2% ± 18.5. Female sex (OR 3.52, CI 1.36-10.1, p=0.009) and younger age (OR 0.91, CI 0.86-0.96, p<0.001) were independently associated with ≥50% LCIV compression. 39 participants (38.2%) had ≥50% LCIV compression; one participant (1%) had ≥70% LCIV compression. One participant developed a right leg DVT. No others underwent venous imaging for CVI or DVT over a median 11-year follow-up (IQR 9.1-12.7). Of 13 participants with ≥50% LCIV compression surveyed, three reported left leg varicosities and three reported an episode of isolated leg swelling without investigation or treatment.
sections.conclusion: LCIV compression is common on supine CT in healthy, asymptomatic individuals, particularly young females. On long term follow-up, no clinically significant left leg venous sequelae were identified in those with ≥50% LCIV compression. Hence, caution is advised when reporting this finding on CT to avoid unnecessary investigation or intervention.

items.title: Ophthalmic Encounters After Tamoxifen Initiation.

sections.objective: Tamoxifen can cause retinal toxicity and vision loss, yet no formal screening guideline exists in the US. To characterize ophthalmic use after tamoxifen initiation, identify predictors, and compare 12-month use between those with breast cancer taking tamoxifen and those taking aromatase inhibitors.
sections.methods: This was a retrospective cohort study conducted May to June 2026 using All of Us data with 365-day minimum follow-up. The setting was a US multisite research program. Participants included adults with a first tamoxifen prescription recorded in All of Us, excluding those taking hydroxychloroquine. The comparator included those with breast cancer taking aromatase inhibitors.
sections.results: Among 2327 individuals taking tamoxifen (mean [SD] age, 53.8 [10.6] years; 2232 [95.9%] female), 162 (7.0%) had an ophthalmic encounter within 12 months, and 39 (1.7%) underwent retinal OCT or fundus photography. Among participants with preexisting glaucoma or diabetic retinopathy, 22 of 88 (25.0%) had an encounter vs 140 of 2239 (6.3%) without either condition (difference, 18.7 percentage points; 95% CI, 10.8-28.8 percentage points; P < .001). Preexisting glaucoma (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 3.87; 95% CI, 2.12-7.06; P < .001), greater preindex health care use (aOR, 1.43; 95% CI, 1.24-1.63; P < .001), and older age (aOR per 10-year increase, 1.21; 95% CI, 1.04-1.42; P = .02) were associated with greater use. Among participants with breast cancer, 126 of 1886 individuals taking tamoxifen (6.7%) had an encounter vs 240 of 2809 individuals taking aromatase inhibitors (8.5%; difference, -1.9 percentage points; 95% CI, -3.4 to -0.3 percentage points; P = .02). After adjustment, tamoxifen use was not associated with greater ophthalmic use (aOR, 1.10; 95% CI, 0.85-1.42; P = .46).
sections.conclusion: Results of this cohort study suggest that ophthalmic use after tamoxifen initiation was uncommon, and retinal-specific testing was rare. Tamoxifen use was not associated with greater adjusted 12-month use than aromatase inhibitor use. Additional evidence on retinopathy incidence, natural history, screening strategies, and clinical benefit is needed to inform guidance.
sections.other: Tamoxifen or aromatase inhibitor initiation. The primary outcome was any ophthalmic encounter within 12 months, identified from eye examination, retinal procedure, and eye visit codes. Retinal optical coherence tomography (OCT) or fundus photography was secondary. Logistic regression assessed predictors and compared treatment groups after adjustment for demographics, preexisting conditions, preindex health care use, region, and initiation year.

items.title: Bi-Allelic PRKCZ Loss-of-Function Variants and Adult-Onset Retinitis Pigmentosa.

sections.objective: Inherited retinal diseases are genetically heterogeneous disorders, with retinitis pigmentosa (RP) representing the most common form; although more than 90 genes have been implicated, many RP cases remain molecularly unsolved. To describe an adult-onset RP phenotype associated with loss-of-function variants in PRKCZ, profile the clinical features of this disorder, and investigate the underlying disease mechanism.
sections.methods: In this case series study, genomic analyses were performed in individuals with unsolved childhood- and adult-onset retinal disease recruited through international research and diagnostic programs. Detailed clinical characterization was conducted in affected individuals. In vitro analyses were carried out to validate the genomic findings using primary and transduced cell-based experimental approaches. Genomic analyses were performed from October 2023 to December 2025; functional studies were carried out from January 2024 to May 2026.
sections.results: Among approximately 4500 individuals with unsolved childhood- and adult-onset retinal disease tested, 6 bi-allelic PRKCZ variants were identified in 13 affected individuals from 10 unrelated families, 5 of which were predicted to lead to loss of function (frameshift, nonsense, or splice-altering variants). Six of 13 affected individuals (46%) were female. Most cases carried a recurrent frameshift variant (c.139_140del; p.Met47Valfs*19). All variants selectively affected the long PRKCZ transcript encoding the N-terminal Phox and Bem1 (PB1) domain. Clinically, PRKCZ-associated RP showed adult onset (18-49 years), progressive night blindness, peripheral visual field constriction, and eventual central vision loss. Four individuals exhibited adult-onset sensorineural hearing loss. Functional studies in patient-derived fibroblasts demonstrated selective loss of the long PRKCZ isoform, impaired ciliogenesis, and altered mitochondrial organization, which were validated in stable PRKCZ knockdown cell lines. Structural modeling and coimmunoprecipitation assays indicated that the missense variant was associated with the disruption of PB1 domain-mediated protein-protein interactions.
sections.conclusion: In this case series study, bi-allelic inactivating variants in PRKCZ were associated with adult-onset RP with an isoform-specific mechanism involving the long retinal-enriched transcript. These findings expand the genetic spectrum of RP and highlight PRKCZ as a potentially clinically relevant gene implicated in adult-onset retinal degeneration.
sections.other: Bi-allelic likely pathogenic variants in a novel RP disease gene candidate, PRKCZ. The primary outcome was genetic, clinical, and functional effects of bi-allelic PRKCZ inactivating variants associated with adult-onset RP. A detailed ophthalmologic assessment was conducted to characterize the clinical phenotype. Functional analyses in patient-derived fibroblasts and transduced cell lines were performed to validate the consequence of disruptive variants on PRKCZ transcript processing and PKCζ function.

items.title: Visual Field and RNFL OCT Testing Among Rural and Urban Residents With Glaucoma.

sections.objective: Rural populations face disparities in eye care; therefore, understanding the utilization of structural imaging and visual field (VF) testing for glaucoma monitoring among rural compared with urban patients is important. To evaluate whether rural residence and sociodemographic factors are associated with patterns of VF testing and retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL) optical coherence tomography (OCT) in patients with glaucoma.
sections.methods: This retrospective longitudinal cohort study used data from the Sight Outcomes Research Collaborative (SOURCE) consortium, a multi-institutional repository of US academic ophthalmic clinical data, from May 2012 to January 2025. Included patients had at least 2 separate dates of glaucoma billing codes, at least 3 years of follow-up data, and at least 1 VF or RNFL OCT test.
sections.results: Among 48 196 patients, 45 843 (95.1%) lived in urban areas (25 613 [55.9%] female; mean [SD] age, 67.78 [12.71] years) and 2353 (4.9%) lived in rural areas (1272 [54.1%] female; mean [SD] age, 67.3 [12.03] years). Mean (SD) VF testing frequency was 0.91 (0.52) tests per year among rural patients and 0.91 (0.56) among urban patients; rural residence was not associated with regular VF monitoring (adjusted odds ratio [AOR], 0.95; 95% CI, 0.88-1.04; P = .28). Rural residence was associated with lower RNFL OCT frequency (mean [SD], 0.57 [0.45] vs 0.63 [0.47] tests per year; difference, -0.06 [95% CI, -0.08 to -0.04] tests per year; adjusted incidence rate ratio, 0.93 [95% CI, 0.88-0.98]; P = .004) and lower odds of regular RNFL OCT monitoring (AOR, 0.82; 95% CI, 0.74-0.90; P < .001). Medicaid insurance was associated with lower odds of regular monitoring with VF (AOR, 0.35; 95% CI, 0.30-0.40; P < .001) and RNFL OCT (AOR, 0.62; 95% CI, 0.52-0.74; P < .001).
sections.conclusion: In this cohort study, rural residence was associated with lower utilization of RNFL OCT but not VF testing, while Medicaid insurance was associated with lower odds of monitoring for both modalities. The findings suggest that ophthalmologists should be aware that rural patients with glaucoma may require additional attention to continuity of structural imaging.
sections.other: Rural vs urban residence, categorized by Rural-Urban Commuting Area codes. Primary outcomes were utilization frequency (tests per year) and regular monitoring (≥1 test every 18 months) for VF and RNFL OCT. Testing frequency was analyzed using multivariable negative binomial regression, and regular monitoring was analyzed using logistic regression adjusted for sociodemographic characteristics and baseline visual acuity.

items.title: Autophagy in macrophages curtails IL-1α-mediated immune priming against lung infections.
items.abstract: Host resistance to infection is initially determined by how well primed the innate immune system is to respond on first exposure to an invader, yet the mechanisms underlying this priming remain incompletely understood. Here we found that basal autophagy suppressed the expression of Il1a in alveolar macrophages (AMs) and an otherwise protective innate immune priming against Staphylococcus aureus and influenza A virus (IAV), independently of the microbiome and adaptive immunity. Inactivating autophagy genes in AMs led to elevated expression of IL-1α in AMs, which subsequently enhanced IL-1R-MyD88 signaling in neutrophils and increased the recruitment of myeloid cells to the lung. As a result, autophagy-deficient mice showed more efficient clearance of S. aureus along with reduced lung damage and inflammation. Similar to genetic inactivation of autophagy, overexpression of IL-1α in AMs conferred broad spectrum protection against S. aureus and IAV, suggesting a possible strategy to fine-tune immune responses to combat important respiratory infections.

items.title: Single-cell imaging of the lytic phage life cycle in bacteria.
items.abstract: Upon infecting a bacterial cell, a lytic bacteriophage commandeers the host's resources to replicate, before lysing the cell to release new virions. As phages are obligate parasites, each stage of the infection process depends on the physiological parameters of the host cell. Given the inherent physiological variability within a population of genetically identical bacterial cells, we ask how the phage infection dynamic reflects such heterogeneity. Here, we introduce a time-lapse imaging assay for investigating the dynamics of individual infection steps by a single T7 phage on a single bacterium. This high-throughput, time-resolved assay enables us to monitor the infection progression simultaneously in multiple cells, uncovering substantial heterogeneity at each step and revealing correlations between infection dynamics and the physiological state of the infected cell. Simulations of competing phage populations reveal that heterogeneity in infection dynamics can significantly impact phage fitness, highlighting it as a potential evolutionary driver of phage-bacteria interactions. A record of this paper's transparent peer review process is included in the supplemental information.

items.title: Microbial products trigger chemosensory dialogues through intestinal G protein-coupled receptors.
items.abstract: Organismal reactions to changing environmental conditions require information relays that sense cues and elicit appropriate responses. G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs), including olfactory receptors, comprise the largest receptor family that recognizes environmental cues, consisting of over 800 genes in the human genome. Here, by screening libraries of gut metabolites and natural products using a multiplexed GPCR reporter system, GPCR-seq, we reveal multiple intestinal chemosensory pathways. Among these, we determine that a cyclic fatty acid promotes serotonin production from enterochromaffin cells via olfactory receptor OR51E1. Two additional gut microbe-derived molecules, a β-carboline and 6-hydroxynicotinic acid (6-HNA), function as agonists for GPR35, a receptor linked to inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). The IBD-associated GPR35 risk variant, T108M, shows aberrant responses to 6-HNA, while Enterocloster bolteae, a species increased in IBD, generates high levels of 6-HNA. This approach provides an accelerated path to mapping critical chemosensory pathways and host physiological responses.

items.title: Prevalence and spectrum of skin diseases in adults in China: a nationwide cross-sectional study.

sections.objective: Skin diseases have been identified as a public health priority at the 78th World Health Assembly, with a call for strengthened national surveillance and evidence-based responses. However, in China, comprehensive national epidemiological data on the prevalence of skin diseases have been lacking. We aimed to bridge this data gap by conducting the China Skin Health study, a large-scale, population-based, cross-sectional study.
sections.methods: In this study, we used a multistage stratified cluster random sampling design to obtain a nationally representative sample of adults aged 18 years or older from diverse geographical regions of China. We collaborated with provincial centres for disease control and prevention to establish a survey team comprising public health workers and ten to 12 certified dermatologists in each of the five provinces selected for the study. Residents' committees disseminated study information through posters and WeChat groups to recruit participants, and data were collected at local community health centres. Standardised electronic questionnaires were administered by trained interviewers to collect information on demographic and other characteristics. Certified dermatologists examined sun-exposed areas (eg, scalp, face, neck, and extremities) in all participants, as well as unexposed areas reported as concerns by respondents, for common skin diseases spanning 12 categories and more than 60 specific conditions. Clinical diagnoses were made on the basis of observed skin manifestations. The total number of skin conditions was recorded for each participant, and the mean number of skin conditions was calculated. Point prevalence of skin diseases was defined as the proportion of participants with a dermatologist-confirmed diagnosis of any listed condition at the time of the survey. Sampling weights derived from the study sampling framework and the 2020 National Population Census were applied when calculating prevalence and conducting logistic regression analyses. The absolute number of dermatological cases nationwide was estimated by applying prevalence estimates to the 2020 Chinese census data.
sections.results: From July 1, 2022, to June 27, 2024, 153 593 participants completed the survey and were included in the analysis. The study population had a mean age of 48·5 years (SD 16·8), with 75 512 (49·2%) men and 78 081 (50·8%) women; 98 926 (64·4%) participants resided in urban areas. The age-standardised prevalence of skin diseases was 55·6% (95% CI 51·2-59·9), corresponding to an estimated 618 million (95% CI 567-666) affected adults in China, with a mean of 0·98 (SD 1·22) skin diseases per person. Prevalence increased with age, from 42·0% (95% CI 35·3-48·6) in those aged 18-29 years to 79·5% (75·8-83·1) in those aged 80 years or older (p<0·0001 for trend). Skin diseases were more common in women (56·5%, 51·8-61·1) than in men (54·6%, 50·5-58·7; p=0·023) and more prevalent in southern China (62·5%, 56·2-68·9) than in northern China (47·4%, 43·2-51·7; p<0·0001). Benign cutaneous tumours were the most prevalent type of condition (31·1%, 28·7-33·5), followed by superficial fungal infections (15·0%, 12·5-17·5); dermatitis, eczema, and allergic dermatoses (9·0%, 7·8-10·1); pigmentary dermatoses (7·9%, 6·3-9·6); and sebaceous and sweat gland dermatoses (5·7%, 5·0-6·4). Factors associated with skin diseases included female sex, increasing age, residence in southern China, current or former smoking, current or former alcohol consumption, overweight or obesity, a history of allergies, and a history of photosensitivity. Despite the substantial burden, only 5·8% (4·5-7·3) of affected individuals had sought medical care, and 18·2% (16·7-19·9) had used over-the-counter medications in the past year.
sections.conclusion: Skin diseases could affect more than half of Chinese adults. These findings highlight a substantial unmet need and should inform national priorities.

items.title: Trends, ethnic inequalities, and determinants of multiple nutrition-related health outcomes among Chinese children and adolescents aged 7-18 years: evidence from four national school health surveys, 2005-19.

sections.objective: Eliminating all forms of malnutrition is essential for optimal child and adolescent development. In multi-ethnic China, nutrition-related conditions coexist, but ethnic-group patterns remain unclear. We assessed trends, between-ethnic inequalities, and co-occurrence among the Han majority and 26 ethnic minority groups.
sections.methods: We analysed four cross-sectional national school health surveys from 2005 to 2019, including 1 201 557 students aged 7-18 years. We estimated age-standardised and sex-standardised prevalence, ethnicity-level sociodemographic index (SDI) inequalities, and co-occurrence; anaemia analyses included 389 124 participants aged 7, 9, 12, and 14 years. Contextual associations and model-based population-attributable fractions (PAFs) were examined.
sections.results: Between 2005 and 2019, overweight and obesity increased from 9·77% (95% CI 9·67-9·88) to 20·06% (19·92-20·20), obesity from 3·27% (3·21-3·34) to 8·18% (8·08-8·28), and high blood pressure from 8·81% (8·71-8·90) to 13·39% (13·28-13·51); stunting declined from 5·16% (5·08-5·24) to 2·12% (2·07-2·17) and thinness from 4·86% (4·78-4·94) to 2·55% (2·50-2·61), whereas anaemia remained prevalent (9·42% [9·24-9·60] in 2005 vs 10·40% [10·20-10·59] in 2019). Stunting remained concentrated among lower-SDI ethnic groups, whereas obesity and overweight and obesity were concentrated among higher-SDI groups and absolute inequalities widened. Among children with anaemia, overweight and obesity increased from 7·89% (7·32-8·46) to 18·19% (17·37-19·01); among those with stunting, overweight and obesity increased from 2·44% (2·18-2·70) to 6·89% (6·15-7·62). Higher education, health, and urbanisation indicators were associated with lower stunting odds; model-based joint PAFs were 16·39% for obesity and 22·01% for high blood pressure.
sections.conclusion: Across multi-ethnic China, the nutrition transition remains incomplete, with anaemia remaining common, stunting declining but persisting in some ethnic groups, and overweight and obesity and high blood pressure rising. Ethnic heterogeneity and increasing within-person co-occurrence of nutrition-related outcomes reveal an increasingly complex burden and limits of single-condition approaches, calling for integrated surveillance and tailored responses.

items.title: Novel dengue serotype 4 live virus human challenge: a phase 1 dose optimisation and homologous rechallenge study.

sections.objective: Dengue live virus human challenges (LVHCs) are key in dengue vaccine and pharmacological development, to down-select candidates and provide a useful platform for understanding viral-host immunology in a controlled setting. The primary aim of this study was to assess the safety, reactogenicity, and immunogenicity of a newly derived underattenuated dengue virus serotype-4-LVHC (DENV-4-LVHC) strain intended for future dengue challenge studies.
sections.methods: We conducted a first-in-human, phase 1, non-randomised, open-label study that evaluated the safety and optimised dose of the DENV-4-LVHC strain H-241 in flavivirus-naive healthy adult volunteers. The trial was conducted between April 28, 2022, and Dec 18, 2023, at the University of Maryland (Baltimore, MD, USA) and included a dose-optimisation study in which participants were enrolled into staggered-start, dose-ranging cohorts, beginning with the lowest dose, and homologous rechallenge substudy in which willing, primary-infected participants were rechallenged with the optimised dose of DENV-4 at least 12 months from the primary challenge. Successful challenge was defined as more than 90% participants developing self-limiting mild-to-moderate dengue symptoms with detectable RNAemia. Participants were analysed on the basis of the treatment group (primary infection vs rechallenge). This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (Identifier: NCT05268302).
sections.results: 14 healthy adult participants were enrolled between March 31, 2022, and June 9, 2022 (dose optimisation), and were challenged with a subcutaneous dose of DENV-4-LVHC on June 12, 2023 (rechallenge). The majority were men (11 [79%] of 14), and almost half were non-White (6 [43%]). The mean participant age was 33·6 years (range 20-48). All 14 participants developed viraemia and symptoms consistent with self-limited, mild-to-moderate dengue at an optimised dose of 95 plaque-forming units (low dose). Six (60%) participants (of the original ten from the 2022 cohort) were rechallenged using the optimised dose 1 year after primary challenge, and none developed detectable dengue. Robust antibody responses, plasmablast expansion, and antiviral gene upregulation were seen during primary infection but not after rechallenge. No severe dengue, need for inpatient observation, or dengue challenge-related serious adverse events were observed.
sections.conclusion: DENV-4-LVHC was found to be safe and highly predictable for use in future challenge studies, to evaluate vaccine and therapeutic candidates. Immunity from previous DENV-4-LVHC infection conferred protection following homologous rechallenge 1 year after primary exposure.

items.title: Clinical and immunological correlates of CXCR4 coreceptor use in people with HIV-1 receiving antiretroviral therapy in the Netherlands: a multicentre cohort study.

sections.objective: CXCR4-using (X4) viruses are associated with faster disease progression in untreated HIV-1 infection, although their clinical, virological, and immunological correlates during suppressive antiretroviral therapy are not well characterised. We aimed to assess the associations between X4 coreceptor use and clinical outcomes, HIV persistence, and immunological profiles in people with HIV-1 receiving suppressive antiretroviral therapy.
sections.methods: In this multicentre cohort study, asymptomatic adults with HIV receiving suppressive antiretroviral therapy were enrolled from four HIV treatment centres in the Netherlands between Oct 16, 2019, and Oct 27, 2021 and followed up for 2 years. Clinical data were obtained from structured questionnaires and electronic health records. HIV-1 coreceptor use was predicted from triplicate env sequencing with Geno2pheno, and participants were classified as having CCR5-using (R5), X4, or mixed virus. HIV-1 subtype was assigned using env and pol sequences. Total and intact HIV DNA in CD4+ T cells were quantified using multiplex digital PCR. Plasma proteomics, bulk peripheral blood mononuclear cell transcriptomics, and high-dimensional flow cytometry were used for systems-level profiling. Associations between predicted coreceptor use and clinical outcomes, HIV-reservoir measures, and immunological profiles were assessed using adjusted regression models and discovery and validation cohorts.
sections.results: Coreceptor use was assigned in 1724 participants; 1222 had R5 virus, 336 had X4 virus, and 166 had mixed classifications. Primary clinical analyses included 1494 participants, of whom 1172 were in the R5 group and 322 were in the X4 group. Compared with the R5 group, the X4 group had a lower CD4+ nadir, a higher prevalence of previous AIDS-defining events, poorer immunological recovery, and more comorbidities, particularly type 2 diabetes and non-affective psychiatric disorders. The median total HIV DNA was 1051 copies per 106 CD4+ T cells in the X4 group versus 599 copies per 106 CD4+ T cells in the R5 group, and the median intact HIV DNA was 23 copies per 106 CD4+ T cells versus 15 copies per 106 CD4+ T cells. No significant differences were observed in plasma inflammatory proteins. Participants in the X4 group had higher frequencies of activated CD4+ T cells and PD-1+ regulatory T cells, and transcriptomic analyses identified downregulation of two validated transcripts involved in transcriptional repression and lipid hydrolysis.
sections.conclusion: Among people with HIV receiving suppressive antiretroviral therapy, infection with X4 virus was associated with markers of more advanced previous HIV disease, impaired immune recovery, larger HIV reservoirs, and selected comorbidities despite viral suppression. Coreceptor use might therefore help to contextualise clinical, virological, and immunological heterogeneity in treated HIV-1 infection and could be relevant to future HIV cure studies.

items.title: Long-term evaluation of the effectiveness and safety of autologous haematopoietic stem-cell transplantation for systemic sclerosis (NISSC1-LTE): a cohort study.

sections.objective: Systemic sclerosis is a rare and heterogeneous chronic autoimmune disease. It has the highest mortality of the rheumatic diseases and few treatment options exist. Autologous haematopoietic stem-cell transplantation (HSCT) is an effective and established therapeutic option in selected patients with early severe systemic sclerosis. This study aimed to evaluate the long-term safety and effectiveness of autologous HSCT in patients with systemic sclerosis in real-life clinical practice.
sections.methods: This cohort study (NISSC1-LTE) followed up patients with systemic sclerosis included in the prospective European Society for Blood and Marrow Transplantation NISSC1 study who had undergone their first autologous HSCT for severe progressive systemic sclerosis. Follow-up data were collected from 13 participating centres in France, Germany, Netherlands, Italy, Spain, Switzerland, and Brazil. Participating centres completed a yearly case report form for each patient alive after 2 years and up to 10 years after autologous HSCT. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival, defined as survival from baseline without evidence of systemic sclerosis progression. Late complications after autologous HSCT, including malignancies, secondary autoimmune diseases, infections, and major adverse cardiovascular events were also analysed. People with lived experience of systemic sclerosis were involved in the design and conduct of this study. The NISSC1 study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT02516124) and is complete.
sections.results: All 80 patients with systemic sclerosis who had an autologous HSCT between Dec 4, 2012, and Jan 19, 2016, were included in this long-term extension study. 12 patients were lost to follow-up, including five patients with a follow-up less than 5 years. Median age at autologous HSCT was 43 years (IQR 33-51), 57 (71%) of 80 patients were female, 23 (29%) were male, and median follow-up was 9·2 years (IQR 8·9-9·6) after autologous HSCT. Progression-free survival was 81% (95% CI 71-88) at 2 years, 72% (61-81) at 5 years, and 60% (47-71) at 10 years. 18 patients died during the study; causes of death were autologous HSCT-related in five (6%) of 80 patients, disease progression in nine (11%) patients, post-autologous HSCT malignancy in two (3%) patients, and late serious infection in two (3%) patients. 34 (43%) of 80 patients maintained remission without immunosuppressive treatment over 10 years.
sections.conclusion: This study provides long-term follow-up data after autologous HSCT in patients with systemic sclerosis allowing robust assessment of response rate, late complications, and sustained treatment benefit. The extended timeframe might serve as an important comparator for all upcoming, cellular treatment options.

items.title: Impact of a large measles outbreak associated with transmission in the Americas and Canada's loss of measles elimination status: descriptive cohort study.

sections.objective: To describe the epidemiological characteristics, public health response, and evidence of international spread of a large measles outbreak that contributed to the loss of Canada's measles elimination status.
sections.methods: Descriptive analysis of the cohort of measles outbreak cases reported to Ontario's public health surveillance system during the outbreak period: epidemiological week of 28 October 2024 to 6 October 2025. Individuals meeting the outbreak case definition for confirmed or probable measles infection during the outbreak period.
sections.results: The outbreak consisted of 2377 cases (2064 confirmed and 313 probable) over 49 weeks and contributed to the loss of Canada's measles elimination status. Most cases (2146/2377, 90.3%) occurred among members of historically under-vaccinated communities, with limited spillover into the broader population. Among the 2377 cases, approximately three quarters of cases (n=1736, 73.0%) occurred in individuals aged 19 years or younger, 2121 (89.2%) were unvaccinated, and 97 (4.1%) had unknown vaccination status. The outbreak was associated with 166 (7%) admissions to hospital, 13 (<1%) admissions to intensive care unit, 51 (2.1%) infections during pregnancy, 10 (<1%) congenital measles infections, one (<1%) case of encephalitis, and one (<1%) infant death. Sequencing identified a novel N450 distinct sequence identifier that was subsequently detected in countries including the United States of America, Mexico, and the Netherlands. The outbreak strain was designated a World Health Organization named strain (MVs/Ontario.CAN/47.24).
sections.conclusion: These findings highlight the risk of measles re-establishment in countries that have attained elimination and underscore the importance of culturally appropriate community engagement to build trust in immunisation and prevent future outbreaks. This outbreak shows the fragility of measles elimination in the presence of long standing immunity gaps within interconnected communities across the Americas and the population-level protection that limited broader community transmission.
sections.other: Ontario, Canada. Exposure to measles virus associated with the Ontario outbreak and related transmission chains. Demographic characteristics, vaccination status, admission to hospital, complications, pregnancy associated outcomes, mortality, and evidence of international spread based on measles virus genotyping and sequencing. Cases were identified using an outbreak-specific case definition incorporating epidemiological, clinical, laboratory, and viral sequencing criteria. Phylogenetic analysis of measles virus sequences was used to assess evidence of onwards spread to other countries.

items.title: Efficacy and cost effectiveness of high volume injections with and without corticosteroid compared with sham for midportion Achilles tendinopathy (Inject trial): randomised controlled trial.

sections.objective: To test the efficacy and cost effectiveness of high volume injections with and without corticosteroid versus sham injection for midportion Achilles tendinopathy.
sections.methods: Single centred, participant and assessor masked, three arm randomised controlled trial (Inject trial). From 5 December 2019 and 24 July 2022, 192 adults (18 years or older) diagnosed with midportion Achilles tendinopathy were randomly assigned (1:1:1) to sham (n=64), high volume injection without corticosteroid (n=63), or high volume injection with corticosteroid (n=65). Participants were allocated to sham injection (2-3 mL 0.5% bupivacaine hydrochloride), high volume injection with corticosteroid (50 mL saline and 0.5% bupivacaine with 25 mg hydrocortisone in the first 10 mL), or high volume injection with no corticosteroid (same solution but without hydrocortisone). They received the same exercise programme, education, and activity modification advice.
sections.results: VISA-A data were obtained from 181 (94%) of 192 participants at 12 months. No clear differences were noted between sham and high volume injection either with (-3.5 (98.33% confidence interval -12.0 to 5.0)) or without corticosteroid (4.0 (-4.2 to 12.3)), and between the two injections (-7.5 (-15.3 to 0.3)), at 12 months. The point estimate was closest to the target difference for the comparison between injections and favoured the arm without steroid. The only differences observed on VISA-A at intermediate time points were a benefit for high volume with corticosteroid versus sham at six weeks (9.2 (1.5 to 16.9)) but worse outcomes for high volume injection with corticosteroid versus high volume injection with no corticosteroid at 26 weeks (-8.6 (-16.4 to -0.7)). The health economic analysis found high volume injection with corticosteroid to be less costly than the sham with similar effectiveness based on quality-adjusted life-years (>0.90 probability of being cost effective at $AUD50 000 and $100 000 willingness-to-pay thresholds). No serious trial related adverse events were recorded.
sections.conclusion: High volume injections with or without corticosteroids did not improve pain or disability compared with sham at 12 months. Although high volume injections with corticosteroid showed short term clinical benefit and potential reduction in healthcare costs over a year, they were associated with worse longer term clinical outcomes. The clinical data do not support routine use for high volume injections with corticosteroid for midportion Achilles tendinopathy.
sections.other: Community. The primary clinical outcome was pain and disability using the validated VISA-A and the primary endpoint was at 52 weeks. The economic outcome was cost per quality-adjusted life-years from a societal perspective.

items.title: The 2026 report of the Lancet Countdown on health and climate change: a decade of escalating health harms and a decisive moment for all.
items.abstract: For the French, Arabic, Spanish, Brazilian-Portuguese and Mandarin translations of the abstract see Supplementary Materials section.

items.title: Crosstalk along the gut-liver axis in liver disease: Clinical and mechanistic aspects.
items.abstract: The gut and liver are anatomically and physiologically interconnected, forming a dynamic axis that plays a central role in the pathogenesis of many liver diseases. Gut-derived factors can influence hepatic injury, inflammation, and fibrosis, acting both as disease modifiers and, in some cases, as primary drivers of aetiology. Conversely, liver-derived factors including bile acids shape microbial ecology, epithelial barrier function, and intestinal immune homeostasis. In this review, we provide an overview of the clinical and mechanistic aspects of the gut-liver axis in hepatology. Using autoimmune, metabolic, and toxic hepatobiliary disorders as model conditions, we highlight recent advances in understanding how intestinal permeability, microbiota composition, and immune signalling contribute to disease initiation and progression. Emphasis is placed on the bidirectional nature of gut-liver interactions and their implications for disease stratification, prevention, and therapy. Finally, we identify key knowledge gaps and outline priorities for future research in this rapidly evolving field.

items.title: 3D Corneal and Retinal Bioprinting: Tissue Engineering Strategies, Translational Challenges, and Clinical Opportunities.
items.abstract: Three-dimensional bioprinting has emerged as a promising strategy for addressing major unmet needs in ophthalmology, including the global shortage of donor corneal tissue and the absence of restorative therapies for retinal degenerative disease. Advances in biomaterials, stem cell biology, and biofabrication have enabled increasingly sophisticated ocular constructs, ranging from engineered corneal grafts to multicellular retinal models that recapitulate key aspects of native tissue architecture. However, substantial challenges remain in reproducing the optical, mechanical, and biological functions required for clinical translation. This review critically evaluates the current state of corneal and retinal bioprinting through a framework organized around tissue target, fabrication modality, and intended application. Major bioprinting approaches, including extrusion-based, laser-assisted, drop-on-demand, and light-based technologies, are compared with respect to resolution, cell compatibility, scalability, and translational potential. Particular emphasis is placed on the engineering constraints governing construct fidelity, bioink design, tissue integration, and long-term functional performance. Current evidence suggests that corneal and retinal bioprinting have progressed along distinct translational trajectories. Corneal bioprinting has achieved encouraging preclinical outcomes, with selected approaches entering early clinical evaluation, whereas retinal bioprinting has generated highly informative disease models but remains at an earlier stage of translational development. Across both tissues, the field has increasingly shifted from reproducing individual cellular components toward reconstructing the biological interfaces and multicellular systems that underlie tissue function. Future progress will depend on establishing functional validation frameworks, reproducible manufacturing workflows, and standardized benchmarks to support the clinical development of vision-restoring bioprinted constructs.

items.title: Subspecialty ILD Clinic Care is Associated with More Guideline-Concordant Evaluation and Improved Outcomes Compared to Other Ambulatory Settings: A Retrospective Cohort Study.

sections.objective: Subspecialty interstitial lung disease (ILD) clinics are associated with improved outcomes, yet access remains uneven. Even within tertiary health systems, patients with ILD are managed across diverse ambulatory settings, with unclear implications for care and outcomes.
sections.methods: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of adults with ILD at a large academic medical center. Identified patients were stratified by care in a subspecialty ILD clinic versus non-specialty setting. Demographic, diagnostic testing, treatment, health care utilization, and survival data were extracted from the electronic health record. Diagnostic and treatment measures were analyzed using multivariable logistic regression. Hospitalization, emergency department visit, and death were analyzed as time-to-event outcomes.
sections.results: Among 6,637 patients with ILD, 4,371 (66%) were seen in the subspecialty ILD clinic. The 2,266 patients (34%) managed in non-specialty settings were more likely to identify as Black or Latinx, reside in more socioeconomically deprived neighborhoods, and have an unspecified ILD diagnosis (all p < 0.001). In the peri-diagnostic period, ILD clinic care was associated with higher adjusted odds of chest CT imaging (OR 2.51, 2.07-3.05) and antifibrotic therapy (OR 1.54, 1.32-1.80), and lower odds of lung biopsy (OR 0.47, 0.32-0.68). ILD clinic care was associated with a lower adjusted hazards of all-cause hospitalization (HR 0.46, 0.42-0.51), emergency department visit (HR 0.68, 0.59-0.78), and death (HR 0.57, 0.45-0.72). P-value <0.001 for all.
sections.conclusion: Within a single health system, subspecialty ILD clinic care was associated with more guideline-concordant care and improved outcomes. Differences in access to subspecialty expertise may contribute to inequities in care delivery, underscoring the need for scalable strategies, referral optimization, telemedicine, and clinical decision support, to extend ILD expertise and improve outcomes.
sections.other: Within a single academic health system, do patient characteristics, care delivery, and outcomes differ between individuals with ILD managed in a subspecialty ILD clinic versus other ambulatory settings?

items.title: Azithromycin Exposure and Incident Nontuberculous Mycobacterial Isolation in Bronchiectasis and COPD: A Nationwide Nested Case-Control Study.

sections.objective: Azithromycin reduces exacerbations in chronic airway disease, but whether it alters the risk of nontuberculous mycobacterial (NTM) isolation is unresolved.
sections.methods: Two nationwide register-based nested case-control analyses in Denmark. Case patients had a first positive respiratory culture for NTM; controls, alive and free of prior NTM isolation on the index date, were matched 1:20 on age, sex, and comorbidity index. The prespecified exposure was at least 3,000 mg of azithromycin with at least two prescriptions redeemed in the preceding 12 months, with a 3-month lag. Conditional logistic regression was adjusted for inhaled and oral corticosteroids. Exploratory analyses examined an active comparator at matched thresholds, recency, and outcome stringency.
sections.results: The analyses comprised 173 cases and 3,409 controls (bronchiectasis) and 365 and 7,300 (COPD). Under the prespecified definition, azithromycin was not associated with incident NTM isolation (bronchiectasis: OR, 1.31; 95% CI, 0.79-2.18; COPD: 1.29; 0.78-2.13). In COPD, the OR was 1.61 (1.14-2.28) for one or more prescriptions and 1.29 (0.78-2.13) for two or more. The COPD association was concentrated within 90 days of the index date (2.55; 1.73-3.76) and attenuated with microbiological stringency (definite isolates: 0.77; 0.27-2.20). Non-macrolide antibacterials were more strongly associated than azithromycin at every matched threshold in bronchiectasis (one or more prescriptions: 1.90 [1.36-2.65] vs 1.15 [0.75-1.75]), and at the two higher thresholds in COPD (two or more: 1.48 [1.17-1.86] vs 1.24 [0.75-2.05]).
sections.conclusion: Azithromycin was not associated with NTM isolation under the prespecified definition. Associations under broader definitions were not dose-dependent and clustered close to the index date, more consistent with indication-driven testing than a drug effect, although in COPD an association with any exposure persisted after accounting for other antibacterials.
sections.other: Is azithromycin exposure in the preceding year associated with incident respiratory NTM isolation in non-cystic fibrosis bronchiectasis and in COPD?

items.title: Intraoperative Estimated Blood Loss and Perioperative Transfusion are Independently Associated with Postoperative Morbidity and Mortality After Lower Extremity Bypass.

sections.objective: Intraoperative estimated blood loss (EBL) and need for perioperative packed red blood cell (pRBC) transfusion are common during lower extremity bypass (LEB) for chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) and have each been associated with adverse postoperative outcomes. However, their joint associations with postoperative outcomes remain incompletely defined. This study aimed to evaluate the associations of EBL and perioperative pRBC transfusion, individually and jointly, with postoperative morbidity and mortality in patients undergoing LEB for CLTI.
sections.methods: A retrospective cohort study was conducted using the Society for Vascular Surgery Vascular Quality Initiative (VQI) database. Patients undergoing LEB for CLTI between 2014 and 2023 were identified. Receiver operating characteristic analysis identified an optimal EBL threshold of 225 mL (area under the curve 0.72) for predicting transfusion, which was used to stratify patients into low-EBL (<225 mL) and high-EBL (≥225 mL) groups. Primary outcomes included myocardial infarction (MI), stroke, 30-day mortality, and a composite endpoint. Multivariable logistic regression was used to assess adjusted associations across four groups defined by EBL and transfusion status. Separate model was used to evaluate the interaction between EBL and pRBC transfusion.
sections.results: Among 36,019 procedures, 58.5% had low EBL and 41.5% had high EBL. Patients who had high EBL and did not require blood transfusion had increased odds of adverse postoperative outcomes, including 30-day mortality (AOR 1.26, 95% CI [1.01, 1.59]), myocardial infarction (AOR 1.88, 95% CI [1.48, 2.39]), stroke (AOR 1.58, 95% CI [1.09, 2.29]), and the composite outcome (AOR 1.51, 95% CI [1.29, 1.78]). Patients who had low EBL and received blood transfusion had increased odds of 30-day mortality (AOR 2.46, 95% CI [1.95, 3.10]), myocardial infarction (AOR 6.57, 95% CI [5.26, 8.21]), stroke (AOR 2.75, 95% CI [1.84, 4.12]), and the composite outcome (AOR 4.08, 95% CI [3.48, 4.78]). Patients who had both high EBL and required perioperative blood transfusion demonstrated the highest odds of adverse outcomes, including 30-day mortality (AOR 2.54, 95% CI [2.09, 3.08]), myocardial infarction (AOR 7.39, 95% CI [6.08, 8.98]), stroke (AOR 3.79, 95% CI [2.76, 5.21]), and the composite outcome (AOR 4.42, 95% CI [3.87, 5.05]). Formal interaction testing demonstrated significant between EBL and transfusion.
sections.conclusion: In patients undergoing LEB for CLTI, intraoperative EBL and perioperative pRBC transfusion were both independently and jointly associated with increased postoperative morbidity and mortality. These findings identify EBL and transfusion as markers of perioperative risk and support further investigation of blood-sparing strategies and individualized transfusion practices.

items.title: Carotid Endarterectomy Versus Trans-Carotid Artery Revascularisation (TCAR) for Asymptomatic Carotid Stenosis A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

sections.objective: The treatment for asymptomatic carotid artery stenosis includes a surgical or interventional approach in selected cases. Although endarterectomy should be considered over stenting for selected patients, according to the latest European Society of Vascular Surgery (ESVS) guidelines, the Carotid Revascularization and Medical Management for Asymptomatic Carotid Stenosis Trials (CREST-2) suggested that carotid stenting would be associated with low rates of perioperative stroke or death. The transcarotid artery revascularization (TCAR) technique is a relatively new endovascular method, which involves placing a stent at the carotid bifurcation through direct carotid artery access, performed under a flow reversal system. This approach avoids manipulation of the aortic arch, potentially reducing embolic events. The aim of this systematic review is to compare TCAR with carotid endarterectomy (CEA) in asymptomatic patients undergoing carotid intervention. It seeks to evaluate whether TCAR is associated with improved perioperative outcomes, such as lower rates of stroke and death, compared with CEA, given its potentially less invasive approach.
sections.methods: The review was performed according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) on the platforms PubMed/Medline, OVID/Embase, and Scopus. The following MeSH terms were used: "asymptomatic carotid stenosis" AND "carotid endarterectomy", "transcarotid artery revascularization" OR "TCAR". Full-text screening and data extraction were performed with the support of the COVIDENCE platform. Six studies were selected for this systematic review, comprising a total of 132,684 patients (30,581 undergoing TCAR and 102,103 undergoing CEA). Statistical analysis was performed using R software.
sections.results: The selected studies for this systematic review showed similar results in terms of perioperative stroke and death for asymptomatic patients who underwent carotid endarterectomy and TCAR.
sections.conclusion: Our results suggest that there are no significant differences between CEA and TCAR for the treatment of asymptomatic patients who require a surgical or interventional approach. Further studies are necessary to provide more robust data in this field.

items.title: Long-term outcomes of cyanoacrylate closure alone versus combined high saphenous ligation and cyanoacrylate closure in large-diameter great saphenous veins.

sections.objective: Long-term evidence regarding the effectiveness of cyanoacrylate closure (CAC) in large-diameter great saphenous veins (GSVs) is limited. This study aimed to compare the long-term outcomes of CAC alone with those of combined high saphenous ligation and cyanoacrylate closure (HSL + CAC) for large-diameter GSV insufficiency.
sections.methods: This single-center retrospective cohort study evaluated 198 extremities in 180 patients treated for symptomatic GSV insufficiency between January 2018 and December 2022 who had a preoperative GSV diameter of ≥8 mm. CAC was performed in 127 extremities and HSL + CAC in 71. Clinical and long-term duplex outcomes were compared using generalized estimating equation (GEE) models that accounted for within-patient clustering and prespecified confounders. Propensity score overlap weighting (PSOW) was used as a sensitivity analysis.
sections.results: Long-term duplex follow-up data were available for 186 extremities (93.9%). HSL + CAC was associated with greater GSV occlusion (84.1% vs 65.8%; P = .007), less saphenofemoral junction (SFJ) reflux (5.8% vs 47.0%; P < .001), a lower postoperative Venous Clinical Severity Score (VCSS; 2.45 ± 2.04 vs 3.15 ± 1.89; P = .019), and greater VCSS improvement (3.45 ± 2.21 vs 1.47 ± 1.93; P < .001). Reoperation was performed in 8.7% of extremities treated with CAC alone but in none treated with HSL + CAC (P = .008). In adjusted GEE analyses, HSL + CAC was associated with a lower postoperative VCSS (β, -1.15; 95% CI, -1.71 to -0.59), greater GSV occlusion (OR, 3.05; 95% CI, 1.31-7.14), and less SFJ reflux (OR, 0.06; 95% CI, 0.015-0.223). PSOW estimates were consistent with the primary analyses. Complication rates were low and similar in both groups.
sections.conclusion: In large-diameter GSVs, HSL + CAC was associated with better long-term anatomic and clinical outcomes than CAC alone, without an appreciable increase in complications. These findings suggest that adding HSL to CAC may improve long-term outcomes in selected patients with large-diameter GSVs.

items.title: An mRNA-lipid nanoparticle vaccine against H5N1 influenza virus protects lactating dairy cows from infection.
items.abstract: Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 virus has recently emerged in dairy cattle in the USA, leading to mastitis and sharp reductions in milk production. The main site of H5N1 viral replication is the mammary tissue rather than the respiratory tract and viral transmission between animals is thought to occur through viral shedding in milk. Here, we generate an mRNA-lipid nanoparticle (mRNA-LNP) vaccine encoding the hemagglutinin (HA) of A/dairy cattle/Texas/24-008749-002/2024, representative of circulating bovine H5N1 viruses, and assess its immunogenicity and efficacy in lactating dairy cows. Eight cows were divided into vaccinated and control groups, receiving two intramuscular doses of the vaccine or saline, followed by intramammary viral challenge. Vaccination elicited HA-reactive and neutralizing antibodies in serum and HA-reactive antibodies in milk. Following viral challenge, vaccinated cows had ~1,000-fold lower peak viral RNA in milk and a lower occurrence of mastitis and mammary fibrosis.

items.title: An engineered, compact Cas12m variant for multiplexed gene activation in vivo.
items.abstract: Achieving coordinated CRISPR-based transactivation (CRISPRa) regulation in vivo remains challenging, as the requisite genetic elements frequently exceed the packaging capacity of AAV vectors. Here we report the identification and engineering of the Cas12m protein family, a naturally nuclease-dead CRISPR system that possesses intrinsic self-processing activity for its precursor crRNA. We develop an optimized variant, denCas12m, and leverage it in the smCRISPRa platform. We show that a single transcriptional unit encoding a multi-gRNA array can be processed into individual functional guides within a target cell, enabling efficient synergistic activation of a single gene through multiple sites or simultaneous activation of distinct endogenous genes from a single all-in-one AAV vector. We demonstrate phenotypic rescue in mouse models of Duchenne muscular dystrophy and Scn1a haploinsufficiency. Furthermore, a single all-in-one AAV vector supports the simultaneous activation of multiple distinct endogenous genes in mice, with a single vector delivering up to eight crRNAs for activation of six different genes, demonstrating the platform's high-order multiplexing.

items.title: In Vitro Fertilization or Intrauterine Insemination in Unexplained Infertility.

sections.objective: Although international guidelines recommend intrauterine insemination (IUI) with ovarian stimulation as first-line treatment for unexplained infertility, evidence from comparisons of this method with in vitro fertilization (IVF) is limited.
sections.methods: We conducted a sequential, multicenter, randomized, controlled trial involving couples with unexplained infertility. Stage 1 was a noninferiority comparison between IUI with ovarian stimulation (up to four cycles) and IVF (one complete cycle, with transfer of all embryos). After 7 months, couples without live birth or ongoing pregnancy could proceed to stage 2: couples in the IUI group could undergo up to two IVF cycles, and those in the IVF group could undergo one further IVF cycle. The primary outcome was the cumulative live-birth rate resulting from stage 1. Couples who were in stage 1 during lockdowns due to coronavirus disease 2019 were omitted from the analysis of the primary outcome. A secondary outcome was the cumulative live-birth rate resulting from stages 1 and 2. Live births were included in analyses if day 1 of the treatment cycle that led to pregnancy or day 1 of the last menstrual period before conception occurred within 7 months (stage 1) or 20 months (stage 2) after randomization. The noninferiority margin for the primary outcome was a between-group difference of 10 percentage points.
sections.results: A total of 737 couples underwent randomization: 365 couples were assigned to undergo IUI with ovarian stimulation before IVF, and 372 were assigned to undergo first-line IVF (1 couple in the IVF group withdrew consent for the use of data). The primary-outcome analysis included 585 couples (288 in the IUI group and 297 in the IVF group). The cumulative live-birth rate from stage 1 was 31% (89 births among 288 couples) with IUI with ovarian stimulation and 55% (164 births among 297 couples) with IVF (adjusted risk difference, -24 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -31 to -16). The cumulative live-birth rate from stages 1 and 2 among all the couples who had undergone randomization and provided consent was 70% (257 births among 365 couples) and 71% (265 births among 371 couples), respectively (adjusted risk difference, 0 percentage points; 99% CI, -9 to 8). Overall, serious adverse events occurred in 6 couples in the IUI group and in 14 couples in the IVF group; most serious adverse events were related to oocyte retrieval or hyperstimulation.
sections.conclusion: In couples with unexplained infertility, treatment with four cycles of IUI with ovarian stimulation was not noninferior to treatment with one complete cycle of IVF with respect to the cumulative live-birth rate. (Funded by the Health Research Council of New Zealand and others; FIIX Australian New Zealand Clinical Trials Registry number, ACTRN12619001003167.).

items.title: Comparative effectiveness of three splints for rehabilitation after finger flexor tendon repair (FIRST): randomised controlled trial.

sections.objective: To compare the clinical effectiveness of three splints after repair of zone 1 and 2 flexor tendons: forearm based (long), Manchester short (short), and relative motion flexion (mini) splints.
sections.methods: Prospective, randomised, parallel group, pragmatic, superiority, clinical trial. 430 participants (aged ≥16 years) requiring rehabilitation after primary repair of zone 1 and 2 flexor tendons in one or two fingers of the hand according to British Society for Surgery of the Hand guidelines. Participants were randomly assigned 1:1:1 to the long, short, or mini splint. Splints were worn continuously for five weeks and intermittently for a further week at night and in vulnerable situations such as public environments. Masking participants was not possible owing to the nature of the intervention.
sections.results: 430 participants were randomised to the long splint (n=143), short splint (n=140), or mini splint (n=147) and 403 were included in the intention-to-treat analysis. Adherence, defined as wearing the splint for a minimum of five weeks, was 83% (118/143) for the long splint, 76% (106/140) for the short splint, and 78% (115/147) for the mini splint. Mean post-randomisation PRWHE scores were 24.5 (standard deviation 15.5) in the long splint group, 23.5 (16.7) in the short splint group, and 22.4 (15.0) in the mini splint group, with adjusted between group differences of 0.3 (98.3% confidence interval -4.0 to 4.6, P=0.88) for the long versus short splint, 2.3 (-1.9 to 6.5, P=0.19) for the long versus mini splint, and 2.0 (-2.2 to 6.3, P=0.25) for the short versus mini splint. Serious adverse event rates occurred in 10% (14/143) of participants in the long splint group, 11% (15/140) in the short splint group, and 11% (16/147) in the mini splint group.
sections.conclusion: This trial found no statistically significant difference in clinical effectiveness between the long, short, and mini splint. Apart from some small differences, secondary outcomes were comparable across all three groups.
sections.other: 26 UK hospitals. The primary outcome was the mean post-randomisation score on the patient-rated wrist and hand evaluation (PRWHE) instrument at 6, 12, 26, and 52 weeks, analysed by intention to treat.

items.title: Prospective circulating tumour DNA surveillance in patients with early high-risk hormone receptor positive, HER2-negative breast cancer in the TRAK-ER study.

sections.objective: CtDNA detection during adjuvant endocrine therapy (ET) strongly associates with recurrence in oestrogen receptor (ER) positive early breast cancer (EBC), with potential to direct switches in adjuvant treatment.
sections.methods: TRAK-ER is a multicentre study for patients with high-risk, ER-positive, HER2-negative EBC, who undergo 3 monthly ctDNA surveillance for up to 3 years during adjuvant ET. High-risk included ≥4 involved lymph nodes; tumour >5 cm; 1-3 involved lymph nodes with additional high-risk features. Upon ctDNA detection, patients have staging scans and in the absence of radiological recurrence, are randomised to receive palbociclib plus fulvestrant or standard ET. ctDNA analysis was performed using a tumour informed assay (Labcorp). We report a protocol-specified analysis of ctDNA detection during surveillance, and results of contemporaneous radiological recurrence.
sections.results: 1133 patients were registered by September 2025, 928 had panels designed (design failed in 16.1% (178/1106), and 912 started ctDNA surveillance including results from 5810 tests (median 7 per patient). ctDNA detection rate was 5.0% (45/897) in the first test, and 1.3% (66/4913) in subsequent tests (P<0.001). Patient level detection rate was 12.0% (109/912), with 1.1% (10/912) of patients having a clinical recurrence without prior ctDNA detection. Detection positively associated with nodal burden (P<0.001) and grade (P=0.04) and negatively associated with increasing time from surgery (P=0.01). Estimated cumulative ctDNA detection rate at 5 years post-surgery was 23.7% (95%CI 14.5-31.9%). In patients with ctDNA detected on the first test, 65.9% (29/44) had radiological recurrence compared to 26.6% (17/64) in patients first detected on subsequent tests (P<0.001).
sections.conclusion: Results from TRAK-ER inform implementation of ctDNA surveillance in ER-positive EBC, including molecular relapse rates, factors associating with ctDNA detection and contemporaneous radiological recurrence. Ultrasensitive assays detecting ctDNA at low levels, are required to robustly identify patients prior to clinical recurrence. TRAK-ER is ongoing to assess the impact of treatment after molecular relapse detection.

items.title: Fundus torsion in strabismus: Measurement, clinical interpretation, and emerging imaging approaches.
items.abstract: Fundus torsion is an important but underused anatomical marker in strabismus evaluation, particularly for cyclovertical disorders. Unlike subjective cyclodeviation testing, fundus-based assessment provides an objective reference based on retinal landmarks, though it remains influenced by image acquisition, head position, ocular anatomy, and measurement conventions. We synthesize the anatomical basis of ocular and fundus torsion, contemporary qualitative and quantitative assessment methods, and disease-specific evidence across superior oblique palsy, pattern strabismus, pediatric and adult strabismus, and surgical follow-up. The review emphasizes 3 clinically important issues: the frequent dissociation between objective fundus torsion and subjective cyclodeviation, the need for method-specific interpretation using reproducibility and minimal-detectable-change data, and the importance of avoiding isolated treatment decisions based on anatomical torsion alone. Recent optical coherence tomography-based and artificial intelligence-assisted approaches may improve measurement consistency and scalability, but current evidence supports their use as adjunctive tools rather than autonomous decision systems. Fundus torsion should therefore be interpreted within a multimodal clinical framework that integrates motility findings, sensory status, age, chronicity, fixation behavior, and surgical history. Treatment options include observation and symptom relief in selected patients, inferior oblique weakening for associated overaction, and torsion-directed surgery for persistent symptomatic excyclotorsion; comparative evidence remains limited. Prospective comparative treatment studies are a clinical research priority. Standardized acquisition protocols, explicit reporting conventions, age- and population-specific normative data, externally validated automated methods, and prospective studies linking torsional change to symptoms and functional outcomes are needed to strengthen the clinical utility of fundus torsion assessment.

items.title: Glioma regulates GABAergic signaling to drive hyperactivity and tumor progression.
items.abstract: Recent studies have identified bi-directional communication between neurons and glioma tumors as a key driver of hyperexcitability and malignant progression. Although much of this work has focused on the activity of excitatory neurons, the roles of inhibitory neurons remain poorly defined. Using in vivo screening approaches in autochthonous glioma models, we found that the loss of a γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA) transporter (Slc6a1) enhanced glioma progression, promoted network hyperactivity, and influenced tonic GABA release by tumors. Mechanistically, we show that glioma tumors influence the activity of inhibitory neurons and that their subsequent stimulation suppresses tumor growth. Further screening of these phenomena identified diazepam binding inhibitor (DBI), a secreted negative allosteric modulator of GABA-A, as a link between glioma-related hyperexcitability and proliferation that functions through modulating inhibitory neuronal signaling. Collectively, our findings indicate that glioma tumors utilize multiple mechanisms to manipulate the activity of inhibitory neurons as a means to drive network hyperactivity, which ultimately facilitates malignant progression.

items.title: Trait-linked brainstem circuit resilience balances tau pathology-induced cellular vulnerability in Alzheimer's disease.
items.abstract: Although tau pathology correlates with cognitive decline in Alzheimer's disease (AD), some individuals exhibit resilience by maintaining cognitive function. The mechanisms enabling this protection, particularly before widespread cortical degeneration occurs, remain elusive. Here, we identify a dynamic interplay between cellular vulnerability and circuit-level resilience that shapes cognitive outcomes in AD. Tau accumulation in the Edinger-Westphal nucleus (EW) impairs attention by inducing hypoexcitability in CART+ neurons via Kcnma1 upregulation, a vulnerability predictive of future decline in both 3×Tg-AD mice and AD patients. Conversely, a subset of AD mice with heightened exploratory behavior activates a compensatory medial parabrachial (mPB)-EW circuit, mediated by substance P-Tacr1 signaling, which sustains CART+ neuron function and delays cognitive deterioration. These findings reveal resilience as an active state enabled by trait-linked circuit plasticity that balances cellular vulnerability, defining multilevel targets for early intervention.

items.title: Defining the Substrate in Scar-Related Ventricular Tachycardia: A Hierarchy of Evidence for Arrhythmogenicity.
items.abstract: Scar-related monomorphic ventricular tachycardia is sustained by a limited re-entry circuit within a much larger field of diseased myocardium. Late gadolinium enhancement cardiac magnetic resonance and cardiac computed tomography define scar distribution, channel architecture, wall thickness, and tissue composition, but cannot demonstrate conduction or circuit participation. Voltage mapping and abnormal electrograms identify electrically abnormal myocardium, although their appearance depends on activation sequence, catheter geometry, contact, and annotation. Functional mapping reveals rate-dependent slowing, decrement, and block that may be concealed during baseline rhythm. Mapping during ventricular tachycardia (VT) provides the most direct evidence of circuit participation, but is often limited by hemodynamic instability, noninducibility, or incomplete surface representation of a 3-dimensional circuit. This review examines how to weight these findings when defining the arrhythmogenic substrate. Structural imaging establishes where a circuit could reside and how it may be accessed. Baseline electroanatomic mapping characterizes the electrical expression of surviving myocardium, while functional mapping tests whether conduction deteriorates with changes in wave front or coupling interval. Activation and entrainment provide the strongest evidence that a region participates in a specific VT. These findings should be integrated hierarchically rather than by simple spatial overlap, adjusting interpretation for disease phenotype, substrate depth, mapped surface, and recording conditions. The arrhythmogenic substrate is best understood as surviving myocardium within scar whose 3-dimensional architecture and electrophysiological behavior permit re-entry. A reproducible definition will require standardized acquisition and annotation, explicit reporting of the evidence linking a region to VT, and prospective validation using mapped circuits.

items.title: Global, regional, and national burden of unintentional poisoning, 1990-2023: results from the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.

sections.objective: Unintentional poisoning is a preventable cause of injury-related morbidity and mortality, yet global patterns, trends, and inequalities remain incompletely characterised. Within the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) framework, unintentional poisoning includes poisoning by carbon monoxide and poisoning by other means, a category largely informed by pesticide poisoning codes plus some indirect capture of other poisoning as part of the GBD re-distribution process. Poisonings by pharmaceuticals and illicit substances are not captured in the GBD definition of poisoning. We aimed to quantify this GBD-defined burden and assess regional variation, sociodemographic gradients, and case fatality between 1990 and 2023.
sections.methods: We analysed GBD 2023 estimates for 204 countries and territories, modelling deaths, incidence, and disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs) using standard GBD cause-of-death and non-fatal estimation methods with 95% uncertainty intervals. We stratified results by age, sex, region, and Socio-demographic Index (SDI), and derived case fatality from modelled deaths and incidence.
sections.results: In 2023, unintentional poisoning from carbon monoxide and other means caused 2·54 million incident poisonings, 69 805 deaths, and 3·68 million DALYs globally, with age-standardised DALY rates declining by 47·5% since 1990. Carbon monoxide accounted for 641 932 poisonings, 30 890 deaths and 1·34 million DALYs, with the highest burdens in central and eastern Europe and central Asia. Most regions showed substantial long-term declines, and the global age-standardised DALY rate for carbon monoxide poisoning declined by 58·2% since 1990.
