sections.methods: In this phase 3, multicenter, open-label, randomized trial conducted in China, we randomly assigned patients with HER2-positive advanced breast cancer in a 1:1 ratio to receive either anbenitamab plus HB1801 or THP. The primary end point was progression-free survival, as assessed by blinded independent central review. Objective response was a secondary end point.
sections.results: A total of 885 patients were enrolled (445 were assigned to receive anbenitamab plus HB1801 and 440 to receive THP). At this prespecified interim analysis (with 401 events [disease progression or death] and a median follow-up of 21.0 months), the estimated 24-month progression-free survival was significantly higher with anbenitamab plus HB1801 than with THP (58.5% vs. 34.4%; hazard ratio for progression or death, 0.46; 95% confidence interval, 0.37 to 0.56; P<0.001). The percentage of patients with an objective response was 87.6% in the anbenitamab group and 73.4% in the THP group. Adverse events of grade 3 or higher occurred in 204 of 444 patients (45.9%) in the anbenitamab group and in 151 of 439 patients (34.4%) in the THP group. Neutropenia was the most common adverse event of grade 3 or higher in both groups (13.1% in the anbenitamab group and 8.4% in the THP group). Adverse events leading to death occurred in 2 patients in each group.
sections.conclusion: Anbenitamab plus HB1801 led to significantly higher progression-free survival than THP among patients with HER2-positive advanced breast cancer. (Funded by Shanghai JMT-Bio Technology and others; HEALER ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05838066.).

items.title: 14-day versus 28-day trifluridine-tipiracil plus bevacizumab for refractory metastatic colorectal cancer (PRABITAS): a pragmatic, multicentre, open-label, randomised, phase 3, non-inferiority trial in Japan.

sections.objective: Trifluridine-tipiracil (FTD-TPI) plus bevacizumab is the standard treatment for refractory metastatic colorectal cancer. However, the conventional schedule is frequently associated with haematological and gastrointestinal toxicity, which is clinically significant and relevant to patients. A simplified 14-day schedule has been proposed to reduce toxicity, but whether this treatment preserves survival has not been established in a randomised trial. We therefore aimed to assess whether the 14-day schedule is non-inferior to the conventional schedule for overall survival.
sections.methods: PRABITAS was a pragmatic, multicentre, open-label, randomised, phase 3, non-inferiority trial conducted in 178 hospitals in Japan. Patients with refractory metastatic colorectal cancer were randomly assigned (1:1) using a minimisation algorithm, stratified by Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status, RAS mutational status, and institution, to FTD-TPI (35 mg/m2 orally twice daily) plus bevacizumab (5 mg/kg intravenously) on either a conventional 28-day (FTD-TPI on days 1-5 and 8-12; bevacizumab on days 1 and 15) or 14-day schedule (FTD-TPI on days 1-5; bevacizumab on day 1). Eligibility criteria were broadened compared with those of conventional explanatory trials, and trial procedures were aligned with routine clinical practice. The primary endpoint was overall survival, analysed in the intention-to-treat population, with a prespecified non-inferiority margin of 1·25. Safety was assessed in all patients who received at least one dose. Missing data were not imputed. This trial is registered with the Japan Registry of Clinical Trials, jRCTs041230120, and is closed to enrolment.
sections.results: Between Dec 26, 2023, and May 20, 2025, we randomly assigned 972 patients, of whom 970 (99%) constituted the intention-to-treat population after two were excluded because they were randomly assigned before site approval (486 [50%] to the 28-day treatment group, 292 [60%] men and 194 [40%] women]; and 484 [50%] to the 14-day treatment group, 264 [55%] men and 220 [45%] women). Median follow-up was 17·9 months (IQR 14·3-22·6). Median overall survival was 10·3 months (95% CI 9·5-11·6) in the 28-day group and 11·3 months (10·2-12·5) in the 14-day group (stratified hazard ratio 0·93 [95% CI 0·80-1·08]). The 12-month overall survival rates were 44·0% (95% CI 39·5-48·5) in the 28-day group and 47·5% (42·9-52·0) in the 14-day group. Neutropenia grade 3 or worse was reduced in the 14-day group (13% vs 39%; absolute difference 25 percentage points [95% CI 20-31]), as was anorexia grade 2 or worse (15% vs 26%; absolute difference 11 percentage points [6-16]). Two treatment-related deaths occurred in the 14-day group and none in the 28-day group.
sections.conclusion: A 14-day schedule of FTD-TPI plus bevacizumab was non-inferior to the conventional 28-day schedule for overall survival, while reducing haematological and gastrointestinal toxicity. These findings support this simplified schedule as the new standard for FTD-TPI plus bevacizumab in refractory metastatic colorectal cancer.

items.title: Efficacy and safety of mitapivat in patients with sickle cell disease (RISE UP): a phase 3, double-blind, global, randomised, placebo-controlled trial.

sections.objective: Persistent haemolytic anaemia and recurrent vaso-occlusion drive complications and accelerate mortality in sickle cell disease. Mitapivat, an oral allosteric activator of pyruvate kinase, increases ATP and decreases 2,3-DPG with the potential to improve haemolytic anaemia and reduce sickling. We aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of mitapivat in patients with sickle cell disease.
sections.methods: We report results from RISE UP, a phase 3, double-blind, global, randomised, placebo-controlled trial from 69 sites across 15 countries. Patients older than 16 years with anaemia and recurrent sickle cell pain crises were randomly assigned (2:1) to either mitapivat 100 mg or placebo twice a day using permuted-block randomisation. Primary endpoints, assessed in all randomly assigned patients, were haemoglobin response (≥1·0 g/dL increase in average haemoglobin concentration from week 24 to week 52 compared with baseline) and annualised rate of sickle cell pain crises. This study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05031780, and the open-label extension is ongoing.
sections.results: A total of 207 patients were randomly assigned to mitapivat (138 [67%]) or placebo (69 [33%]). 56 (41%) of 138 patients in the mitapivat group had a haemoglobin response, compared with two (3%) of 69 patients on placebo (adjusted difference 38%, 95% CI 29-47; two-sided p<0·0001). The annualised rate (95% CI) of sickle cell pain crises was 2·6 (2·3-3·0) for mitapivat and 3·1 (2·6-3·6) for placebo (two-sided p=0·1213). Serious adverse events were reported in 28 (20%) patients on mitapivat and 20 (29%) patients on placebo; one (1%) patient and 0 patients, respectively, were deemed treatment related.
sections.conclusion: Mitapivat, an oral pyruvate kinase activator, with a novel mechanism that ameliorates haemolytic anaemia, has the potential to be an effective and convenient disease-modifying treatment for people with sickle cell disease.

items.title: Conversational diagnostic artificial intelligence in ambulatory primary care: a prospective feasibility study.

sections.objective: Artificial intelligence (AI)-based systems show promise for assisting primary care providers (PCPs) with patient care. We aimed to evaluate the safety and quality of clinical conversations of a patient-facing conversational AI system, which engaged in real-world urgent primary care appointments.
sections.methods: In this prospective, single-centre, single-arm feasibility study, English-speaking patients aged at least 18 years interacted with the Articulate Medical Intelligence Explorer (AMIE) up to 5 days before a single-complaint urgent primary care appointment. Physician safety supervisors monitored all interactions and were trained to intervene on the basis of predefined safety criteria. AMIE transcripts and summaries were shared with PCPs before the visit. Primary outcomes were the number of supervised conversation safety stops, AMIE's conversation quality assessed by clinical evaluators, and patient and PCP experiences per surveys. This study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06911398).
sections.results: From April to November, 2025, 114 patients were enrolled with 98 completing both the AMIE interaction and the PCP appointment. Zero conversation safety stops were required on the basis of prespecified criteria. Safety supervisors noted one hallucination and added clinical information in five interactions. AMIE's conversations were rated favourably in 87-100% of cases (17 criteria) by clinical evaluators, and 48-96% (16 criteria) by patients. Patient attitudes towards AI improved after interacting with AMIE and remained elevated after the patient's visit with their physician. PCPs completed post-surveys in 60 of 98 cases, including 44 cases in which they reviewed the AMIE transcript before the visit. PCPs found AMIE helpful for visit preparation in 33 of 44 cases and reported that it might have changed their behaviour in 25 of 44 cases.
sections.conclusion: Although further research is needed, this study shows the initial feasibility of conversational AI in a real-world setting-assessed via conversation safety and quality, as well as user acceptance-and represents a crucial step towards clinical translation.

items.title: Oral deucrictibant for on-demand treatment of hereditary angioedema attacks: a phase 3, multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial.

sections.objective: In hereditary angioedema, a rare bradykinin-mediated condition, oral on-demand treatments facilitating prompt administration and providing rapid, sustained relief and attack resolution remain scant. We investigated the efficacy and safety of deucrictibant, an oral bradykinin B2 receptor antagonist, for on-demand treatment of hereditary angioedema attacks.
sections.methods: RAPIDe-3 was a phase 3, double-blind, 2 × 2 crossover trial in adolescent and adult participants (aged ≥12 to <18 years and aged ≥18 to ≤75 years, respectively) with hereditary angioedema, at 59 sites across 24 countries on six continents. Eligible participants had hereditary angioedema, including those with normal C1 inhibitor associated with a documented genetic variant, at least two attacks within the last 3 months before screening, and experience with effectively using conventional on-demand therapies for hereditary angioedema attacks. Participants were randomly allocated in a 1:1 ratio to one of two double-blind crossover sequences to treat two attacks with a 20 mg oral deucrictibant immediate-release capsule or placebo as either deucrictibant-placebo or placebo-deucrictibant, stratified by age and use of long-term prophylaxis. The primary endpoint was time to onset of symptom relief, defined as Patient Global Impression of Change rating of at least a little better. Safety was assessed in all participants who received any dose of study drug. RAPIDe-3 is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06343779) and is complete.
sections.results: Between April 4, 2024, and Sept 1, 2025, 149 people were assessed for eligibility, and 134 eligible participants (ten [7%] adolescents and 124 [93%] adults) were randomly allocated. 58 (43%) were male and 76 (57%) were female, and the median age was 38·0 years (IQR 27·0-50·0). 113 participants treated 201 attacks. The primary efficacy analysis included 88 participants with paired treated attacks. Of these, 47 (53%) participants were female and 41 (47%) were male, and 60 (68%), 16 (18%), 4 (5%), and 1 (1%) were White, Asian, Black, and American Indian or Alaska Native, respectively. Onset of symptom relief occurred significantly faster with deucrictibant than placebo, with median times of 1·28 h (95% CI 1·05 to 1·52) and more than 12 h (5·82 to >12), respectively (p<0·0001). Fatigue was the only adverse event reported more than once within 3 days post-treatment: a single event was reported by two participants, one of which was deemed unrelated to treatment. Across the study, no treatment-related adverse events were assessed as severe or serious, and no adverse events led to treatment discontinuation.
sections.conclusion: Oral deucrictibant provided faster times to symptom relief than placebo and was generally well tolerated. These results support the use of deucrictibant as potentially the first orally administered bradykinin B2 receptor antagonist for the treatment of attacks of bradykinin-mediated angioedema, including hereditary angioedema, and may address an unmet need for options that are effective and well tolerated, with convenient administration.

items.title: The public health challenges of children's and adolescents' digital media use: applying the digital determinants of health as an interpretive framework.
items.abstract: Children and adolescents are growing up in a hybrid world in which digital media has become part of the infrastructure of everyday life and a structural determinant of their health. In the second paper of this Series on the digital determinants of health, we apply the framework introduced in the first paper to one of the most contested questions in public health: how young people's digital media use shapes their health and wellbeing. Using the digital determinants of health framework to interpret the current evidence base, we examine what is known, and what remains poorly understood, about the public health implications of children's and adolescents' digital media use. Evidence suggests that digital media use can be associated with both benefits and harms although it is more consistently associated with adverse mental, behavioural, physical, cognitive, and social outcomes, with developmental stage emerging as an important moderator. Illustrative modelling indicates the potential population burden is substantial, even as its causal basis remains uncertain. Research to date has privileged easily measured proxies, such as screen time, and given insufficient attention to the platform design, algorithmic systems, and commercial incentives that shape young people's experiences. Situating young people's digital media use with a digital determinants of health framework, we conclude that protecting children's and adolescents' health calls for a precautionary, structural response-one that moves beyond individual behaviour change to reshape the digital systems, incentives, and knowledge practices that determine how digital media affects health.

items.title: Governing the digital determinants of health for children and young people: a global public health imperative.
items.abstract: The digital determinants of health are the structural conditions through which digital infrastructures, business models, and design choices shape health outcomes. Yet these determinants remain largely outside public health policy and remain fragmented across regulatory sectors. Rather than regulating individual technologies in isolation, governance should ensure that digital systems and environments advance population health and reduce inequities. A public health approach shifts attention from individual responsibility-and the tendency to blame users-towards the governance of the structural features that produce health risks and inequities. We identify four governance domains for the digital determinants of health: infrastructure and access, platform design and commercial practices, data governance and surveillance, and institutional accountability and rights. Effectively governing these domains requires intersectoral strategies that tackle problematic concentrations of political and economic power. We argue that the governance of the digital determinants of health should be recognised as a core public health function, with the health of children and young people as a priority and entry point and precaution as a guiding governance principle.

items.title: The digital determinants of health: a new era for global public health.
items.abstract: Digital transformations exert increasing influence over the lives of the global population, shaping opportunities and generating harms for health and wellbeing across the spectrum of digital access and engagement. The scale of influence of digital transformations on human and planetary health marks the urgency of attention to the digital determinants of health (DDoH). In this Series paper, we describe a prevailing digital sociotechnological order (DSTO) as the structural source of the DDoH. The DSTO is composed of a set of dominant assumptions that motivate digital practices operating through four features (political norms, economic logics, infrastructures, and personal and social practices) to affect human and planetary health. We describe the implications of the DSTO for understanding, studying, and governing the DDoH, and present recommendations for future work.

items.title: Treatment Effect of Perioperative (Neoadjuvant and Adjuvant) Apalutamide plus Androgen-deprivation Therapy Versus Radical Prostatectomy Alone in Patients with High-risk Localized or Locally Advanced Prostate Cancer from the PROTEUS Substudy.

sections.objective: The blinded placebo-controlled PROTEUS (Perioperative Treatment with Erleada United with Surgery) study demonstrated that adding 1-yr perioperative apalutamide plus androgen-deprivation therapy (ADT) benefited patients with high-risk localized prostate cancer or locally advanced prostate cancer (HR-LPC/LAPC) who were undergoing radical prostatectomy with pelvic lymph node dissection (RP). This substudy evaluated 1-yr perioperative apalutamide plus ADT versus standard-of-care (SOC) RP.
sections.methods: Patients with newly diagnosed HR-LPC/LAPC were randomized 1:3 to open-label perioperative apalutamide (240 mg/d) plus ADT (six 28-d cycles before and after RP) or RP.
sections.results: The primary end point was event-free survival (EFS), defined as time to biochemical failure, local/regional recurrence, distant metastasis, or death. Secondary/other end points included metastasis-free survival (MFS) by conventional or prostate-specific membrane antigen positron emission tomography (PSMA PET) imaging, MFS by conventional imaging, and time to first subsequent therapy; p values were nominal. Time-to-event end points were analyzed with the Kaplan-Meier method and stratified Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for the randomization stratification factors to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). In total, 408 patients (median age 66 yr [interquartile range 62-71]) were randomized: perioperative apalutamide plus ADT, n = 102; RP, n = 306. Median follow-up was 37.4 mo in patients without EFS events. Perioperative apalutamide plus ADT significantly improved EFS compared with RP alone (median not reached vs 19.1 mo; estimated 3-yr event-free rates 63% vs 41%; HR 0.38; 95% CI 0.26-0.55; p < 0.001). Because of the nonconstant HR over time, indicating that the proportional hazards assumption was not met, a post hoc restricted mean survival time analysis was performed. This analysis estimated that the average event-free time during the first 36 mo was 31.7 mo (95% CI 30.3-33.1) with perioperative apalutamide plus ADT versus 20.7 mo (95% CI 19.1-22.4) with RP alone, a difference of 11.0 mo (95% CI 8.8-13.1; p < 0.001). MFS by conventional or PSMA PET imaging favored perioperative apalutamide plus ADT over RP alone (estimated 3-yr event-free rates 87% vs 78%; HR 0.49; 95% CI 0.26-0.90; p = 0.019), and the hazard of subsequent therapy was reduced by 71% (HR 0.29; 95% CI 0.20-0.43; p < 0.001). MFS by conventional imaging showed no difference between study groups (estimated 3-yr event-free rates 94% vs 92%; HR 0.74; 95% CI 0.30-1.82; p = 0.5). Grade 3-4 treatment-emergent adverse events occurred in 31 patients (31%) receiving perioperative apalutamide plus ADT versus 62 patients (22%) receiving RP.
sections.conclusion: Perioperative apalutamide plus ADT improved EFS and delayed subsequent therapy compared with SOC. Together with the blinded PROTEUS main study, these results support perioperative apalutamide plus ADT as a new therapeutic option for selected patients with HR-LPC/LAPC who are fit for surgery and 1-yr systemic therapy.

items.title: Defining the clinical benefits of disease-modifying therapy in people living with spinal muscular atrophy who require permanent ventilation: a UK-based modified Delphi consensus process.

sections.objective: Spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) is a rare inherited neuromuscular disorder that may require permanent ventilation (PV) in severe cases. Although disease-modifying therapies (DMTs) have transformed outcomes for many, prior to this research, access in the UK was restricted for patients receiving PV (SMA-PV). This study aimed to develop consensus recommendations on DMT use and to define clinical benefit in SMA-PV.
sections.methods: A multidisciplinary UK-based expert panel conducted a modified Delphi consensus process between 08 April and 09 June 2025. Draft statements informed by published evidence and expert insights were anonymously voted on for up to three rounds, with consensus defined as ≥75% agreement. Statements not achieving consensus were revised and re-evaluated. Input from a non-voting patient advisory panel (PAP) was also considered. The study was not prospectively registered.
sections.results: Excluding the Chair, 18 participants evaluated 22 statements across seven thematic areas specific to SMA-PV: DMT access; treatment initiation; treatment monitoring; defining clinical benefit; functional outcomes; quality of life (QoL); and future research priorities. All 22 statements achieved consensus after two voting rounds (100% participation; agreement range 89-100%). Two statements were revised and re-voted in round 2: one after narrowly missing consensus (72% agreement) and the other to incorporate PAP feedback despite achieving 100% agreement in round 1. The panel agreed that PV alone should not preclude access to DMTs and that trial access with personalised treatment goals may be appropriate. The panel also emphasised broader definitions of clinical benefit, including subtle changes in function and QoL, alongside sensitive assessment approaches and harmonised outcome measurement.
sections.conclusion: These consensus-based recommendations support careful reconsideration of treatment exclusions for patients with SMA-PV and more inclusive, patient-centred approaches to evaluating treatment benefit.

items.title: Interim Analysis of a Phase 3 Trial of Povetacicept in IgA Nephropathy.

sections.objective: B-cell activating factor (BAFF) and a proliferation-inducing ligand (APRIL) have distinct roles in IgA-producing B-cell populations and appear to be central to the pathogenesis of IgA nephropathy. Povetacicept, an enhanced, variant transmembrane activator and calcium-modulator and cyclophilin-ligand interactor (TACI)-Fc fragment fusion therapeutic, is engineered for dual inhibition of BAFF and APRIL.
sections.methods: In this ongoing, phase 3, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, participants with biopsy-proven IgA nephropathy receiving stable background therapy were randomly assigned in a 2:1 ratio to receive povetacicept at a dose of 80 mg or placebo subcutaneously every 4 weeks. The primary end point of this prespecified interim analysis was the change in the 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio at week 36. Secondary end points were the change at week 36 in galactose-deficient IgA1 levels and hematuria resolution at week 36 among participants with baseline hematuria.
sections.results: A total of 557 participants received povetacicept (372 participants) or placebo (185 participants). Efficacy analyses included the first 199 participants who had undergone randomization (131 in the povetacicept group and 68 in the placebo group). The 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio decreased by 52.0% with povetacicept and by 4.3% with placebo by week 36 (adjusted difference, -49.8 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -58.6 to -39.2; P<0.001). Galactose-deficient IgA1 levels decreased by 77.4% with povetacicept and increased by 9.1% with placebo (adjusted difference, -79.3 percentage points; 95% CI, -82.2 to -75.9; P<0.001). Among the participants with baseline hematuria, resolution occurred in 85% with povetacicept and in 23% with placebo (adjusted difference, 62 percentage points; 95% CI, 45 to 78; P<0.001). The incidence of adverse events (75% with povetacicept and 78% with placebo) and serious adverse events (3% and 4%, respectively) were similar in the trial groups.
sections.conclusion: Povetacicept led to a significantly greater reduction in the 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio than placebo by week 36 in participants with IgA nephropathy. (Funded by Vertex Pharmaceuticals; RAINIER AIS-D08 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06564142.).

items.title: Trial of Endovascular Therapy for Mild Stroke with Large-Vessel Occlusion.

sections.objective: Whether endovascular therapy benefits patients with mild acute ischemic stroke from large-vessel occlusion involving the anterior circulation is uncertain.
sections.methods: We conducted a multicenter, open-label, randomized trial in China involving patients with acute ischemic stroke of mild clinical severity (defined by a score of <6 on the National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale) that had resulted from large-vessel occlusion involving the anterior circulation. Patients also had neuroimaging features of a small infarct core and a large perfusion-mismatch volume, representing substantial at-risk tissue, within 24 hours after symptom onset or after they were last known to be well. The patients were randomly assigned to undergo endovascular therapy and receive medical management or to receive medical management alone. The primary outcome was an excellent functional outcome (defined by a modified Rankin scale score of 0 [no symptoms] or 1 [no clinically significant disability]) at 90 days.
sections.results: A total of 304 patients underwent randomization, of whom 300 were included in the modified intention-to-treat population: 144 in the endovascular-therapy group and 156 in the medical-management group. At 90 days, a modified Rankin scale score of 0 or 1 was reported in 69.4% of the patients in the endovascular-therapy group and in 50.0% of those in the medical-management group (odds ratio, 2.32; 95% confidence interval, 1.41 to 3.81; P<0.001). Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage within 48 hours occurred in 3 patients in each group. Serious procedure-related complications occurred in 19 patients (13.2%) in the endovascular-therapy group. Among all the participants, one death occurred (in the endovascular-therapy group).
sections.conclusion: In this trial from China involving patients with mild acute ischemic stroke caused by large-vessel occlusion and substantial at-risk tissue on perfusion imaging, endovascular therapy performed within 24 hours after symptom onset plus medical management resulted in better 90-day functional outcomes than medical management alone, without an increase in the risk of symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage but with a high incidence of serious procedural complications. (Funded by Fujian Medical University Union Hospital and others; MILD-MT ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06179017.).

items.title: Mechanical Thrombectomy 24 to 72 Hours after Large-Vessel Ischemic Stroke.

sections.objective: Endovascular thrombectomy is an established treatment for acute ischemic stroke. Whether the benefit extends to patients with salvageable brain tissue in the infarct who present more than 24 hours after symptom onset or the time when they were last known to be well is uncertain.
sections.methods: We conducted an open-label, randomized trial with blinded outcome assessment at comprehensive stroke centers in China. Patients with acute ischemic stroke from large-vessel occlusion of the anterior circulation and imaging-identified salvageable brain tissue at 24 to 72 hours were assigned to receive endovascular therapy plus standard medical care (intervention group) or standard medical care alone (control group). The primary outcome was functional status, defined by the score on the modified Rankin scale (range, 0 to 6, with higher scores indicating greater disability and a score of 6 indicating death) at 90 days, with results assessed as the distribution of scores in each group. Secondary outcomes included disability, neurologic impairment, and safety.
sections.results: A total of 336 patients were included in the intention-to-treat population, with 168 assigned to each group. The median time from symptom onset or from the point when the patient was last known to be well to randomization was 38.5 hours. Endovascular therapy resulted in a more favorable distribution of modified Rankin scale scores at 90 days than standard medical care alone (common odds ratio for a better functional outcome, 1.74; 95% confidence interval, 1.19 to 2.55). Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage occurred in 4.8% of the patients in the intervention group and in no patients in the control group, and the 90-day case fatality rate was 6.0% and 1.8%, respectively.
sections.conclusion: Among patients who presented 24 to 72 hours after an acute ischemic stroke from large-vessel occlusion of the anterior circulation and had imaging-identified salvageable tissue, endovascular therapy resulted in better functional outcomes than standard care but led to a higher risk of intracranial hemorrhage and death. (Funded by the National Health Commission Capacity Building and Continuing Education Center and others; LATE-MT ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05326932.).

items.title: Remibrutinib versus teriflunomide in relapsing multiple sclerosis (REMODEL-1 and REMODEL-2): two randomised, phase 3 trials.

sections.objective: Remibrutinib is a highly selective, potent, covalent, CNS-penetrant, oral BTK inhibitor. We assessed the efficacy and safety of remibrutinib in adult patients with relapsing multiple sclerosis.
sections.methods: REMODEL-1 and REMODEL-2 are two identical, randomised, double-blind, double-dummy, active comparator-controlled, parallel-group, event-driven, phase 3 trials conducted at 407 centres in 46 countries. Patients aged 18-55 years with relapsing multiple sclerosis, an Expanded Disability Status Scale score of 0-5·5, and evidence of recent disease activity were randomly assigned 1:1 to oral remibrutinib 100 mg twice daily or teriflunomide 14 mg once daily via interactive response technology. Randomisation was stratified by geographical region, MRI cohort participation, and multiple sclerosis subtype. Patients, site investigators, and trial team were masked to treatment allocation. The primary endpoint was annualised relapse rate (ARR), defined as the number of confirmed multiple sclerosis relapses per patient-year with up to 30 months of follow-up, and assessed in all randomly assigned patients. These trials are registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05147220 and NCT05156281) and are ongoing, not recruiting.
sections.results: Between Dec 13, 2021, and Dec 30, 2025, 2632 patients were screened and 2007 patients were randomly assigned. REMODEL-1 included 1000 patients (remibrutinib 502, teriflunomide 498; mean age 38·2 years, 666 [66·6%] female, 334 [33·4%] male) and REMODEL-2 included 1007 patients (remibrutinib 504, teriflunomide 503; mean age 39·0 years, 675 [67·0%] female, 332 [33·0%] male). ARR was significantly lower with remibrutinib than with teriflunomide: 0·073 versus 0·112 (rate ratio [RR] 0·648 [95% CI 0·453-0·927]; p=0·018) in REMODEL-1 and 0·080 versus 0·116 (RR 0·688 [0·487-0·972]; p=0·034) in REMODEL-2. The most common adverse events were upper respiratory tract infection (132 [13·1%] of 1006 with remibrutinib vs 137 [13·7%] of 1001 with teriflunomide), nasopharyngitis (92 [9·1%] vs 123 [12·3%]), diarrhoea (84 [8·3%] vs 109 [10·9%]), and alopecia (58 [5·8%] vs 135 [13·5%]). Adverse events leading to treatment discontinuation were less frequent with remibrutinib (31 [3·1%]) versus teriflunomide (58 [5·8%]). The safety profile of remibrutinib was consistent with that in other indications, including no liver safety concerns.
sections.conclusion: Remibrutinib was superior to teriflunomide in patients with relapsing multiple sclerosis, while maintaining a favourable safety profile. These findings support remibrutinib as a potential new oral treatment option for relapsing multiple sclerosis.

items.title: Ravulizumab in IgA Nephropathy - Interim Analysis of a Phase 3 Trial.

sections.objective: In patients with IgA nephropathy, complement activation drives glomerular inflammation, which leads to hematuria, proteinuria, and nephron loss. Ravulizumab is a terminal complement inhibitor that prevents formation of C5a and C5b-9.
sections.methods: In this phase 3 trial, we enrolled adults with IgA nephropathy who had an estimated glomerular filtration rate of at least 30 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 of body-surface area and proteinuria (24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio [with protein and creatinine both measured in grams] of ≥0.75 or total urinary protein excretion of ≥1.0 g per day), despite standard therapy. Patients were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive an intravenous infusion of either ravulizumab or placebo every 8 weeks. In the prespecified interim analysis, the primary efficacy end point was the change from baseline in the 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio at week 34. Safety was also assessed.
sections.results: In all, 485 patients underwent randomization, with 240 patients assigned to the ravulizumab group and 245 to the placebo group; 352 patients (176 in each group) were included in the interim analysis. In the ravulizumab group, the geometric mean 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio at baseline and at week 34 was 1.56 and 0.83, respectively; in the placebo group, it was 1.60 and 1.48, respectively. At week 34, a significant reduction in the geometric mean 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio was observed with ravulizumab (-46.6%) as compared with the reduction observed with placebo (-5.6%), corresponding to an adjusted geometric mean 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio that was 43.4% (99% confidence interval, 30.1 to 54.2) lower with ravulizumab than with placebo (P<0.001). Adverse events occurred in 69.5% of the patients receiving ravulizumab and in 75.8% of those receiving placebo; serious adverse events occurred in 4.6% and 9.0%, respectively. No meningococcal infections or deaths occurred.
sections.conclusion: In adults with IgA nephropathy, ravulizumab resulted in a significantly greater reduction in the protein-to-creatinine ratio than placebo at week 34. (Funded by Alexion, AstraZeneca Rare Disease Unit; I CAN ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06291376; EU Clinical Trials number, 2023-507851-31-00.).

items.title: Current Applications of Robotic Surgery in Aortic Procedures: A Scoping Review.
items.abstract: ObjectiveTo map the applications and outcomes of robotic technologies in aortic and aortoiliac procedures, including robot-assisted laparoscopic surgery, endovascular procedures, and micro-robotics.MethodsPubMed was searched up to October 4, 2026, for primary studies including at least 3 patients treated with robotic or robot-assisted interventions for aortic or aortoiliac disease, following PRISMA-ScR guidelines. Case reports and two-patient series were summarized separately.ResultsFifteen observational studies (552 patients) were included. Robot-assisted laparoscopic surgery (9 studies; 494 patients) was mainly applied to aortoiliac occlusive disease (385 procedures), with robotic proximal aortic anastomosis and open distal anastomoses, and less frequently to aneurysm repair. Conversion rates ranged from 0% to 20%, graft patency from 89% to 100% at up to 48 months, and hospital stay from 4 to 8 days. Robot-assisted endovascular procedures (5 studies; 49 patients) were mostly applied to single procedural steps. Robotic target vessel cannulation succeeded in 81% of vessels, and robotic gate cannulation achieved a shorter catheter path length than manual cannulation (35.7 vs 74.1 cm; P = 0.019), but longer cannulation time. Robotic arch navigation was associated with fewer cerebral high-intensity transient signals (median 0 vs 2; P = 0.018), and operator radiation dose at the shielded console was 96.5% lower than at the procedure table. No robot-related complications were reported. Micro-robotic sac puncture for type II endoleak embolization (1 study; 9 patients) succeeded in all cases.ConclusionRobotic technologies are a promising and feasible option for selected patients undergoing aortic procedures at experienced centers. Robot-assisted laparoscopic surgery showed acceptable conversion rates and favorable mid-term patency, while endovascular robotics improved technical and surrogate endpoints. As current evidence is limited to small observational series, prospective comparative studies are needed to define the clinical benefit of robotics compared with open and endovascular repair.

items.title: Epidemiology, Risk Factors, and Prevention of Prostate Cancer.

sections.objective: To assess geographical differences and temporal trends in PCa incidence and mortality and PCa risk factors.
sections.conclusion: The global burden of PCa because of population increase and aging is projected to rise substantially by 2050, particularly in low- and middle-income regions. Family history, germ line pathogenic variants, and ancestry are risk factors for PCa. Evidence remains insufficient to support any specific preventive intervention, although smoking, diet, and physical activity may modify risk of progression or mortality.
sections.other: There are substantial regional differences in prostate cancer (PCa) epidemiology reflecting differences in risk factors, screening, management, and access to care. Estimated incidence and mortality data for the year 2024 and projections to 2050 based on the assumption that 2024 age-specific incidence and mortality rates remain unchanged (not accounting for changes in risk factors and/or treatments) in 185 countries were derived from the International Agency for Research on Cancer's GLOBOCAN 2024 database. A narrative review of the literature summarized risk factors and preventive measures. Worldwide, 1.55 million new PCa cases were estimated in 2024, with an age-standardized rate (ASR) for incidence of 29 per 100 000. Northern America had the highest all-age incidence ASR (81), and South-Central Asia the lowest (7.2). PCa caused an estimated 420 000 deaths (7.5 per 100 000), with the highest mortality ASRs in the Caribbean (29) and the lowest in South-Central Asia (3.4). By 2050, new cases are projected to be 2.88 million (+86%) and deaths 924 000 (+120%), with the largest relative increases in Africa (+156%). Prostate-specific antigen-based screening influences both incidence and geographic variation. Family history, germ line pathogenic variants, polygenic risk scores, and ancestry are risk factors. Disparities in men of African versus European ancestry reflect both tumor biology and unequal access to care, with mortality gaps narrowing in equal-access health systems. No single nutrient or supplement has been shown to reduce PCa incidence. Cigarette smoking and obesity are associated with PCa-specific mortality, whereas physical activity and plant-based or Mediterranean dietary patterns are associated with a lower risk of disease progression.

items.title: Characterization of IgA, IgA immune complexes and complement depositions in IgA nephropathy using laser microdissection and mass spectrometry.

sections.objective: IgA nephropathy is characterized by accumulation of mesangial IgA immune complexes. These IgA immune complexes result in glomerular inflammation and subsequent sclerosis. Glomerular inflammation is mediated in part by activation of the complement pathway by these immune complexes.
sections.methods: In this study of 22 cases of IgA nephropathy, using laser microdissection and mass spectrometry (LMD/MS), we characterized both IgA and complement deposits.
sections.results: LMD/MS detected abundant IgA1 but also IgA2; detected in 100% and 82% of cases, respectively. Furthermore, J chains, that link IgA monomers to form dimeric IgA on mucosal surfaces, was detected in 91% of cases, while the polymeric Ig receptor found in secretory IgA was found in only 9% of the cases. IgG1 was the dominant IgG subclass and was detected in 100% of cases. IgG subclass staining and confocal immunofluorescence microscopy confirmed the IgG1 subclass and colocalization of IgG1 with IgA1 and IgA2.Evaluation of the complement pathways revealed abundant C3, C9, C5, C6, C7 and C8 with lesser amounts of C4 indicating activation of predominantly the alternative and terminal pathways of complement. LMD/MS also detected abundant complement regulating proteins including CFH, CFHR1, CFHR2 and CFHR5, CD59, and smaller amounts of CFB, indicating active regulation of the complement pathways. Although it did not reach statistical significance, high counts of C3, C5 and C9 were present in lesions with endocapillary hypercellularity/crescentic lesions. High counts of complement regulating proteins, particularly CFHR5, were also present in active lesions. C3 sequence coverage data showed the majority of amino acids detected belong to C3dg along with smaller amounts of C3c.
sections.conclusion: Our data shows that the IgA immune complexes are composed of mucosal-derived dimeric IgA1/IgA2 and IgG1. The majority of complement proteins detected are components of the alternative and terminal complement pathway.

items.title: The clinical relevance of multiple sclerosis genetics: from susceptibility to disease severity and progression.
items.abstract: Large-scale genome-wide association studies have identified hundreds of multiple sclerosis risk loci, most of which implicate immune pathways and establish multiple sclerosis as a highly polygenic, immune-mediated disease. These findings help explain why immune-modifying therapies suppress relapses and new lesion formation. However, susceptibility genetics does not adequately explain disability accumulation, variation in disease course, or treatment response. Evidence from rare-variant studies, genetic studies of disease severity and disability progression, epigenetic analyses, gene-environment studies, and Epstein-Barr virus research is beginning to extend this genetic framework from susceptibility to disease expression. Still, the direct clinical relevance of this research remains constrained by modest individual-level predictive value, underpowered studies of genetic determinants of disease severity and disability progression, complex regulatory mechanisms linking variants to function, and restricted generalisability across populations. At present, multiple sclerosis genetics is most useful for interpreting mechanisms, prioritising therapeutic targets, supporting causal inference, informing biomarker discovery, and enriching research cohorts. Future clinical value will likely depend on integrating genetic architecture with longitudinal clinical, imaging, biomarker, and multi-omic data to identify the contexts in which prevention or treatment is most likely to succeed.

items.title: Examining reliance patterns on AI advice in medical imaging: a mixed-methods, randomised, crossover experiment.

sections.objective: Artificial intelligence (AI) holds significant potential to support diagnostic decision making; however, the collaboration between clinicians and AI systems often does not surpass the performance of unaided humans or standalone AI. This study aimed to examine the effect of AI advice on diagnostic decision making among experts and novices, focusing on the occurrence of AI over-reliance and under-reliance and the potential mitigating effect of explainable AI.
sections.methods: We used a mixed-methods, randomised, crossover experimental design. Participants (50 task experts [radiologists] and 75 novices [non-radiologist physicians and medical trainees]) were randomly assigned in equal proportions to one of six groups, which determined the order in which the three conditions were presented across the three sessions. In each session, participants read 50 head CT scans with or without the presence of an intracranial haemorrhage, under one of three experimental conditions: control, no AI prediction; basic AI advice, AI prediction without annotations; and explainable AI advice, AI prediction with scan annotations. 80% of cases with basic or explainable AI advice received correct advice, and 20% received incorrect advice. The main outcomes were diagnostic performance (the correct identification of intracranial haemorrhage), confidence in the diagnosis, case reading time, and AI advice usefulness ratings. We defined under-reliance as a final decision that did not align with correct AI advice, and over-reliance as a final decision that aligned with incorrect AI advice. All elements of the project were preregistered and are available on the project's Open Science Framework repository.
sections.results: Data were collected between Feb 16, 2023, and Aug 10, 2023. Both over-reliance on incorrect advice and under-reliance on correct advice occurred. Under-reliance was associated with high uncertainty and, in absolute terms, had a more detrimental effect on diagnostic performance than over-reliance. Correct explainable AI advice reduced under-reliance and improved performance (OR=1·84, p<0·0001, 95% CI 1·49-2·28) and confidence (b=0·15, p<0·0001, 0·09-0·22) compared with no advice, particularly when reviewing more difficult cases with intracranial haemorrhage. Correct explainable AI did not reduce reading time compared with the no-advice condition (b=-1·81, p=0·071, -3·78 to 0·16). Explainable AI was perceived as more useful than basic AI advice (b=0·12, p=0·0029, 0·04-0·20), especially among novices.
sections.conclusion: The occurrence of both under-reliance and over-reliance highlights the need for efficient counterstrategies beyond classic explainable AI methods to foster appropriate reliance and synergy in AI-supported clinical decision-making.

items.title: Safety and immunogenicity of an adenoviral-vectored vaccine against Crimean-Congo haemorrhagic fever in the UK (CCHF01): an open-label, first-in-human, non-randomised, phase 1 clinical trial.

sections.objective: There are no approved vaccines for Crimean-Congo haemorrhagic fever virus (CCHFV), which remains a WHO priority pathogen for vaccine development. We evaluated the safety and immunogenicity of ChAdOx2 Crimean-Congo haemorrhagic fever (CCHF), a novel, non-replicating adenoviral-vectored vaccine, in a first-in-human phase 1 clinical trial.
sections.methods: CCHF01 was an open-label, first-in-human, non-randomised, phase 1 trial conducted at a single centre, the University of Oxford Centre for Clinical Vaccinology and Tropical Medicine in Oxford, UK. Healthy adults aged 18-55 years, with no confirmed or suspected previous CCHFV infection and no known clinically significant medical comorbidities, received two intramuscular doses of ChAdOx2 CCHF administered 12 weeks apart. Six participants were enrolled into a lead-in cohort (cohort 1). 40 participants were enrolled in cohort 2 and stratified by previous vaccination with a ChAdOx-vectored vaccine: cohort 2A (ChAdOx exposed; n=20) and cohort 2B (ChAdOx naive; n=20). Primary outcomes were safety and tolerability, assessed in all participants who received at least one vaccine dose. Secondary outcome was CCHFV glycoprotein-specific binding antibody responses, assessed at prespecified timepoints in participants who received two vaccine doses with available data. The trial was registered on the ISRCTN registry (ISRCTN12 351 734) and is now complete.
sections.results: Between Aug 31, 2023, and Jan 31, 2024, 46 adult participants aged 18-55 years were enrolled. Of these, 44 received the second vaccine dose; two were discontinued from further vaccination: one due to persistent neutropenia and one following a mild self-limiting allergic reaction after the first vaccination. Solicited local adverse events occurred in 30 (65%) of 46 participants after the first vaccination and 30 (68%) of 44 after the second vaccination, and solicited systemic adverse events occurred in 39 (85%) of 46 participants after the first vaccination and 28 (64%) of 44 participants after the second vaccination. Reactogenicity was predominantly mild, with injection-site pain and fatigue being the most commonly reported local and systemic adverse events. No serious adverse events were reported. Median CCHFV glycoprotein Gc-specific IgG response was 26·17 arbitrary units (AU) 28 days after first vaccination and was 88·20 AU 28 days after second vaccination. Median GP38-specific IgG response was 92·74 AU 28 days after first vaccination and 1064·13 AU 28 days after second vaccination.
sections.conclusion: ChAdOx2 CCHF demonstrated acceptable tolerability and induced CCHFV-specific humoral immune responses in this phase 1 trial. These findings provide proof of principle for vaccination against CCHFV and support further clinical development of this vaccine. The effect of previous ChAdOx-vectored vaccination on immunogenicity could not be conclusively determined because of the study sample size and age differences between groups.

items.title: Secretory bile salt hydrolases regulate niche displacement and gut colonization of vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus.
items.abstract: Vancomycin-resistant enterococci (VRE) residing in the gut are major causes of hospital-acquired infections worldwide. Bacteria belonging to the Bacteroidales order have been linked to protection against VRE, but the mechanism remains unclear. Here, we identify an important role for Bacteroidales species in mediating resistance to VRE through a distinct subtype of bile salt hydrolases (BSHs) that retain an uncleaved N-terminal signal peptide. This subclass of BSHs harbored by Bacteroides species promotes VRE inhibition through deoxycholic acid (DCA) production in the presence of Lachnospiraceae bai+ bacteria. Mechanistically, the N-terminal signal peptide is required for extracellular enzyme release, DCA production, and VRE growth inhibition. In the presence of VRE, Bacteroidales species producing this subclass of BSH eliminate and displace VRE from its ecological niche through DCA production. These results reveal a previously unknown regulatory role for BSHs in VRE colonization and suggest therapeutic approaches for individuals at risk of VRE infection.

items.title: Sibeprenlimab in IgA Nephropathy - Final Phase 3 Trial Analysis.

sections.objective: Sibeprenlimab, a humanized monoclonal antibody, selectively inhibits the cytokine A proliferation-inducing ligand (APRIL), a key driver of IgA nephropathy. Preliminary trial results with regard to the primary end point of the 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio at 9 months after treatment as compared with baseline have been reported, but secondary end points, including outcomes regarding estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), have not.
sections.methods: We randomly assigned adults with IgA nephropathy to receive subcutaneous sibeprenlimab (at a dose of 400 mg) or placebo every 4 weeks. The key secondary end point was the annualized slope of the eGFR over 24 months. Other secondary end points included the change in eGFR from baseline to 24 months, a composite kidney end point of kidney-function decline or kidney failure, and pharmacodynamic and safety end points.
sections.results: A total of 510 patients underwent randomization - 259 to receive sibeprenlimab and 251 to receive placebo. The annualized eGFR slope over 24 months was 0.3 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 of body-surface area per year (95% confidence interval [CI], -0.4 to 0.9) with sibeprenlimab and -4.2 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 per year (95% CI, -4.9 to -3.6) with placebo (between-group difference, 4.5 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 per year; 95% CI, 3.6 to 5.4; P<0.001). The least-squares mean treatment difference for the change in eGFR from baseline to 24 months was 9.2 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 (95% CI, 7.1 to 11.4; P<0.001). A composite kidney end-point event occurred in 1 patient (0.4%) in the sibeprenlimab group and in 28 patients (11.2%) in the placebo group (adjusted difference, -10.8 percentage points; hazard ratio, 0.029; 95% CI, 0.004 to 0.214; P<0.001). Adverse events occurred in 235 patients (90.7%) in the sibeprenlimab group and 226 patients (90.0%) in the placebo group; serious adverse events occurred in 21 patients (8.1%) and 32 patients (12.7%), respectively; and serious infections in 5 patients (1.9%) and 10 patients (4.0%). No deaths were reported.
sections.conclusion: Among patients with IgA nephropathy, treatment with sibeprenlimab stabilized the eGFR slope over 24 months, a finding consistent with a reduced risk of kidney-function decline. (Funded by Otsuka Pharmaceutical Development and Commercialization; VISIONARY ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05248646.).

items.title: Atacicept in IgA Nephropathy - Phase 3 Trial Final Efficacy Analysis.

sections.objective: Atacicept resulted in a significantly greater reduction in the urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio than placebo in a previously published analysis of this trial, ORIGIN 3. Final prespecified efficacy results are reported here.
sections.methods: We randomly assigned adults with biopsy-confirmed IgA nephropathy to receive weekly subcutaneous atacicept at a dose of 150 mg or placebo. We carried out final analyses of two secondary end points: the change in the estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) at week 52 and the annualized eGFR slope through week 104; additional hierarchically tested end points and safety were assessed.
sections.results: Of 431 patients who underwent randomization, 428 received atacicept or placebo (214 per group). At week 52, the mean change in the eGFR was -0.11 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 of body-surface area (95% confidence interval [CI], -1.44 to 1.22) with atacicept and -5.69 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 (95% CI, -7.04 to -4.35) with placebo (mean difference, 5.58 ml per minute per 1.73 m2; 95% CI, 3.68 to 7.48; P<0.001). Through week 104, the mean annualized eGFR slope was -0.60 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 (95% CI, -1.62 to 0.41) with atacicept and -5.60 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 (95% CI, -6.64 to -4.57) with placebo (difference, 5.00 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 per year; 95% CI, 3.55 to 6.45; P<0.001). Composite kidney-disease progression occurred in 11 patients (5.1%) in the atacicept group and in 38 patients (17.8%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.24; 95% CI, 0.12 to 0.48; P<0.001); no patients in the atacicept group had progression to dialysis, transplantation, or death, as compared with 7 patients in the placebo group. Adverse events occurred in 160 of 214 patients (74.8%) in the atacicept group and in 167 of 214 patients (78.0%) in the placebo group; serious adverse events occurred in 7.0% and 15.4%, respectively. One patient (in the placebo group) died.
sections.conclusion: Atacicept slowed and stabilized the decline in the eGFR as compared with placebo. (Funded by Vera Therapeutics; ORIGIN 3 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04716231.).

items.title: Helicobacter pylori Infection - Advances, Challenges, and the Road Ahead.
items.abstract: The discovery of Helicobacter pylori has revolutionized the prevention and treatment of gastritis, peptic ulcers, and, most important, gastric cancer. In the past 40 years, enormous progress has been achieved in the clinical and basic research on H. pylori infection. However, challenges in preventing and treating H. pylori infection exist owing to the lack of an H. pylori vaccine and the ever-increasing resistance to antibiotics worldwide. This review summarizes the history of and key milestones in H. pylori research, provides an update on the understanding of the pathogenesis and global burden of H. pylori infection and the screening strategy for the primary prevention of gastric cancer, and focuses on the emerging trends in the management of H. pylori infection.

items.title: Ianalumab for the Treatment of Patients with Sjögren's Disease.

sections.objective: Sjögren's disease is a complex, systemic autoimmune disease with no approved targeted therapies. Ianalumab is an IgG1 monoclonal antibody with a dual mechanism of action, depleting B cells through antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity and inhibiting B-cell activation and survival through blockade of B-cell activating factor receptor.
sections.methods: We conducted two 52-week, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trials involving patients with active Sjögren's disease. Patients in the NEPTUNUS-1 trial were assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive subcutaneous ianalumab (300 mg monthly) or placebo; patients in the NEPTUNUS-2 trial were assigned in a 1:1:1 ratio to receive 300 mg of ianalumab monthly or every 3 months or placebo. The primary end point was the change from baseline in the score on the European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology (EULAR) Sjögren's Syndrome Disease Activity Index (ESSDAI) at week 48 (scores range from 0 to 123, with higher scores indicating greater disease activity). The first key secondary end point in the hierarchical plan for the NEPTUNUS-1 trial was an ESSDAI response (≥5-point reduction) at week 48; for the NEPTUNUS-2 trial, it was the change from baseline in the score on the Sjögren's Syndrome Symptom Diary (SSSD) or EULAR Sjögren's Syndrome Patient Reported Index (ESSPRI) at week 48.
sections.results: Overall, 275 patients underwent randomization in the NEPTUNUS-1 trial (ianalumab monthly, 137 patients; placebo, 138 patients) and 504 in the NEPTUNUS-2 trial (ianalumab monthly, 168 patients; ianalumab every 3 months, 167 patients; and placebo, 169 patients). In both trials, ianalumab monthly led to a significantly greater decrease in the ESSDAI score at week 48 than placebo, with a between-group difference of -1.3 points (95% confidence interval [CI], -2.6 to 0.0; P = 0.0496) in NEPTUNUS-1 and -1.0 points (95% CI, -2.0 to 0.0; P = 0.04) in NEPTUNUS-2. No significant differences in the incidence of an ESSDAI response or in the change from baseline in SSSD or ESSPRI scores were observed at week 48. The incidence of serious adverse events was similar with ianalumab and placebo. Nonserious local injection-site and systemic injection-related reactions were more common in the ianalumab groups.
sections.conclusion: In these two trials involving patients with active Sjögren's disease, ianalumab at a dose of 300 mg monthly resulted in a significantly greater decrease in disease activity at week 48 than placebo, although there were no significant differences in the incidence of an ESSDAI response or in the change from baseline in SSSD or ESSPRI symptom scores. (Funded by Novartis Pharma; NEPTUNUS-1 and NEPTUNUS-2 ClinicalTrials.gov numbers, NCT05350072 and NCT05349214, respectively.).

items.title: Tambotatug Pelitecan in Small-Cell Lung Cancer after Platinum-Based Therapy.

sections.objective: Tambotatug pelitecan (known as Tam-Peli, a new antibody-drug conjugate that targets the immune-checkpoint molecule B7-H3) showed promising clinical efficacy in patients with relapsed extensive-stage small-cell lung cancer in early-phase trials.
sections.methods: In this phase 3, multicenter, open-label, randomized trial, we assigned eligible patients with small-cell lung cancer that had progressed after first-line platinum-based therapy in a 1:1 ratio to receive tambotatug pelitecan or topotecan. The primary end point was overall survival. The key secondary end points were progression-free survival and objective response as assessed by investigators. Here, we report the results from the prespecified interim analysis.
sections.results: A total of 451 patients underwent randomization: 225 were assigned to receive tambotatug pelitecan and 226 to receive topotecan. Overall survival was significantly longer with tambotatug pelitecan than with topotecan - a median of 13.3 months (95% confidence interval [CI], 12.1 to could not be estimated), as compared with 9.4 months (95% CI, 7.7 to 10.5); the stratified hazard ratio for death was 0.46 (95% CI, 0.35 to 0.62; P<0.001). Treatment with tambotatug pelitecan also resulted in significantly longer progression-free survival than treatment with topotecan (median, 7.4 months [95% CI, 6.1 to 7.6] vs. 2.8 months [95% CI, 1.8 to 3.0]; stratified hazard ratio, 0.29 [95% CI, 0.23 to 0.37]; P<0.001). A confirmed objective response occurred in 59.1% of the patients in the tambotatug pelitecan group, as compared with 9.7% of those in the topotecan group (P<0.001). The overall incidence of adverse events of grade 3 or higher was lower with tambotatug pelitecan than with topotecan (55.4% vs. 77.9%).
sections.conclusion: Among patients with relapsed small-cell lung cancer after platinum-based therapy, treatment with tambotatug pelitecan resulted in longer overall survival, longer progression-free survival, and a higher percentage of patients with an objective response than treatment with topotecan, with a lower incidence of adverse events of grade 3 or higher. (Funded by the Innovative Drug Research and Development National Science and Technology Major Project and MediLink Therapeutics; TAISHAN-302 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06612151.).

items.title: Surgery in Motion: Different Surgical Techniques for Inguinal Lymph Node Dissection in Penile Cancer.
items.abstract: Inguinal lymph node dissection (ILND) remains a cornerstone of nodal management in penile cancer, providing definitive treatment for clinically node-positive disease and surgical staging for high-risk clinically node-negative patients when dynamic sentinel node biopsy (DSNB) is unavailable. Despite its oncological importance, ILND is associated with substantial morbidity. Over the past decade, minimally invasive (MI) approaches have emerged as alternatives to open ILND, with the potential to reduce wound-related complications while maintaining oncological efficacy. This Surgery in Motion article provides a practical overview of contemporary open, video-endoscopic (VEIL), and robot-assisted (RAVEIL) ILND techniques, integrating anatomical principles, technical variations, and current clinical evidence. Open ILND remains the reference approach, particularly in patients with advanced nodal disease, while MI techniques may be considered in selected patients with limited nodal disease at experienced centres. Across all approaches, meticulous adherence to anatomical templates, appropriate patient selection, and preservation of lymphatic and vascular structures where oncologically feasible are key principles for minimising morbidity. Emerging robotic and image-guided technologies may further refine ILND, although their clinical benefits and long-term oncological outcomes require further evaluation. This stepwise educational review and accompanying surgical video aim to support surgical training, standardisation, and safe implementation of contemporary ILND techniques.

items.title: Psoriasis: Which therapy for which patient, updated, part II. Focus on special populations and chronic infections.
items.abstract: Choosing systemic therapy for psoriasis remains challenging in populations underrepresented in clinical trials, including pregnant and pediatric patients, patients with chronic infections, and those with difficult-to-treat phenotypes. Since the 2019 version of this article, therapeutic options have expanded substantially, including new pediatric approvals, oral targeted agents, and biologics with increasingly phenotype-specific evidence. This second article in the continuing medical education series reviews systemic treatment selection for moderate-to-severe psoriasis in pregnancy, pediatric patients, hepatitis, HIV, latent tuberculosis, nail psoriasis, erythrodermic psoriasis, generalized pustular psoriasis, and palmoplantar psoriasis. Emphasis is placed on balancing efficacy, safety, monitoring burden, infection/reactivation risk, reproductive considerations, and disease phenotype. Traditional agents remain useful in selected scenarios, while IL-17, IL-23, IL-36, TNF-α, TYK2, JAK, and other targeted therapies offer expanding options. Available evidence is summarized with expert-opinion recommendations where comparative data are limited.

items.title: Covered Stent Assisted Coil Embolisation of a Rare Splenomesenteric Artery Aneurysm - A Case Report and Literature Review.
items.abstract: BackgroundSplenomesenteric artery aneurysms are a rare clinical entity occurring in <1% of the population, where the splenic artery originates from the superior mesenteric artery (SMA). These aneurysms carry a high risk of rupture due to exposure to high-flow hemodynamic stress near the SMA origin.Case PresentationA 76-year-old female was incidentally diagnosed with a 1.6 cm saccular splenomesenteric aneurysm during investigation for sepsis. The patient underwent successful endovascular exclusion using a combination of a microvascular plug and coil embolisation to address the aneurysm 'front' and 'back' doors, while a covered stent was deployed in the SMA to prevent coil prolapse and preserve mesenteric perfusion. Follow-up at 3 months confirmed successful exclusion with preserved visceral flow.DiscussionDue to the rarity of this anatomical variant, documented in less than 60 cases in English literature, no standardised treatment algorithm exists. This study adds to the literature by demonstrating procedural innovation, refining management strategies and advocating for early intervention for such conditions.

items.title: Long-term efficacy and safety for the complement factor B inhibitor iptacopan in IgA nephropathy.

sections.objective: Iptacopan, a factor B inhibitor, targets alternative complement pathway overactivation, a key driver of glomerular inflammation in IgA nephropathy. In the phase 3 APPLAUSE-IgAN trial (NCT04578834), iptacopan significantly slowed kidney function decline versus placebo over 24 months (difference in total estimated glomerular filtration rate [eGFR] slope: 3.02 ml/min per 1.73 m2 per year [95% confidence interval (CI) 2.02, 4.01; P < 0.001]).
sections.methods: Patients who completed APPLAUSE-IgAN or the phase 2 iptacopan trial (NCT03373461) could enter an open-label rollover extension program (REP) (NCT04557462). Patients in this REP receive oral iptacopan 200 mg twice daily alongside supportive care. Patients from the phase 2 trial were not included in efficacy analyses.
sections.results: Overall, 194 and 174 patients from the APPLAUSE-IgAN iptacopan and placebo arms, respectively, entered the REP. In patients who received iptacopan for up to 48 months, the total annualized eGFR slope was -3.49 ml/min per 1.73 m2 per year (95% CI -4.17, -2.80). Urine protein-to-creatinine ratio from first morning void (UPCR-FMV) reduction was sustained through 48 months with iptacopan (geometric mean ratio to baseline: 0.61 [95% CI 0.50, 0.75]). Before receiving iptacopan, the total eGFR slope over 24 months in APPLAUSE-IgAN placebo arm patients who entered the REP was -5.29 ml/min per 1.73 m2 per year (95% CI -6.09, -4.49). After switching to iptacopan, the total eGFR slope improved to -2.11 ml/min per 1.73 m2 per year (95% CI -3.08, -1.13) over the next 24 months. UPCR-FMV decreased after switching (geometric mean ratio to baseline at month 48: 0.74 [95% CI 0.59, 0.91]). Long-term safety up to 5 years (median treatment duration: 29.9 months) was consistent with the known profile of iptacopan.
sections.conclusion: Long-term treatment with iptacopan led to sustained slowing in eGFR decline and proteinuria reduction that were also observed after switching from placebo. No new safety signals were observed.

items.title: Circulating Immune and Cancer Driver Gene Biomarkers Precede Prostate Cancer Diagnosis by over 10 yr.

sections.objective: Prospective proteomic and proteogenomic studies may enhance the understanding of proteins associated with prostate cancer (PCa) development.
sections.methods: In a case-cohort study within the European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition (EPIC), baseline plasma samples from 982 incident PCa cases and 1573 subcohort participants were profiled using the SomaScan 7k platform (over 6000 proteins). Associations were estimated using Prentice-weighted Cox models. The coprimary end points were incident overall PCa and aggressive PCa (n = 290). Findings were evaluated in the Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities (ARIC) study and supported by Mendelian randomization (MR) and exome gene-burden analyses.
sections.conclusion: Prospective plasma proteomic analyses identified circulating proteins associated with future PCa risk, including proteins related to immune, adhesion, angiogenesis, and PCa driver-gene pathways. These findings identify candidate protein risk factors for overall and clinically significant PCa, and warrant further validation and mechanistic evaluation.
sections.other: ACP3, FLT4, and KLK3 were associated with overall PCa risk (hazard ratio [HR] per 1 standard deviation [SD] increase were 1.20 [1.10-1.31], 1.26 [1.13-1.40], and 2.28 [1.96-2.65], respectively). Seven proteins were associated with aggressive PCa risk, with ANKRD1 consistently associated across multiple clinically relevant disease subtypes. Twelve proteins were associated with PCa diagnosed >15 yr after blood draw, including ANXA2, GZMK, and OSCAR. ACP3, ANXA2, APOC2, and KLK3 showed consistent associations in both EPIC and ARIC. Additionally, four proteins had support from MR analyses and eight from rare-variant burden tests. Circulating products of established PCa driver genes, including ERBB3, KRAS, and NRAS, were associated with future aggressive disease. Limitations include incomplete external replication and differences in end point availability across cohorts.

items.title: Bacteriophage-derived ectolysin: a promising antimicrobial against fluoroquinolone-resistant MRSA.

sections.objective: Microbial keratitis remains one of the leading causes of blindness globally. With the rising threat of antimicrobial resistance, there is an urgent need for the development of novel antimicrobial agents with innovative mechanisms of action.
sections.results: P128 demonstrated potent antibacterial activity against multidrug resistant S. aureus strains collected from patients with infectious keratitis, with minimum inhibitory concentrations ranging from 0.5 µg/mL to 16 µg/mL. Topical instillation of P128 to an injured cornea did not interfere with the re-epithelialisation rates nor cause any adverse effects. In a rabbit S. aureus keratitis model, P128 showed similar therapeutic efficacy to standard of care antibiotic, gatifloxacin. In a mouse model of fluoroquinolone-resistant methicillin-resistant S. aureus (MRSA) keratitis, P128 decreased the bacterial bioburden as well as corneal oedema. P128 displayed potent synergism with membrane active antimicrobial peptides, and their combination eradicated the preformed 96 hours biofilms.
sections.conclusion: These results demonstrate the therapeutic potential of P128 for the management of drug-resistant MRSA keratitis and its combination with antimicrobial peptides may expand the antimicrobial armamentarium against biofilm-associated infections.
sections.other: Antibacterial properties of P128, a peptidoglycan degrading enzyme derived from bacteriophage K, was determined against multi-drug resistant Staphylococcus aureus clinical strains. P128 was tested for its ocular safety in a rabbit corneal wound healing model. The antibacterial efficacy of P128 was investigated in in vivo rabbit and mouse infectious keratitis models.

items.title: Clinical characteristics and ompA serovar correlation in adult inclusion conjunctivitis: a cohort study in China.

sections.objective: Adult inclusion conjunctivitis (AIC) caused by non-trachomatous Chlamydia trachomatis is often under-recognised due to variable and non-specific clinical features. This study aimed to describe its clinical and laboratory characteristics, ompA serotype distribution, and their association with clinical presentation and outcome.
sections.methods: This retrospective cohort study included 22 patients with laboratory-confirmed AIC diagnosed at a tertiary eye centre between February 2023 and January 2026. Clinical signs were graded using a structured conjunctival scoring system. Diagnosis was based on conjunctival cytology, nucleic acid amplification testing and cell culture. C. trachomatis ompA genotyping was performed by PCR and sequencing with phylogenetic analysis. Patients were classified into serovar D and non-D groups, and clinical severity scores and time to resolution were compared using the Mann-Whitney U test.
sections.results: Patients presented with subacute or chronic conjunctivitis with variable conjunctival hyperaemia, follicular reaction, papillary hypertrophy and discharge. ompA genotyping revealed a heterogeneous serovar distribution, with serovar D predominating. Overall clinical scores at presentation were higher in patients with non-D serovars than in those with serovar D (p<0.05), while only papillary reaction differed among individual signs. Time to clinical resolution after standard antibiotic therapy varied but did not differ significantly between groups.
sections.conclusion: This study provides a clinical and molecular profile of AIC and highlights variability across ompA serotypes. By generating data from a Chinese cohort, it helps address the limited evidence base in this setting and may support improved clinical recognition and future genotype–phenotype research.

items.title: Clade-specific ophthalmic manifestations of mpox: an umbrella review and meta-analysis of systematic reviews.

sections.objective: On 14 August 2024, the WHO redesignated Monkeypox (mpox) as a Public Health Emergency of International Concern. Ocular disease is under-recognised and can cause irreversible vision loss. Clarifying its burden, clade-specific patterns and HIV-related risks is essential for clinical care and public health.
sections.methods: We conducted an umbrella review and meta-analysis, systematically searching PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science and the Cochrane Library from inception to September 2025. Eligible studies were systematic reviews reporting ophthalmic manifestations in laboratory-confirmed mpox cases, stratified by viral clades I, II and IIb. Pooled proportions were estimated using random-effects meta-analysis, with clade-stratified subgroup analyses. The protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251137180).
sections.results: Five systematic reviews (36 primary studies; 28 139 patients) were included. The pooled proportion of conjunctivitis was 8.9% (95% CI 4.8 to 13.9), highest in clade I (21.9%) and lowest in clade IIb (2.7%). Keratitis (1.5%), eyelid lesions (3.3%), conjunctival lesions (8.4%) and corneal ulceration (3.3%) varied by clade. Visual impairment occurred in 4.5% overall; unilateral (0.9%) and bilateral (0.4%) blindness were reported only with clade I. Across reviews, people living with advanced HIV experienced disproportionately higher rates of severe and persistent ocular complications than HIV-negative individuals.
sections.conclusion: Mpox-related ophthalmic disease can cause substantial—and potentially preventable—visual disability. Clade I infection is associated with a greater burden of ocular complications than clade II—particularly IIb. Improved access to eye health services, early recognition and integration of HIV and mpox care are critical to reducing vision loss, especially in resource-limited settings.
